news.abstract: George W Bush administration, expecting victory of Ariel Sharon in Israel, dispatches messages calling for calm in Middle East and reassuring Israel that relationship with US remains 'rock solid'; Sec Colin Powell issues plea for restraint, call apparently aimed at Palestinian Authority and Arab nations; says he will visit region this month (M)
news.title: White House Reaches Out To Both Sides In Peace Talks

news.abstract: Initial results from survey of opium-growing areas of Afghanistan indicate that Taliban may have succeeded in sharply reducing poppy crop; astonished UN narcotics-control officials report no major signs of cultivation this year in northern provinces; farmers tell inspectors they are trying to grow other crops; World Bank warns at same time that country faces major famine; UN appeals for help for 100,000 Afghans caught in bitter cold (S)
news.title: Taliban Seem to Be Making Good on Opium Ban, U.N. Says

news.abstract: Man in the News profile of Ariel Sharon, 72-year-old veteran soldier and controversial political figure now elected to lead Israel; photos (M)
news.title: Warrior Who Confounds -- Ariel Sharon

news.abstract: American Jewish groups react to Ariel Sharon's victory in Israel (S)
news.title: Support Mixed With Concern Among U.S. Jewish Groups

news.abstract: Abdelbaset Ali Mohmed al-Megrahi tells Scottish courts that he wants to appeal his murder convictions in bombing of Pan American jet over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988 (M)
news.title: Libyan Wants Lockerbie Appeal

news.abstract: Pres Andres Pastrana of Colombia is set to meet with Manuel Marulanda, who leads Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, and political analysts say that Pastrana risks losing his political legitimacy and presidential authority if he does not get more from Marulanda than a pledge that his group is committed to peaceful resolution of 37-year-old conflict; Marulanda's supporters are divided about whether to continue war or to make peace (M)
news.title: Meeting Today With Rebels Crucial for Colombia's Leader

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, Feb. 8 — President Bush will order a comprehensive review of the nation's nuclear arsenal, a first step toward the unilateral cuts in warheads and missiles that he promised during last year's campaign, senior military and administration officials said today.
news.title: Bush Takes First Step to Shrink Arsenal of Nuclear Warheads

news.abstract: Alfred Sirven, former executive at Elf Aquitaine, makes brief appearance in French court, where he is crucial defendant in multimillion-dollar corruption case; is greeted by fellow defendants, including Roland Dumas, former foreign minister, and Dumas's former mistress, Christine Deviers-Joncour; justice minister urges Sirven to tell all he knows about high-level bribery and fraud (M)
news.title: Ex-Fugitive Appears at French Corruption Trial

news.abstract: Stormy debate is ignited in Germany by publication of The Holocaust Industry, book by Norman Finkelstein, American historian and son of Holocaust survivors, which declares that Holocaust has become an 'extortion racket' through which 'American-Jewish elite' blackmails Germany; Finkelstein says he is unhappy with enthusisastic reception of book by right-wing circles in Germany, but is determined to put 'Holocaust industry' out of business and so end 'exploitation of my parents' memory' (M)
news.title: Book Calling Holocaust a Shakedown Starts a German Storm

news.abstract: Pres Andres Pastrana of Colombia arrives in heart of guerrilla-held territory to hold first day of meetings with leader of Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, Manuel Marulanda; Pastrana assures mothers and relatives of 470 soldiers and policemen held by FARC that one of first points he will raise with Marulanda is need for exchange of sick rebels held by government for other ailing soldiers held by guerrillas; FARC has said that it would release 50 or more soldiers and policemen once sick prisoners are exchanged; mothers' movement in Colombia has coalesced to put pressure on government; they believe government places priority on securing release of hostages who are wealthy; photos (M)
news.title: In Unruly Colombia, a Mother's Hope

news.abstract: Russia pledges to finally begin destroying 40,000 tons of lethal chemical weapons, largest stockpile in world, this summer; United States and other Western nations are assisting Russia's preparations to destroy its chemical arms, but Congress froze money for project after Moscow missed earlier deadline; funds, up to $50 million a year, can be restored if Moscow puts in place well-financed program (M)
news.title: Russia Vows to Start Destroying Chemical Arms

news.abstract: Human Rights in China, organization based in New York, says silk-factory worker in China was forcibly placed in psychiatric care in December after trying to organize independent union; says worker, Cao Maobing, is protesting his detention with hunger strike, and that he is being forcibly drugged and subjected to electroshock; Cao's friends and relatives insist he is not mentally ill, and rights group is calling for independent inquiry into his health; Cao has been eloquent spokesman for angry workers at plant in Jiangsu Province (M)
news.title: China Is Said to Abuse Promoter of Factory Union

news.abstract: Pres Bush will order comprehensive review of nation's nuclear arsenal, first step toward unilateral cuts in warheads and missiles that he promised during his campaign; administration officials say Bush's order will also underscore his commitment to building defense missile shield; say review is intended to move United States toward new strategic doctrine, as well as new approach to arms control that reflects today's world rather than cold war's superpower standoff; say Bush's directive does not declare his intention to withdraw from Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty; review appears intended to lay foundation for decision to do so in parallel with nuclear cutbacks; nation's arsenal as of last year included 7,519 nuclear warheads on missiles, submarines or bombers; significant reductions in American arsenal could smooth anxieties among opponents about administration's pursuit of missile shield (M)
news.title: BUSH IN FIRST STEP TO SHRINK ARSENAL OF U.S. WARHEADS

news.abstract: Hong Kong's top official, Tung Chee-hwa, says he is shocked by television images of what Beijing says are members of Falun Gong setting themselves on fire in Tiananmen Square, and that Hong Kong will more closely monitor group, which is outlawed in China but remains legal in Hong Kong; his comments are closely scrutinized, because he has not spoken publicly about Falun Gong since it held conference in Hong Kong at which China's treatment of Falun Gong was protested (M)
news.title: Hong Kong Will Check on Falun Gong

news.abstract: colomb
news.title: Colombia and Rebels Agree on Restarting Peace Talks

news.abstract: State Sec Colin L Powell, in another sign of Bush administration's broad regional approach to Israeli-Palestinian conflict, plans to visit Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Kuwait, Israel and Palestinian territories later in Feb; says he will consult with Israeli Prime Min-elect Ariel Sharon, Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and other area leaders; also plans to discuss Iraq and ways to keep pressure from United Nations sanctions on Pres Saddam Hussein; Pres Bush says he urged Arafat in phone call to give Sharon chance to form government and fulfill pledge to pursue peace; says he urged calm in talks with Sharon and other regional leaders; Powell's trip will also include stop in Brussels to consult with NATO and European Union leaders on national missile defense system (M)
news.title: POWELL WILL VISIT MIDEAST, SETTING A WIDE ITINERARY

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min-elect Ariel Sharon asks Prime Min Ehud Barak to join his government as defense minister and Shimon Peres to become foreign minister in bid to form coalition with their Labor Party; Israeli soldiers and Palestinian gunmen exchange fire in both Ramallah and Hebron; Palestinian officials say Israeli soldiers shot Palestinian goatherd to death in Gaza Strip; Islamic Jihad leader Abdallah al-Shami pledges bombing attacks inside Israel will continue, rally, Gaza; Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat speaks by phone to Sharon for first time since election; indicates interest in restarting peace talks; Sharon holds Palestinians must first end violence; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon Asks Barak and Peres To Join a Unity Government

news.abstract: chevron tal
news.title: Chevron Talks to Azerbaijanis About Pipeline

news.abstract: BERLIN, Feb. 10 — A little phrase from Rudolf Scharping, the German defense minister, recently caused American military commanders to shudder: "As the European Union develops its security and defense policy and becomes an independent actor, we must determine our security policy with Russia, our biggest neighbor."
news.title: Europe's Shifting Role Poses Challenge to U.S.

news.abstract: Special report The Dividing Line: Misery on the Border describes hardship, squalor and poverty afflicting Mexicans living near United States border, Mexicans who are part of tidal wave of workers lured to border by increased trade between United States and Mexico; in last five years, more than one million Mexicans have moved to border; many come not to cross border, but to work in thousands of mostly foreign-owned manufacturing plants, known as maquiladoras; scene in shantytowns such as Ciudad Juarez described; photos; map (L)
news.title: Chasing Mexico's Dream Into Squalor

news.abstract: South Africa is going public with its battle to stop Canadian government from recruiting its desperately needed doctors, who are fleeing South Africa by the hundreds as they tire of high crime rates and chronically understaffed and underfinanced hospitals; Andre Jaquet, South Africa's ambassador to Canada, argues that it is unethical for the West to lure doctors from the developing world, particularly from South Africa, which has too few doctors (M)
news.title: West Lures Its Doctors; South Africa Fights Back

news.abstract: Adrian Nastase, new Romanian prime minister, knows that his government represents Romania's last, best chance of reversing huge popular frustration that fed a sizable vote for neofascism in last December's elections; Western officials, diplomats and investors know it too, after 10 years of watching Romania slide deeper into poverty and anger; they are skeptical, frustrated by Romania's years of dawdling on economic change, its endemic corruption and narrow-minded political squabbling; photo of Nastase; map (M)
news.title: Romania Seeks to Stay On the Track to Europe

news.abstract: As Russia's most powerful businessmen gradually lose their influence over government in Moscow, some have moved into local politics; group of Moscow entrepreneurs has just staged takeover of regional government of Dudinka, far above Arctic Circle in Russia's northernmost region; group is led by Aleksandr Khloponin, 35-year-old former banker; Khloponin's victory follows win by Russia's aluminum tycoon, Roman Abramovich, in region of Chukotka, in Russia's far northeast corner (M)
news.title: Russia Entrepreneurs Try The Business of Governing

news.abstract: Five Australians have been killed in shark attacks since August, 2000, and a sixth man, Richard Butler, makes dramatic escape after shark takes chunk out of his leg while surfing off Brooms Head; last six months have been bloodiest period of shark attacks ever recorded (M)
news.title: Shark Tale in Nervous Australia From the One Who Got Away

news.abstract: LIJIANG, China—  At his simple wooden desk in a room along the shores of the Black Dragon pool high in the Chinese Himalayas, the brush in He Kai-xian's steady hand marks a series of distinctive symbols, the meaning of which almost nobody else can fully decipher.
news.title: Hieroglyphic Script Fights for Life

news.abstract: Flare-up in Israeli-Palestinian violence that followed election of Ariel Sharon as prime minister continues; Palestinian gunmen fire toward Israeli neighborhood of Gilo on outskirts of Jerusalem for first time in more than month; Israeli troops respond with barrage against source of gunfire in Palestinian town of Beit Jala; photo (M)
news.title: Flare-Up of Mideast Violence Continues

news.abstract: Thousands of demonstrators marched through the capital of Ukraine today, the second such outpouring in a week, demanding the resignation of President Leonid D. Kuchma and calling for new presidential elections.    Up to 5,000 people watched as a wreath of black and white ribbons was laid at the entrance of Ukraine's state intelligence service to celebrate the news that Mr. Kuchma had on Saturday fired its top two officers, Leonid Derkach and Veleriy Strogov. The two had been criticized for orchestrating a crackdown on freedom of the press and suppressing Mr. Kuchma's political opponents.
news.title: Ukraine Rally Calls on Chief To Step Down

news.abstract: BEIJING—  Hua Lijun owns a most decidedly unfashionable pair of thick black reading glasses, and when she puts them on she has no trouble at all threading a needle. Still, she mutters constantly about her poor eyesight.
news.title: China's Long — but Uneven — March to Literacy

news.abstract: Russia's Primorsky Region, one of country's most mismanaged and corrupt, is suffering devastating fuel shortage for fourth winter in row in nation that boasts largest coal reserves on earth; regionwide shortage has disrupted lives of hundreds of thousands, brought unspeakable misery for tens of thousands and killed scores; region may be first major test for Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin, who has pledged to bring such wayward areas back under central control; situation in Razdolnoye, desolate town of 13,000 not far from Russia's Pacific coast, described; map; photos (M)
news.title: Fuel-Short Region in Russia Is Now Freezing in the Dark

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, Feb. 13 — Two Israeli helicopter gunships swooped over northern Gaza this morning and dropped four missiles on the car of a senior Palestinian security officer, instantly killing a man whom Israel considered a terrorist in a uniform and a beret.
news.title: Israel Hunts Down and Kills a Top Arafat Security Officer

news.abstract: SAN SALVADOR, Feb. 13 — A powerful earthquake struck El Salvador this morning.
news.title: Second Quake in One Month Kills More Than 100 in El Salvador

news.abstract: United Nations and private aid officials say dozens of Afghan children, exhausted from long journeys with their families to seek food and shelter, have frozen to death at makeshift refugee camps in recent weeks; they are newest, youngest victims of unending Afghan war, and of severe drought, lack of international assistance and shortcomings among ruling Taliban; Bush administration sends mixed signals to Taliban, sending American planes with relief supplies while announcing it would close down Taliban office in New York, which Taliban has used to stay in touch with United Nations officials and with Washington; photo; map (M)
news.title: Dozens of Afghans Are Dying in the Cold, U.N. Says

news.abstract: In a corner of Niger that was once a vast sea, dozens of families mine salt, and are the inheritors of a caravan trade that brought life to the Sahara for centuries. Page A12.
news.title: On Africa's Caravan Trail

news.abstract: Instances of police torture in China are increasingly being reported in official press; in rare cases, offending officials are being prosecuted; experts say public reports and prosecutions barely scratch surface of what one Chinese scholar calls legal system's 'chronic illness'; Amnesty International holds torture and ill-treatment of detainees and prisoners is widespread and systematic in China; China is party to United Nations treaty banning torture, but has exempted itself from clause allowing outsiders to investigate alleged torture cases (M)
news.title: China Begins to Shine Light on Use of Torture

news.abstract: Two Israeli helicopter gunships attack car in northern Gaza carrying Massoud Ayyad, killing senior Palestinian security officer Israel deems terrorist; Palestinian officials score Israel's use of assassinations to eliminate Palestinian militants; Prime Min Ehud Barak, other Israeli officials publicly laud mission; Israel's Likud and Labor parties formulate guidelines for unity government based partly on what seems view that peace accord with Palestinians cannot be reached soon; United Nations official Terje Rod-Larsen reports 'anger and uncertainty' have replaced many Palestinians' hopes for peace; finds fighting and Israeli border closings cost Palestinian economy $8.6 million a day; reports urging Israel to bar fiscal collapse of Palestinian authority; photo (M)
news.title: Israel Hunts Down and Kills a Top Arafat Security Officer

news.abstract: MOSCOW, Feb. 14 — Reviving a practice that was hated, feared and ultimately banned in Soviet times, the domestic successor to the K.G.B. has served notice that it once again is investigating anonymous accusations of crimes against Russian citizens.
news.title: Russia Reviving Dreaded Practice of Anonymous Complaints

news.abstract: German Min Joschka Fischer, meeting with Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin, sees signs of new Russian flexibility on proposed American shield against rogue missiles; he and Russian officials deny Germany acts as intermediary on issue (M)
news.title: German Sees Russia Bending on Missiles

news.abstract: AZOR, Israel, Feb. 14 -- The day began here with a typical morning rush hour as scores of young Israeli soldiers waited at a junction near Tel Aviv for a ride to their military bases. Pvt. Moshe Saroussi, 19, his black hair spiky and his eyes sleepy, saw an empty bus approaching and stretched, letting the others rush ahead of him.
news.title: Palestinian's Hit-and-Run Bus Kills 8 Israelis and Injures 20

news.abstract: Columbia University and Pharos Finance Ltd join civil suit in London against Viktor Kozeny, Czech promoter accused of fraud in $450 million deal to acquire control of Socar, Azerbaijan's state-owned oil company; Kozeny holds he did nothing wrong and lost miillions of dollars of his own because Azerbaijan has not sold Socar (M)
news.title: Civil Suit Over Azerbaijan Oil Deal Gains Plaintiffs in London

news.abstract: European Union Parliament passes measure establishing strict rules on genetically modified organisms, preparing to end Europe's unofficial moratorium on bioengineered seeds and food; strictness of new controls is intended to respond to intense suspicions about genetically modified foods; rules govern testing, planting and sale of crops and food for humans and animals and testing and sale of pharmaceuticals; all genetically altered products will be tracked in database that will also mark locations of all crops; separate bill to set tough food labeling and tracing requirements is to be ready by April, and is widely expected to pass in some form; under European Union law, all 15 member countries are required to make their laws conform to new rules in 18 months; governments of France and Denmark say they would resist approvals; defying laws would open countries to suit in European Court of Justice to force compliance (M)
news.title: EUROPE APPROVES STRICT FOOD RULES

news.abstract: ASIA    AFGHANISTAN: OPPOSITION TAKES CITY -- Bamiyan, a strategic city west of Kabul, has been captured by opposition forces, according to spokesmen for both sides in the conflict. If itcan hold the city, the opposition will deal a major setback to the Taliban militia, which has suffered few battlefield reversals in the past year. Bamiyan was once a bastion for Afghan Shiite Muslims. The Taliban are primarily Sunni.    Barry Bearak (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Governments of Armenia and Turkey said to initiate quiet diplomatic contacts to evaluate prospects for cooperation and opening border between them; countries have no diplomatic relations, but mid-level officials from both foreign ministries have exchanged visits; talks occur as private organizations in Turkey take steps toward expanding contacts with Armenia and Armenian-Americans; signs of progress are small and come at time of rising anxiety in Turkey over actions by Armenian diaspora to persuade world governments to recognize killing of Armenians under Ottoman Empire as genocide (M)
news.title: Longtime Enemies, Armenia and Turkey Softly Broach Détente

news.abstract: Ambassador Alon Pinkas, the consulate general of Israel in New York, answered questions about the Mideast peace process on Wednesday in a forum on The New York Times on the Web.
news.title: Transcript of Ambassador Alon Pinkas's Visit to the Middle East Forum

news.abstract: Latest article in Dividing Line series on life along Mexican side of border, on rules, written and unwritten, under which mostly American corporations operate on border; there is rising concern that as factories spread through developing world, labor rights and environmental standards are being overlooked; Mexico's government began offering tax-exempt status to border assembly plants in late 1960's, and over years Mexico and its people came to accept poor working conditions and low pay in return for steady jobs; in Acuna, tensions have flared with Alcoa, which has eight plants there; despite Alcoa's wage increases and improvements in factory conditions, Acuna workers still live in squalid grid of dirt streets, rotting garbage and swamps of open sewage; some officials are beginning to question whether Mexico benefits from tax breaks given to foreign companies; photos; map (L)
news.title: Profits Raise Pressures On U.S.-Owned Factories In Mexican Border Zone

news.abstract: Myanmar, ruled by one of world's most repressive military governments, welcomes high-level Indian cabinet minister, first to visit since Burmese generals set aside 1990 elections and crushed democracy movement; Jaswant Singh, India's minister of external affairs, or foreign minister, speaks during his visit of growing partnership between two nations; Singh tells Indian reporters traveling with him that he hopes India could encourage return to democracy through its engagement with Myanmar (M)
news.title: Visit by High Indian Minister Warms Ties With Burmese Junta

news.abstract: Ehud Barak has reportedly agreed to serve as defense minister under Israel's Prime Min-elect Ariel Sharon, right-wing leader who crushed him at polls last week; Barak also tentatively agrees to bring his Labor Party into national unity government with Sharon's Likud Party; this would be victory for Sharon's determined bid to forge stable government; agreement between two men is conditioned on final coalition agreement and endorsement of both parties; if agreement stands, Sharon will be flanked by two Laborites, Barak as defense minister and Shimon Peres as foreign minister; Likud-Labor government creates united Israeli front to take on Israeli-Palestinian crisis; Labor would be backing away from or deferring its peace platform, which Sharon opposes; at same time, Labor politicians would be expected to moderate Sharon's hawkish tendencies; photo (M)
news.title: BARAK MAY JOIN SHARON'S CABINET AS DEFENSE CHIEF

news.abstract: Confidential auditor's report finds that Zambia had 'imprudent and irregular' dealings in mineral sales that cost country $60 million in lost revenues, just as World Bank and International Monetary Fund were granting debt relief to 22 poor nations, including Zambia; missing revenues are equal to two years of debt relief, in program to encourage sound financial management; many debts date from cold war era of superpower rivalry, when aid was used to build loyalty to West; Zambia case illustrates judgments that Western institutions must make to avoid allegation that by forgiving debts they are helping foster corruption and mismanaged economies; map (M)
news.title: Draft Audit Faults Zambia's Mining Deals

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, Feb. 16 — The United States and Britain staged air strikes against radar stations and air defense command centers in Iraq today, including targets around Baghdad, in what President Bush called a necessary response to Iraqi provocation.
news.title: U.S. and British Jets Strike Air-Defense Centers in Iraq

news.abstract: Warring parties in Congo move closer to peace with unexpected agreements on handful of crucial issues; Pres Joseph Kabila, breaking with his late father, who was assassinated, agrees to open political talks with rebels challenging his government; he accepts former president of Botswana, Ketumile Masire, as chief facilitator; in exchange, group challenging Kabila agrees to endorse detailed withdrawal plan that had been signed by other parties in December; photo (M)
news.title: Congo Leader Offers Talks To the Rebels; Tensions Ease

news.abstract: News analysis of decision by former Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak to conditionally accept position of defense minister in Likud government of Prime Minister-elect Ariel Sharon; photo (M)
news.title: Lost Bearings in Israel: Some Expectations Defied

news.abstract: US and British warplanes stage air strikes against Iraqi radar stations and air command centers, including targets around Baghdad, in what Pres Bush calls necessary response to Iraqi provocation; raid, carried out by more than three dozen planes, represents escalation of long-running, low-level skirmishes between American and British jets and Iraqi forces; is first in two years against Iraqi targets north of no-flight zone over southern Iraq, which American and British planes have patrolled since 1992; officials say American military commanders in region requested strikes because Iraqi air defense stations have become increasingly aggressive and effective in targeting patrols over zone; photos; map; diagram (M)
news.title: U.S. AND BRITISH JETS STRIKE AIR-DEFENSE CENTERS IN IRAQ

news.abstract: Chinese state media report that another member of banned Falun Gong spiritual group has committed suicide by setting himself on fire on street in western part of Beijing (M)
news.title: Another Falun Gong Member Reportedly Burns Himself in China

news.abstract: Peruvian government calls on Bush administration to step up its effort to apprehend Vladimiro Montesinos, fugitive former Peruvian spy chief, saying US has a special moral obligation to find him in view of his long ties to CIA (M)
news.title: In Spy Hunt, Peru Wants U.S. to Make A Better Effort

news.abstract: Bush administration plans to sponsor United Nations resolution condemning China's record on human rights, but it is unclear how vigorously it will seek international support necessary to make resolution a diplomatic success (M)
news.title: U.S. Is Set to Assail China on Rights at U.N.

news.abstract: Crackdown on Falun Gong spiritual movement is focusing new attention on China's practice of imprisoning dissenters in psychiatric hospitals; China's official press has openly suggested believers are mentally disturbed and need treatment and hundreds of followers reportedly have been forcibly hospitalized and medicated; photo (M)
news.title: China's Crackdown on Sect Stirs Alarm Over Psychiatric Abuse

news.abstract: South African government, after months of criticism for refusing to provide anti-AIDS drugs, has quietly begun offering nevirapine free to pregnant women to help prevent transmission of AIDS virus to infants; clinic in impoverished Guguletu is first in national network of 18 public clinics to offer drug; one tablet taken during labor and single dose for newborn can cut transmission risk by 50 percent; program will reach probably no more than 20 percent of infected pregnant women in AIDS-ravaged nation and offers mothers no hope of drug treatment for selves; map; photo (M)
news.title: AIDS Drug: Giving the Gift of Life in South Africa

news.abstract: United Nations war crimes tribunal in Hague hears testimony from many Bosnia Muslim women trapped in 'quasi brothels' in Foca in 1992 by Bosnian Serb soldiers; trial is first to focus entirely on wartime sex crimes and first in international court to prosecute sexual slavery; three former Bosnian Serb fighters on trial, Dragoljub Kunarac, Radomir Kovac and Zoran Vukovic, are charged with mass rape and forced prostitution; photo (M)
news.title: Bosnian War Trial Focuses on Sex Crimes

news.abstract: Japanese are angry at reports that civilian visitors were at controls of United States Navy submarine Greeneville when it collided with Japanese boat Ehime Maru; mounting Japanese irritation over accident is worsening personal and political troubles of Prime Min Yoshiro Mori, who continued to play golf after learning of incident (M)
news.title: Sub Incident Erodes Trust In Japan Chief And the U.S.

news.abstract: British peacekeepers and United Nations police say 11 people including baby died in bomb blast, Podujevo, that destroyed bus full of Serbs escorted into Kosovo by Swedish peacekeepers; say two others are missing and dozens hurt; attack raises tensions across Kosovo and sets back return of any Serbian refugees; most Albanians express weariness at violence and shame at terrorism; map; photo (M)
news.title: Death Toll in the Kosovo Bomb Attack on Serbs Rises to 11

news.abstract: South Koreans are growing increasingly uneasy about whether they can sustain momentum toward detente with North Korea in face of change of administrations in United States; have been pleased with some of early statements from Bush administration, but note many of Pres Bush's senior advisers have held in recent past that Clinton administration was too eager to normalize ties with North; photo (M)
news.title: Signs of Uneasiness in Seoul Over Change at White House

news.abstract: Top Russian officialr
news.title: A Moscow Pooh-Bah, Bearing Up in Brooklyn

news.abstract: Human Rights Watch urges United Natio
news.title: Rights Group Tells of Taliban Massacres

news.abstract: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change working group says global warming will likely increase crop yields in temperate northern regions while harming agriculture in tropics, further widening gap between industrialized and poor nations; finds rise in global temperatures in recent decades has already had impact on wildlife, glaciers, sea ice and other earth features; warns of damage and disruption from further temperature rise (M)
news.title: Warming's Likely Victims

news.abstract: PALERMO, Sicily—  The Group of Seven countries, seeking to soothe fears about the impact of the U.S. slowdown on the global economy, signaled cautious optimism that the world would avert recession this year, but they also made clear that the United States and Japan, the two biggest economies, needed to take steps to stimulate growth and recovery.
news.title: But Ministers Tell U.S. And Japan That They Must Stimulate Growth : G-7 Leaders Optimistic On Averting Recession

news.abstract: Elisabeth Rosenthal, a New York Times correspondent in Beijing and a physician, visited North Korea Feb. 6-10 with AmeriCares, a private, United States-based relief organization that was inspecting the use of aid it had already provided to North Korea. Two days after Dr. Rosenthal arrived, North Korean authorities told her that she could not work as a reporter during the trip. She said she could not continue the visit under those circumstances, and later left the country.
news.title: Article 2001022090953850769 -- No Title

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, Feb. 21 — Ehud Barak quit politics for the second time in two weeks early today. He resigned as Labor Party chairman in the face of bitter internal opposition, and declined Prime Minister-elect Ariel Sharon's invitation to serve as defense minister.
news.title: Barak Turns Down Sharon and Leaves Politics Again

news.abstract: EUROPE    GERMANY: JEWS TO SUE OVER INTERNET -- The Central Council for Jews said it intended to sue Internet service providers exhibiting extreme right-wing or racist Web pages. The group expressed frustration at what it called the ''snail's pace'' of government action in applying anti-Nazi laws to fight racist and anti-Semitic Internet content.    Desmond Butler (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Spurred by growing international alarm about Osama bin Laden's militant networks, the police in Britain and Germany have recently arrested more than a dozen Islamic radicals. American officials say some of those arrested were plotting terrorist attacks in Europe and elsewhere.
news.title: Hunting bin Laden's Allies, U.S. Extends Net to Europe

news.abstract: Israel holds first public hearings into police killings of 13 people during wave of violent protests by Israeli Arabs in October; hearings are laden with grief of bereaved families and pent-up grievances of Israel's one million Arab citizens; many Israeli Arabs see police shootings as climax of decades of discrimination, including inadequate government funding for their towns and villages, inferior roads and schools, and unemployment and poverty; protests were in sympathy with Palestinian uprising; photo (M)
news.title: Emotions Escalate at Hearing on Killings of Israeli Arabs

news.abstract: Ehud Barak quits politics for second time since his election defeat, resigning as Israeli Labor Party chairman in face of bitter internal opposition and resigning his seat in Knesset; letter to Prime Min-elect Ariel Sharon declines invitation to be defense minister, accusing Sharon of offering less than wholehearted backing during tumultuous last week; Sharon, without Labor Party, will have shaky right-wing coalition and razor-thin majority (M)
news.title: Barak, Angry With His Party and Sharon, Quits Politics Again

news.abstract: Ehud Barak's resignation from Israeli politics noted
news.title: Barak, Under Fire, Again Quits Politics

news.abstract: LONDON, Feb. 21 — Faced with its first outbreak in 20 years of foot-and-mouth disease, a virulent illness that spreads with relentless speed, Britain said today that it was suspending all exports of live animals, milk, meat and other animal products.
news.title: Britain Stops Animal Exports Because of Foot-and-Mouth Disease

news.abstract: Chinese authorities in Beijing sweep streets, give taxi drivers crash course in English phrases and generally burnish city in preparation for inspection by technical delegation from International Olympic Committee; photo (M)
news.title: Beijing Is Given an Olympian Burnish

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair, who will be first European leader to visit Pres Bush, offers to revive his Clinton-era role as bridge between US and Europe, even as US and British bombings of Iraqi targets spark tension with European allies; Blair defends actions but indicates he and Bush will discuss revision of sanctions; blames Saddam Hussein's refusal to spend authorized oil revenues on food and medicines for hardships of Iraqi people (S)
news.title: Blair Seeking To Ease Tension On Iraq Strikes

news.abstract: UNITED NATIONS, Feb. 22 — In a groundbreaking prosecution of sexual slavery, a United Nations war crimes tribunal in the Hague convicted three Bosnian Serbs for taking part in the systematic rape of Muslim women during the Bosnian war and sentenced the men to long prison terms.
news.title: U.N. War Crimes Court Convicts Bosnian Serbs in Rape Case

news.abstract: Ehud Barak's sudden resignation from political life seems to have cleared way for unity government under Israeli Prime Min-elect Ariel Sharon, despite continued opposition from some in Barak's now leaderless Labor Party; has stilled some of Labor infighting (M)
news.title: Barak's Party Reels After His Swift Exit

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, Feb. 22 — An American fighter jet attacked a missile defense battery in Northern Iraq today, Pentagon officials said, resuming low-level skirmishes with Iraqi air-defense forces six days after American and British jets launched the first military strike authorized by President Bush.
news.title: U.S. Fighter Jet Attacks Iraqi Defenses

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II elevates 44 men to rank of cardinal, largest number ever, rite, Rome; has now named 166 cardinals, more than any other pope, and all but 10 of 135 cardinals eligible to vote for next pope; choses prelates who espouse his traditionalist views and bring greater geographical and ethnic diversity to assembly that will choose his successor; three Americans elevated are Cardinals Edward M Egan, Theodore E McCarrick and Avery Dulles; photos (M)
news.title: Shaping a Legacy, Pope Installs 44 Cardinals

news.abstract: PARIS—  Leftist members of the French Parliament attacked Switzerland on Wednesday over money-laundering, accusing the Swiss authorities of paying only lip service to banking standards intended to fight organized crime.
news.title: But Bern Rejects Charges That It Fails to Act Against Money-Laundering : French Assail Swiss on Financial Crime

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, Feb. 23 — On the eve of General Colin L. Powell's first visit to the region as secretary of state, officials in Israel today rebuffed his pleas for an easing of the blockade of Palestinian territories, while Palestinian militants burned him in effigy.
news.title: A Tense Mideast Awaits Powell's Visit

news.abstract: Progress in weaning Peruvian farmers off coca production and into other crops is slowing, and anti-drug officials cannot keep ahead of traffickers and control the many factors that lead farmers to resort to coca in times of economic desperation; coca cultivation actually fell by 12 percent in Peru in 2000, as abandonment and eradication of crop outpaced new plantings; it is feared that as US steps up its effort to eradicate coca crops in Colombia, traffickers will cross borders and increase their activity in Peru; photos (M)
news.title: Desperate Farmers Imperil Peru's Fight on Coca

news.abstract: Transcript of Pres Bush's news conference; photo (M)
news.title: Transcript of President Bush's White House News Conference

news.abstract: Cardinal Lubomyr Husar, leader of Ukrainian Greek Catholics, says he wants Russian Orthodox Church and Vatican to realize that Greek Catholic Church is a genuine Eastern church, but his church is viewed with deep distrust by the leading Esatern Orthodox church in Ukraine, which is under jurisdiction of Russian Orthodox patriarch, Aleksy II, and is also in conflict with two rival Orthodox churches in Ukraine; Husar's elevation to cardinal signals Pope John Paul II's desire to support Catholic churches in countries that are predominantly Eastern Orthodox even as he seeks to improve Rome's strained relations with Eastern Orothodoxy (M)
news.title: New Cardinal In a Clash Of Creeds

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, Feb. 23 — President Bush and Prime Minister Tony Blair of Britain discussed a wide range of world issues today and vowed that their countries would continue to have, as Mr. Bush put it, "an alliance that has made a huge difference in the world."
news.title: Bush Meets With British Prime Minister

news.abstract: CAIRO, Feb. 24 — Secretary of State Colin L. Powell arrived here today on the first leg of his first overseas trip as the United States' chief diplomat and immediately plunged into talks with the Russian foreign minister, Igor S. Ivanov, on the two sides' widely differing plans for missile defenses.
news.title: U.S. and Russians Meet on Defenses Against Missiles

news.abstract: Jehovah's Witnesses win potentially far-reaching victory in Moscow court over prosecutors who sought to ban group under 1997 law that prohibits religious sects that incite hatred or intolerance; city court judge throws out charges that Witnesses broke up families, tried to convert minors without parents' consent and even pushed members toward suicide; ruling means group's 10,000 Moscow adherents can continue to practice their religion freely; it also sets political precedent, though not legal one, for many other religious groups outside Russian mainstream; Orthodox Church has been critical of Witnesses, who have been aggressive in recruiting members (M)
news.title: Religious Sect Gains Victory In Moscow Trial

news.abstract: Pres Andres Pastrana of Colombia says that when he meets with Pres Bush this week he will ask for trade preferences to spur his country's economic growth, rather than press ahead with earlier plan to request $600 million a year in new aid to fight drug trafficking; says he wants Colombia to receive same tariff reductions given to Caribbean and Central American nations through Caribbean Basin Initiative; Colombia is not covered by that trade pact; it is one of four countries in Andean Trade Preference Act, which was intended to stimulate commerce in drug-producing countries but does not offer benefits for important products of Colombia; photo (M)
news.title: Colombian to Ask Bush for Trade Help

news.abstract: Pres Bush tells Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain that United States has no objections to separate rapid-reaction military force to help keep peace in Europe as long as it is clearly secondary to NATO; announcement, coming during Blair's visit to Camp David, is notable because both Secretary of State Colin L Powell and Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld have indicated reservations about European force, which would make use of NATO equipment and could be dispatched on missions that United States does not endorse, or choses not to join; Blair describes purpose of rapid-reaction force quite narrowly; says it would be limited to peacekeeping and humanitarin tasks and is not a standing army; says it would strengthen NATO by offering alternative when NATO does not want to be involved; photo (M)
news.title: BUSH TELLS BLAIR HE DOESN'T OPPOSE NEW EUROPE FORCE

news.abstract: Aquarium has been proposed for site of huge statue of Stalin in Letna Park in Prague that was destroyed in 1962; photos; map (M)
news.title: Prague Journal; Stalin's Ghost Haunts a Czech Park

news.abstract: Bush administration comes under pressure from Christian groups and members of Congress to help Christian rebels in southern Sudan, but nonpartisan group that includes many diplomatic experts on Africa recommends that United States begin international effort to end 18-year-old war there; conflicting recommendations come at time of increased political turmoil in Sudan itself; Islamist leader, Hassan al-Turabi, who was once allied with Pres Omar Hassan al-Bashir, has been detained, along with 30 of his supporters; Turabi had reportedly undetaken his own efforts to end war, which pits northern Islamic govenrment against southern Christian and animist rebels (M)
news.title: Pair of Views About Sudan: Help Rebels Or End War

news.abstract: Bush administration seeks to build international consensus around new, perhaps less punitive sanctions against Iraq; ordinary Iraqis, who have endured decade of incremental misery, are skeptical; country's state-controlled newspapers dismiss Bush's meeting with Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain as 'Anglo-Saxon aggression'; Iraqi officials are defiant, and senior aides to Saddam Hussein are said to feel that Iraq can outlast United States and Britian, using propaganda and diplomacy in Arab world to win complete abandonment of sanctions; photos (M)
news.title: Iraq Defiant as U.S. Lobbies Arabs on Shift in Sanctions

news.abstract: RAMALLAH, West Bank, Feb 25v - U.S. Secretary of State Colin Powell urged Israelis and Palestinians on Sunday to end violence that has taken more than 400 lives in five months, but fresh shootings immediately showed the distance left to go.
news.title: Powell Urges an End Violence and Pledges Support

news.abstract: GENEVA, Feb. 24 — Swiss bankers and officials are bristling once again over accusations, this time from neighboring France, that the country is an international haven for dubious money dealings.
news.title: Swiss Bristle at New Blast at Their Banks

news.abstract: BAGHDAD, Iraq, Feb. 25 — Ten years ago, Saddam Hussein looked — at least in the view of the American- led military alliance that defeated his forces in Kuwait — every inch a finished man, another discredited dictator heading for the ignominy of history's rubbish heap.
news.title: 10 Years Later, Hussein Is Firmly in Control

news.abstract: Saddam Hussein is firmly in control of Iraq 10 years after defeat of his forces in Kuwait, when it was thought that his regime would collapse of its own dead weight; he continues to consign opponents, would-be assassins and 'traitors' to prisons, firing squad and gallows; successfully resists any United Nations inspection of his suspected effort to develop chemical, biological and nuclear weapons; Baghdad is rebuilt with glittering new palaces and state guesthouses, imposing new statues of Hussein and scaffolding cladding the few bombed-out government buildings not yet restored; still, a decade of sanctions has reduced Iraqi people, if not pampered elite, to destitution; photos (M)
news.title: 10 Years Later, Hussein Is Firmly in Control

news.abstract: Swiss bankers and officials are bristling at report to French National Assembly by two Socialist legislators charging that Switzerland is lax in enforcing its laws against laundering money; Finance Ministry accuses authors of arrogance, and Swiss Bankers Association issues point-by-point rebuttal; Swiss banking industry has grown increasingly sensitive to such charges in recent years and believes that it is at disadvantge with banking sectors of competing countries because Swiss laws now require that bankers find out source of money they accept and eschew questionable dealings (M)
news.title: Swiss Angry At Charges Of Laxness In Banking

news.abstract: Russian military officials promise to investigate grave containing a number of bodies found near Russian military base outside Chechen capital, Grozny, but make clear that they believe that its inhabitants were killed by Chechen rebels and not by Russian soldiers (M)
news.title: Russia to Investigate a Mass Grave in Chechnya

news.abstract: BEIJING, Feb. 26 — He had been detained for six months in 1989 for helping to organize a strike, and later he tried to sue the police on behalf of an exiled labor leader, so Zhou Guoqiang, a lawyer and longtime human rights advocate, knew he was on thin ice. Still, he was surprised in 1994 at the pretext they used to jail him.
news.title: China Hones Old Tool: 'Re-educating' Unruly

news.abstract: Poverty and powerlessness of women in Africa and Asia are combining to make them increasingly vulnerable to AIDS, which some research groups are now calling a women's disease; girls and women in many cultures and in the most disadvantaged societies do not have power to reject unwanted or unsafe sex; more than half the people in Africa infected by AIDS are women; special General Assembly session in June will be devoted to AIDS, and women's groups are increasing their effort to have it focus more attention on women's vulnerability (M)
news.title: In India and Africa, Women's Low Status Worsens Their Risk of AIDS

news.abstract: The Fellowship Church in Grapevine, Texas, is not the only church to establish an Internet site to reach a new generation of parishioners. But its new site goes far beyond the traditional Bible messages or video sales.
news.title: AMERICAN TOPICS : Getting Religion — Online

news.abstract: Article on Citibank's former ties to mysterious Cayman Islands bank where drug traffickers hid large sums of money; interviews with government investigators and new study of case by Democratic Senate staff raise questions about Citibank's slow response to signs of problems with M A Bank Ltd, even after US agents seized seized $1.8 million in 1998 from Citibank accounts in one of biggest money-laundering probes ever; Citibank continued to do business with shell bank for almost two years, moving another $300 million through accounts before they were finally closed; Citibank and Citigroup deny knowing anything was amiss (M)
news.title: The Citibank Connection: Real Money, Shadow Banks

news.abstract: SEOUL—  The Russian president, Vladimir Putin, arrived here Monday night in search of an expanded role for Russia on the Korean Peninsula and northeast Asia.
news.title: Russia Wants to Cut Debt and Raise Influence : With Much to Discuss, Putin Arrives in Seoul

news.abstract: PARIS—  A Luxembourg financial facility used by banks to clear stock trades has denounced as "complete nonsense" allegations in France that it has operated secret accounts for money laundering and other illegitimate purposes.
news.title: Luxembourg Firm Rejects Allegations

news.abstract: Group of 100 North Koreans arrives in Seoul on third round of long-awaited family reunions; Pres Kim Dae Jung highlights his 'sunshine' policy as he prepares to receive Russian Pres Vladimir Putin (S)
news.title: North Koreans Join Relatives In the South As Putin Visits

news.abstract: Russia's Federal Security Service, domestic successor to KGB, unexpectedly says that American graduate student John Edward Tobbin, arrested nearly month ago on seemingly minor drug charges, was probably working for United States military intelligence; allegations stir tempest in Russian press and apparently surprise US officials, who say they were close to settling drug charges and securing Tobbin's exit from Russia; photo (M)
news.title: Russia Turns Drug Arrest Into Spy Case

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Minister-elect Ariel Sharon, bolstered by Labor Party's agreement to join him in a unity government, shifts his attention to satisfying demands of potential partners from religious and right-wing political factions; Sharon, long a polarizing figure himself, will inherit Parliament that is fractious collection of small and medium-size parties with widely divergent ideologies, and can only assure himself solid majority by taking pragmatic approach of offering government posts to parties to both his left and his right (M)
news.title: Sharon Turns To Recruiting Some Partners From the Right

news.abstract: South Korean Pres Kim Dae Jung publicly takes Russia's side in debate over United States plan for national missile defense; joint communique issued by Kim with visiting Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin declares that 1972 Antiballistic Missile Treaty, which would be threatend by US plan, is 'cornerstone of strategic stability' (M)
news.title: South Korea Takes Russia's Side in Dispute Over American Plan for Missile Defense

news.abstract: Ethnic clashes that erupted 10 days ago in Kalimantan area of Borneo, where hundreds of people have been decapitated and thousands more left destitute, is drawing minimal response from Indonesian government and little or no reaction by foreign governments; human rights activists and opposition politicians have sharply criticized Pres Abdurrahman Wahid, who departed on two-week overseas trip as conflict unfolded, and Indonesian military and police, which witnesses said stood by and watched as Dayak mobs unleashed campaign of terror against rival Madurese; rejecting calls for his return, Pres Wahid says reports of violence are greatly exaggerated; map; photo (M)
news.title: Borneo Backwater's Clashes Draw Little Notice

news.abstract: KIGALI, Rwanda, Feb. 28 — Two armies in the sprawling conflict in Congo took what appeared to be a major step toward peace today, pulling back soldiers from front-line positions with the expectation that other combatants would do the same soon.
news.title: Rwanda and Uganda Cut Back Troops in Congo

news.abstract: In major step toward peace in Congo, armies of Rwanda and Uganda pull back soldiers from front-line positions with expectation that other combatants will do same soon; Rwanda and Uganda, which are two of six outside nations fighting in Congo, make clear they are not withdrawing their forces entirely; but their latest moves are most hopeful sign since August 1999, when most combatants signed accord they all promptly ignored; foreign diplomats react cautiously to latest events, warning of many failures in past; photo; map (M)
news.title: Rwanda and Uganda Begin Pulling Troops From Congo

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, March 1 — A taxi van exploded in northern Israel today after police stopped it at a roadblock during a search for a terror suspect. As officers were checking passengers' identification cards, a bomb aboard was detonated, killing one person and wounding nine others.
news.title: Bomb in Northern Israel Kills 1, Wounds 9

news.abstract: Russian Federal Security Service says it has no further interest in John Edward Tobin, American student arrested on drug charges last month but accused of training to become American military spy; other Russian officials indicate they might charge him with more serious violations of narcotics law that could lead to lengthy prison sentence; Tobin is graduate student in Voronezh, under State Dept Fulbright scholar program; he was arrested Feb 1 outside nightclub after police found what they say was marijuana in his clothes (M)
news.title: Spy Case Ends for American Held on Russia Drug Charge

news.abstract: Analysis of South Korea's act of independence from Washington, tilting toward Russia on issue of American missile-defense program; South Korean officials say they fear another crisis over North Korea's ballistic missile program, and value Russia's increasingly important role in trying to persuade North Korean leader, Kim Jong Il, to give it up; photo of Pres Vladimir V Putin during visit to Seoul (M)
news.title: South Korea's New Best Friend?

news.abstract: Thirteen people are killed and 70 injured when high-speed passenger train hits empty Land Rover stuck across track and then collides with freight train coming from opposite direction near North Yorkshire village of Great Heck; accident is latest in series of devastating incidents to hit Britain's railways; photo (M)
news.title: 13 Die in British Train Crash, Adding to the Industry's Woes

news.abstract: Secretary of State Colin L Powell's just-completed first trip abroad reveals intensely personal style of diplomacy imbued with authority and confidence; Powell seems reassured that he was able to rally Arab leaders around new policy on Iraq that would tighten sanctions on military equipement and money and relax them on civilian goods; Powell acknowledged during trip that this policy has not been approved by Bush administration, but by traveling early and speaking out, he has put State Department squarely in favor of sanctions reform, not overthrow; several highlights of trip noted (M)
news.title: Powell Goes on the Road And Scores Some Points

news.abstract: Chinese-language edition of Japanese comic book is causing storm in Taiwan over depiction of Taiwanese women who were kept in Japanese military brothels during World War II; mob of Taiwan legislators and other protesters recently stormed into Taipei's biggest bookstore, grabbed armloads of comics and set them on fire on sidewalk outside; critics are outraged by what they say is distorted account of Japan's last years in Taiwan, when army rounded up 'comfort women' for soldiers' use; cartoonist Kobayashi Yoshinori depicts women lining up willingly for duty, and to buttress his claims includes long interview with aging Taiwanese industrialist Hsu Wen-lung, who asserts that no women were forced to serve Japanese military; Hsu's remarks are particularly explosive because he is supporter and adviser to Pres Chen Shui-bian (M)
news.title: Cartoon of Wartime 'Comfort Women' Irks Taiwan

news.abstract: MILAN—  Lucia Sansalvadore, resembling a gothic heroine with her long brown tresses, slight figure and rosary beads, rose at sunrise in the Piedmont town of Asti, packed a van full of her clothing designs, and headed to the most fashionable boutiques in Milan, hoping for a break.
news.title: ITALIAN FASHION : Mavericks With a Touch of Whimsy

news.abstract: Special report on Afghanistan, where thousands of villagers are fleeing famine, many of them dying on journey to bigger towns and cities or borders of neighboring Iran and Pakistan; United Nations officials plea for emergency aid, saying more than million of people are at risk of starvation in country afflicted with unending war, no effectual government and three years of drought; photos of refugee camps; map (M)
news.title: DESPERATE MIGRATION -- A special report.; Fleeing Famine and War, Afghans Again Meet Death

news.abstract: Plan for new dam along Macal River, which raised hopes in Belize of weaning itself from electricity bought from Mexico and providing new water source for existing dam and power plant that struggles during dry season, unleashes barrage of criticism from environmentalists; opponents, who say project would flood sensitive jungle habitat with several endangered species and dispute claim that dam would lower electricity rates, are garnering support of Natural Resources Defense Council and other international groups; map; photos (M)
news.title: Upbeat Plan for a Dam in Belize Turns Nasty

news.abstract: PARIS—  British farmers, long used to seeing their beef banned in Europe, reacted angrily Friday to findings that meat imports from Germany and the Netherlands contained material most at risk from mad cow disease, and a leading agriculture spokesman in Brussels termed the fact "criminal."
news.title: Tissue Tied to Mad Cow Is Found in Some Beef From the Continent : Risky Meat In Imports Angers U.K. Farmers

news.abstract: British farmers fear for their futures as foot-and-mouth disease, highly contagious virus that attacks cloven-hoofed animals like cows, pigs and sheep, spreads; are barring visitors and leaving farms only when necessary; hunting, fishing and sports events have been cancelled to deter spread of virus, which rarely affects humans but can be carried by people, cars, clothes and even wind; photos (M)
news.title: Foot-and-Mouth Disease Intrudes, Putting British Farmers in Dread

news.abstract: oaxaca journal: mexican rebels' hopes
news.title: Oaxaca Journal; Mexican Rebels' Hopes Meet Hard Indian Reality

news.abstract: Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin, ending visits to South Korea and Vietnam, seems pleased that he has re-established Russia as player in region; trip also shows how far Russia lags behind United States, Japan and China in playing meaningful Far East role (M)
news.title: Putin, Ending Asia Trip, Appears Pleased With Renewed Stature

news.abstract: China sentences seven people to death for tax fraud, Guangdong, and executes two others for embezzlement, Guizhou Province; is in midst of wave of executions intended to curb corruption and economic crimes government blames for weakening economy and fears could threaten Communist Party's legitimacy (M)
news.title: China Pursues Executions As Way to Cut Tax Swindles

news.abstract: Iraqis like 66-year-old Hamza Jabbar are anguished at loss of good jobs, pensions and better lives they had in Kuwait, before they were expelled in days following Iraqi invasion of 1991; photo; map; Iraqi regime itself holds onto to proud pronouncements on 'joyous moment' of Saddam Hussein's invasion (M)
news.title: Iraqis Who Look Back in Anguish

news.abstract: Colombian Pres Andres Pastrana, seeking more aid from US and Europe, vows to fight right-wing parramilitaries as well as leftist rebels, interview; some American officials and rights groups see little effort against paramilitary groups, which killed 577 people last year alone; photo (M)
news.title: We're Doing Battle Right and Left, Colombia Insists

news.abstract: C M Woodhouse, writer on modern Greece, dies at age 83; photo (M)
news.title: C. M. Woodhouse, Writer on Modern Greece, Dies at 83

news.abstract: UN conference on racism, planned for this summer in South Africa, may be explosive, given moves afoot to cast globalization as racial issue and to demand reparations for slave trade and colonialism; meeting first proposed by Cuba was always expected to have anti-Western bias, but chance to air grievances has been seized by groups in developing countries from China to Chile (M)
news.title: Global Look at Racism Hits Many Sore Points

news.abstract: Afghanistan's Taliban officially announces ongoing systematic destruction of Great Buddhas of Bamiyan, priceless artifacts that survived wrathful cannon of Genghis Khan 800 years ago; supreme leader Mullah Muhammad Omar has ordered destruction of 'idols' that date to centuries befor Islam supplanted Buddhism, more than 1,000 years ago; international outcry results (M)
news.title: Over World Protests, Taliban Are Destroying Ancient Buddhas

news.abstract: Beijing, March 5 - Prime Minister Zhu Rongji unveiled China's 10th Five-Year Plan today, promising that the country would forge ahead with the introduction of market forces and private enterprise. He said the Government would continue its program of large-scale investment's in the country's infrastructure and other forms of economic stimulus. He also predicted an annual growth rate of 7 percent in the years ahead, somewhat lower than in the previous five years.
news.title: China's Prime Minister Pledges to Promote Private Enterprise

news.abstract: TEHRAN, March 4 — A hard-line court has sentenced Iran's senior election official to jail for vote tampering, the state-run news media reported today, toppling one of the reformist president's top allies just three months before presidential elections.
news.title: Moderate Jailed by Court in Iran

news.abstract: Swiss voters resoundingly reject, by 77 percent margin, referendum calling for immediate negotiations on membership in European Union; government opposed referendum, calling it 'wrong question at the wrong time' (S)
news.title: Swiss Voters Solidly Reject Talks On Joining the European Union

news.abstract: Prince Haakon of Norway, country's hereditary prince, and 27-year-old lover Mette-Marit Tjessem Hoiby have become test for famously tolerant compatriots; Haakon will make her future queen in grand cathedral marriage in summer 2001, even though father of her three-year-old son is convicted cocaine supplier and she has well-known past in Oslo's dance-and-drugs house party scene; direct descendant of Queen Victoria was educated in public schools and received higher education not at Oxford, like grandparents, but at University of California at Berkeley, where he publicly reveled in society markedly more diverse than that in Scandinavia; photos (M)
news.title: Norway's Thoroughly Modern Royal Pair

news.abstract: Beijing, March 5 - Prime Minister Zhu Rongji unveiled China's 10th Five-Year Plan today, promising that the country would forge ahead with the introduction of market forces and private enterprise. He said the Government would continue its program of large-scale investment's in the country's infrastructure and other forms of economic stimulus. He also predicted an annual growth rate of 7 percent in the years ahead, somewhat lower than in the previous five years.
news.title: China's Prime Minister Pledges to Promote Private Enterprise

news.abstract: Population of endangered mountain gorrillas in Volcano National Park in Rwanda, one of two places in world where they still exist, is inching up mainly because of modest conservation efforts to save them; recent preliminary estimate puts population at 358, up from 324 in 1989; scientists are pleased, given that numbers could easily have declined since park straddles Rwanda, Congo and Uganda--part of world with extraordinary amount of strife; important strategy of International Gorilla Conservation Program has been merely to keep park rangers paid and equipped in times of war so they can follow gorillas regularly and continue anti-poaching projects; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Simple Aid to Gorillas Pays Off: Babies in the Bamboo

news.abstract: Leader of Afghanistan's ruling Taliban movement rejects international appeals to spare ancient sculptures of Buddha deemed un-Islamic; says world is creating unnecessary 'drama' about campaign to destroy sculptures (S)
news.title: Afghans Reject Appeals to Spare Statues

news.abstract: Alarm that Britain's outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease may have crossed English Channel mounts after French officials report traces of virus in sheep on nine farms in five regions; government quickly halts meat exports and moves to complete slaughter of more than 50,000 animals that either came from Britain or came in contact with those that did; photo (M)
news.title: Animals Set Afire as France Fears Outbreak

news.abstract: Residents of Castelo de Paiva, small Portuguese town, are in mourning for more than 60 people, killed on March 4 when bridge over Douro River collapsed, dropping crowded bus and two cars into raging waters; sorrow is mixed with anger; many say they have long complained to central government that 116-year-old bridge was unsafe, but that money to repair it was never given; public works minister, Jorge Coelho, resigns; Prime Min Antonio Guterres rejects criticisms of government during visit to assess damage (S)
news.title: Lisbon Blamed After a Plunge That Killed 60

news.abstract: ASIA    JAPAN: MORI SURVIVES VOTE -- Prime Minister Yoshiro Mori survived a no-confidence vote brought by the opposition. The governing Liberal Democratic Party, together with its coalition partners, blocked the motion in a 274-to-192 vote that largely followed party lines. Mr. Mori called the vote a show of confidence in his government. But with his own party members increasingly calling for his replacement, the vote was seen as little more than a face-saving reprieve for Mr. Mori, who is widely expected to quit soon.   Howard French (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Pres Jim Dae Jung of South Korea arrives, Washington, for meeting with Pres Bush; faces possible clash with administration over right strategy for dealing with North Korea as it emerges from self-imposed isolation for first time in nearly 50 years; plans by Kim to sign peace 'declaration' with North in coming months noted; decision comes as Bush administration is undertaking thorough review of American policy toward North Korea, with clear view toward taking far harder line than Clinton administration; senior administration officials continue to view North as major threat; are wary that Kim's peace initiatives have moved too fast, with too few concessions from North; photo (M)
news.title: Korean to Visit Bush, but They Could Be at Odds

news.abstract: GENEVA—  Tackling the threat of global warming can be effectively started with existing technologies if governments decide to take action, a group of top climate-change experts says in a final report wrapping up the first comprehensive study of climate change data in five years.
news.title: Warming Data:The Threat Can Now Be Tackled

news.abstract: The destruction of two giant Buddhas carved out of a mountainside at Bamian, in the highlands of Afghanistan, is a disaster of abysmal proportions reminiscent of China's Cultural Revolution.
news.title: Taleban's Act Flies in Face of Islam's Tenets

news.abstract: SHANGHAI, March 7 — Rescue workers combed through the rubble of a school in central China today, looking for clues to an explosion Tuesday that killed 41 people, most of them children.
news.title: 41 Killed After School in China Explodes

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, March 7 - President Bush told President Kim Dae Jung of South Korea today that he would not resume negotiations with North Korea on missile talks anytime soon, putting the United States and a major Asian ally at sharp odds over how to deal with the communist regime.
news.title: South Korean President and Bush at Odds on North Korea

news.abstract: Security Council votes unanimously to bar all diamond exports from Liberia if country does not stop supporting rebel army that has ravaged neighboring Sierra Leone (M)
news.title: Behave or Face a Diamond Ban, Security Council Tells Liberians

news.abstract: NATO soldiers in Kosovo open fire and wound two Albanian gunmen, raising prospect that peacekeeping force could become tangled in violent Albanian insurgency that has suddenly flared in neighboring Macedonia; peacekeepers are in command of multinational force that moved into Kosovo village of Mijak in operation to stem flow of arms and men to Albanian guerrillas in Macedonia, where clashes have erupted between ethnic Albanians and Macedonian military force; photo (M)
news.title: NATO Soldiers Fire on Kosovo Albanians

news.abstract: Rade Markovic, Serbia's former secret police chief, and several other senior police officers who served under Pres Slobodan Milosevic will be summoned as witness in trial in Belgrade of 10 men accused of killing Arkan, notorious paramilitary leader; Vojislav Jekic, former police chief of Loznica, testifies that two of defendants told him that group was responsible for killings and that it was backed by Markovic and a wealthy businessman (M)
news.title: Witness Ties Ex-Police Boss To Killing Of Warlord

news.abstract: SKOPJE, Macedonia, March 8 — United States-led peacekeeping troops in southern Kosovo occupied a village on the border with Macedonia today, as part of a coordinated move with Macedonian military forces through the night and morning to flush out ethnic Albanian rebels from their mountain base.
news.title: NATO Troops Help Macedonians Drive Away Ethnic Albanian Rebels

news.abstract: Explosion in school in Wanzai, China, kills 41 people, mostly children, who reportedly have been assembling fireworks in a business set up by head teacher and local officials; officials deny reports that blast went off during assembly of fireworks, dominant industry in impoverished region; map (M)
news.title: Explosion Kills 41 in School in Central China

news.abstract: Ruling by federal Judge Gabril Cavallo to overturn two laws granting immunity to hundreds of military officers comes as another sign that human rights law is gaining new force in Argentina; ruling is expected to lead to new criminal complaints against military commanders, perhaps including current army chief Gen Ricardo Brinzoni, who served in 1976-83 military dictatorship that was involved in killings of more than 15,000 people case is expected to put Pres Fernando de la Rua in awkward
news.title: Argentine Court Ruling Could Open the Military to Prosecution

news.abstract: GENEVA—  On the day set aside each year for women to celebrate their progress and achievements, there were some sober notes Thursday reminding women that while they are increasingly able to support themselves, they still face discrimination and even violence in the workplace, in public life and at home.
news.title: Worldwide, There Remains a 'Long Way to Go' in Combating Inequality : Rallying Cries on a Sober Women's Day

news.abstract: Throughout the United States, chores are becoming as obsolete as hi-fi turntables. The amount of time 9- to 12-year-olds spent doing housework declined 30 percent from 1981 to 1997, from an average of 5 hours a week to 3 hours, 42 minutes a week, according to a University of Michigan researcher.
news.title: American Topics : Chores:A Thing of the Past

news.abstract: Largely American peacekeeping force goes on offensive against Albanian rebels, occupying village of Tanusevci on Macedonia-Kosovo border in coordinated move with Macedonia to flush guerrillas from their mountain base; operation by some 300 peacekeepers is most powerful thrust to date against Albanian gunmen moving between Macedonia and Kosovo; NATO's original mission in Kosovo was to drive Serbian forces out and police the province, but major challenge now is armed Albanians who have taken control of border areas inside Serbia and are also active in Macedonia; map; photo (M)
news.title: G.I.'s Join Macedonians in Fight Against Albanian Rebels

news.abstract: Bush administration tells NATO allies that it will not let American peacekeepers cross from Kosovo into Serbia proper despite spreading Albanian insurgency; Britain and other allies have urged more assertive action to monitor Albanian insurgents in border zone in Serbia from which NATO has excluded Yugoslav Army; administration concern that expanded mission would embroil US in wider Balkans conflict comes even as largely American force of peacekeepers takes its strongest action to date against Albanians in Macedonia, where an insurgency has also sprung up; troops act to support Macedonian government, which fears an open rebellion that could foment its Albanian minority and cause wider conflict; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Won't Send Its Kosovo G.I.'s On Peacekeeping Patrol in Serbia

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon has told Yasir Arafat that he hopes they can establish 'personal contact' after violence diminishes in region, but prospects for meeting any time soon appear remote as street clashes and gun battles flare anew throughout Gaza and West Bank; photo (M)
news.title: Leaders' Cordiality Doesn't Halt Gaza Clashes

news.abstract: News analysis of AIDS epidemic in Africa; says now that world's biggest pharmaceutical companies have been forced into painful negotiations over patient rights and price of medicines, question suddenly is no longer whether Africans will get life-saving drug cocktails, but how; many African nations are too poor to afford medicines, even at steeply discounted prices, and some lack infrastructure to deliver drugs and educate patients about how to use them (M)
news.title: Africa's AIDS War

news.abstract: SHANGHAI, March 10 — When Qiu Xuanming's body arrived at the crematory from the execution ground last June, his brother recognized it by the clothes it wore. Mr. Qiu's head, which had been shot in the back at close range, was a tightly wrapped ball of white gauze, but the clothes were the same he had worn at his final court hearing a little more than an hour before.
news.title: A Tale of China's Harsh and Secretive Justice

news.abstract: AL BIREH, West Bank, March 8 — Muhammad Darraj, a 40-year-old construction worker with weathered hands and dirt-caked boots, moved his family into a new apartment with a commanding view of a Jewish settlement several weeks ago. His reasons were pedestrian but loomed large in his life: he wanted to own, not rent.
news.title: Palestinians Delicately Begin Debate on Circle of Violence

news.abstract: TOKYO, March 10 — After a week of resignation rumors and steady denials, Prime Minister Yoshiro Mori met privately with senior members of his party today to signal his intention to step down early next month.
news.title: Japan's Chief Sends Signal He's Prepared to Step Down

news.abstract: Dani tribe, largest ethnic group in Irian Jaya, Indonesia, lives much as its ancestors did, six decades after Western explorers arrived; but ancient farming village of Anemaugi faces church and government pressures to change its ways; tribal leaders and anthropologists express concern that growing number of Dani young people are abandoning tribe's traditions and animist beliefs for modern conveniences and Christianity; they blame mounting pressure fromp government and missionaries, who have tried hard to bring Dani into modern world, as well as recent influx of migrants from other parts of Indonesia and foreign tourists; photos; map (L)
news.title: Stone Age Ways Surviving, Barely

news.abstract: Uganda Pres Yoweri Museveni faces election challenge; Dr Kizza Besigye is his main opponent; compared with election campaigns in other African countries, Uganda's election has had relatively contained violence; but given Museveni's accomplishments since he took office in 1986, disappointments run deep; and given Uganda's past, violence has scared many Ugandans; photos (L)
news.title: Election Bringing Out New Uganda's Rough Edges

news.abstract: Members of largest tribal group in British Columbia sign their first treaty with provincial and federal governments; treaty gives Indians--7,000 members of Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council--self-rule, a large cash payment and shared control with non-Indians of spectacular old-growth forests and other natural resources; map (M)
news.title: Canada and British Columbia's Largest Indian Group Taking Steps to First Permanent Treaty

news.abstract: Yasir Arafat, in his first major speech since violence erupted last fall, reaffirms his commitment to 'strategic path of peace' but stops short of calling for end to violence as a component of Palestinian uprising; addresses first full meeting of Palestinian legislative council in more than five months, Gaza City; photo (M)
news.title: Arafat Stops Short of Rejecting Violence

news.abstract: Colombia rebels, who have been cold to idea of foreign participation in peace talks, agree to meet with envoys from 25 countries, move that is seen encouraging sign; rebels agree that small group of nations could serve as facilitators in future peace negotiations (M)a
news.title: Some Hopeful Signs as Colombia Meets With Rebels and Envoys

news.abstract: KATETE, Uganda, March 12 — Voting today in Uganda was far more peaceful than the last few weeks of campaigning, but at least here, problems lingered: Felix Hakiza, holding his 4-year-old son by the hand, showed up to vote this afternoon only to find that someone else had done it for him.
news.title: Ugandans Casting Their Votes Today for President

news.abstract: Mexico's Zapatista rebels and leader Subcommander Marcos end two-week trek from jungle hideout in Chiapas with massive demonstration in capital of Mexico City; Marcos addresses throng, estimated at 100,000; demands democracy, liberty and justice for nation's minority Indian population of about 10 million; disproportionately poor, illiterate, malnourished and disenfranchised, they have been traditionally treated as second-class citizens; photos (M)
news.title: Zapatista Rebels Rally in Mexico City

news.abstract: Washington Memo on gap in tone between Pres Bush and Sec of State Colin L Powell; says it raises questions of whose voice is dominant in foreign policy and in longer term which opinions will prevail; early disagreements could put factions within Republican Party at odds with one another, leaving Bush to pick policy and risk alienating some faction and possible overseas allies; early disagreements over Iraq and North Korea discussed (M)
news.title: Washington Memo; Divergent Voices Heard In Bush Foreign Policy

news.abstract: Syria is living through heady period of ferment, shifting from repressive and stagnant socialized state created by late president Hafez al-Assad, to reign of son Bashar al-Assad and outcome remains uncertain; change is in keeping with Bashar's promise to transform country, fostering more openness and robust economy, but has been more in tone than substance; daily life remains unchanged and long-dominant Baath Party easily ressurects oppressive measures whenever it deems denunciations of government to be too harsh; even though Bashar intimates he wants freer country, question remains how free; general sense is that he seeks change along lines of China, unfettering economy while Baath Party hold political reins firmly; photo (M)
news.title: Syria Reaches Turning Point, But Which Way Will It Turn?

news.abstract: Four-day meeting in Geneva, aimed at bringing some coherence to agenda of an UN conference on racism in August, ends with virtually every major issue still in dispute; European countries and bloc of Asian, African and Latin American nations said to be increasingly divided over what conference will address (M)
news.title: 2 Stubborn Factions Divide Coming U.N. Meeting on Racism
