news.abstract: Human rights groups say UN Human Rights Commission, focal point of debate among nations on range of political and civil liberties, is growing steadily less free and tolerant in its membership; say makeup of commission, whose members are elected for staggered three-year terms, is becoming problematic with each passing year; recent ranking of commission members found approximately half represent governments with repressive human rights policies; some members bar human rights monitors from visiting their countries (S)
news.title: A U.N. Paradox: Some on Rights Panel Are Accused of Wrongs

news.abstract: Four Colombian governors charge American-supported aerial spraying of illicit coca crops is jeopardizing health and food supply of small-scale farmers; are urging Pres Andres Pastrana and Bush administration to rethink what they maintain is militaristic approach toward peasant farmers, in exchange for plan involving social pacts and alternative crops in southern drug-growing states that they represent (M)
news.title: Colombian Governors Protest U.S.-Backed Spraying of Coca

news.abstract: Russia's Pres Vladimir V Putin breaks openly with US and predecessor Boris N Yeltsin, formally agreeing to resume sales of conventional arms to Iran after hiatus of more than five years; reiterates at Kremlin meeting with Pres Mohammad Khatami Russia's intention to help Iran complete long-stalled nuclear power plant some American experts contend could advance Iran's nuclear weapons program; announcements, neither unexpected, come during first meeting in four decades between Iranian and Russian heads of state in warm session billed as diplomatic turning point; meeting is seen as pointed signal to Bush administration that Iranians and Russians intend to limit American influence in Middle East by both diplomatic and military means; Russia sold approximately $5 billion in weapons to Iran from 1989 and 1995, when sales stopped under terms of accord signed secretly with US by former Pres Boris Yeltsin; photo (M)
news.title: Putin to Sell Arms and Nuclear Help to Iran

news.abstract: Israeli Army seals off Ramallah, unofficial seat of government of Palestinian Authority in West Bank; blocks roads with trenches, mounds of earth and checkpoints backed by tanks and armored troop carriers; action is first against Palestinians by newly inaugurated government of Prime Min Ariel Sharon and is most severe blockade imposed by Israelis on major commercial and cultural community of 60,000 people; Palestinians officials condemn action as collective punishment; Sharon denies blockade represents new policy; says it is imposed to foil car bombing in Jerusalem following arrest of members of group planning attack; says policy is directed at attackers and their accomplices; Defense Min Binyamin Ben-Eliezer orders lifting of less stringent blockades imposed by previous government on four other West Bank cities; photo; map (M)
news.title: Sharon Blockades a Palestinian Center in the West Bank

news.abstract: SEOUL, March 13 — North Korea postponed without warning today a series of meetings planned for this week between North and South Korean cabinet members on major topics affecting inter-Korean relations.
news.title: North Korea Abruptly Cancels Meetings with South

news.abstract: US bans imports of animals and animal products from European Union countries in response to spread of foot-and-mouth disease from Britain to France; photos; virus poses little danger to people but is virulently contagious and devastating among cloven-hoofed animals; Belgium, Portugal, Spain, Switzerland and other countries take parallel measures; Canada bans meat from Argentina as well because disease has been found there; Agriculture Department explains that most cheeses and cured or cooked meats are not affected because heating preparation kills virus; pork producers are most affected since most European beef is already banned by US because of mad cow disease (M)
news.title: MEAT FROM EUROPE IS BANNED BY U.S. AS ILLNESS SPREADS

news.abstract: FRANKFURT, March 14 — A foundation set up by German industry announced on Tuesday that it had raised nearly $2.5 billion to compensate former slave workers during the Third Reich, but executives said today they will not release the money until all lawsuits pending in the United States have been dismissed.
news.title: Fund for Former Slaves of Third Reich Tops $2.5 Billion

news.abstract: Western European countries have chosen to deal with foot-and-mouth disease largely by slaughter and cremation during rare outbreaks, rather than by inoculating animals as many other countries, including some in Eastern Europe, do; some British scientists argue that killing huge numbers is senseless because 80-95 percent will survive disease; urge return to pre-1991 practice of inoculation (S)
news.title: Foot-and-Mouth's Harsh Approach

news.abstract: Israel eases tight blockade of Ramallah, opening two roads on West Bank and allowing some Palestinians through after security checks (S)
news.title: Under Pressure, Israel Eases Blockade a Bit at West Bank City

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  A U.S. serviceman on the ground at a firing range in Kuwait mistakenly directed a pilot to drop his bombs over the site where he and other observers were watching a routine exercise, then sought frantically, but in vain, to call off the bombing, American officials said Tuesday.
news.title: Pilot Given Wrong Site For Bombs In Kuwait

news.abstract: Confirmation of 27 new cases of foot-and-mouth disease brings total in Britain to 232 and prompts Prime Min Tony Blair to order intensified slaughter of animals in areas directly affected; he also says government should consider easing restrictions caused by disease in economically hard-hit regions that are free of virus; says difficulty is weighing any relaxation of rules with need to make sure government is taking right precautions; Australia, which earlier banned importing horses from Britain, expands its ban to include all livestock from Europe (M)
news.title: As the Disease Marches On, Britain Dooms More Animals

news.abstract: North Korea calls United States 'a cannibals' nation' and charges Bush administration with escalating provocative and reckless diatribe against North; pledges 'thousandfold revenge' if United States turns to confrontation; North has been ratcheting up its criticism since Pres Bush, in talks with South Korean president, Kim Dae Jung, expressed 'skepticism' about North Korean leader, Kim Jong Il (M)
news.title: North Korea Turns Up the Heat; Calls U.S. a Nation of Cannibals

news.abstract: SAN FRANCISCO—  This is what the Japanese are discovering about the San Francisco Bay area: It almost feels like home. Home without the kinks of societal and corporate pressures, frenetic pace (and damnable cost) of living. Home plus leafy tree-lined streets and trolley cars and coffee that comes in stupendously large cups.
news.title: Japan's Affair With Bay Area

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, March 15 — Administration officials said today that President Bush intends to make a state visit to China in October, but the White House held off on an official announcement of the visit even though Chinese Prime Minister Zhu Rongji prematurely mentioned it in Beijing.
news.title: Bush Plans to Visit China in October

news.abstract: Pres Yoweri Museveni sweeps hard-fought elections in Uganda, winning 69.3 percent of vote; his main challenger, Kizza Besigye, takes 27.8 percent and four other candidates split rest; Museveni calls his victory acclamation of 15 years of peaceful rule; Besigye accuses him of extensive cheating and vote rigging; weeks leading up to election were fraught with incidents of violence, disturbing to nation so eager to transcend its turbulent past; photo (M)
news.title: Final Count Has Uganda President Winning 69% of Vote

news.abstract: SHANGHAI, March 16 — A series of apparently coordinated blasts killed at least 18 people in an industrial city 120 miles south of Beijing early Friday, sending riot police into the streets and sparking rumors that laid-off factory workers were wreaking revenge.
news.title: Blasts in China Leave at Least 18 Dead

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  Hong Kong is still a magnet for the born-to-consume crowd, but now the main attraction is a shopping mall just across the border in mainland China.
news.title: Shenzhen Lures Savvy Shoppers

news.abstract: Outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease is taking its toll on entire regions of England where hoteliers, shopkeepers and suppliers depend on visitors for their livelihoods; much of Britain has been placed off limits to walkers and outsiders for fear they may carry disease to infect new animals; many hotels are all but empty, roads are free of tourists' cars and delivery vans, and employees in tourism business are being laid off; photo (M)
news.title: Foot-and-Mouth Damages English Tourism, Too

news.abstract: Police troops in Tetovo, Macedonia's second-largest city, battle ethnic Albanian rebels at edge of town for two days, and there have been some civilian casualties; fighting demonstrates how Albanians are intensifying their activity in Macedonia, even as Albanian rebels in southern Serbia, east of Kosovo, enter negotiations to end year of conflict there; insurgents are trying to dominate border areas in Macedonia where residents are overwhelmingly Albanian; photo; map (M)
news.title: Albanian Rebels Widen Attack Along Macedonia Border

news.abstract: Prime Min Zhu Rongji makes highly unusual nationally televised apology to people of China for deadly schoolhouse explosion in rural Jiangxi Province, and softens earlier denials that children at school were making fireworks; says he has ordered high-level investigation; government's attempts to contain conflicting accounts of blast were undermined by citizens' rapidly spreading access to Internet and other information channels and by increasingly self-assertive press; explosion killed 42 people, 38 of them children aged 9 to 11 years old; local government had announced that deranged suicide bomber was responsible for blast; bereaved parents and surviving students unanimously rejected this, saying children were forced to make fireworks at school; attempted media blackout only fueled speculation that there was coverup reaching into central government; photo (M)
news.title: China Backs Away From Initial Denial In School Explosion

news.abstract: Battle over Paris mayoralty continues to provide twists, turns, name-calling, bruised egos and distinct possibility that conservatives will lose control of capital for first time in more than century; Parisians are disgusted with corruption charges that plague right, and bewildered by spectacle of conservative candidates insulting each other; many pollsters believe voters may give Socialists' candidate, Bertrand Delanoe, a narrow victory; current mayor, Jean Tiberi, who had been handpicked for job by Pres Jacques Chirac, has become subject of growing number of investigations; Tiberi has refused to step aside for Philippe Seguin, chosen by his party to run for mayor; photo (M)
news.title: Ego Bashing And Scandals As Paris Picks A New Mayor

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    BRAZIL: SINKING OIL RIG  The world's biggest offshore oil rig, hit by a series of blasts on Thursday that killed at least one person and left nine missing, could sink within days as the chances of recovery fade, said the president of the state oil company, Petrobras. Engineers said the sinking of the 40-story rig could cause an environmental catastrophe as oil spills into the sea. The cause of the explosion is still unknown.   (Reuters)    ASIA    INDIA: ARMS SCANDAL INQUIRY  The cabinet authorized a Supreme Court judge to begin an investigation into allegations of high-level corruption that came to light in a sting operation by journalists pretending to be arms dealers. For the fourth day, the opposition forced the adjournment of Parliament in protest over the scandal, but the governing coalition rallied around Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee.    Celia W. Dugger (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Chtaura, Lebanon, just 10 miles from Syrian border, has prospered even during years of civil war that made Beirut unlivable; Syrian citizens visit Chtaura in droves to stash their illegal dollars away from prying eyes in Lebanese banks, to get credit cards that Syria's state-controlled banks do not issue, and to shop for delicacies, like real Coca-Cola, not available or forbidden in their own country; bankers and merchants of Chtaura worry that boom may end now that Hafez al-Assad has died and been succeeded by his son, Bashar al-Assad, who has started relaxing all kinds of rules in Syria; photo; map (M)
news.title: Chtaura Journal; In a Foreign Town, Syrians (Shhh!) Bank and Buy

news.abstract: Apparently coordinated explosions kill at least 18 people in Shijiazhuang, industrial city 120 miles south of Beijing, send riot police into streets and spark rumors of laid-off textile workers and others seeking revenge; map (S)
news.title: Blasts Kill 18 In Textile City South of Beijing

news.abstract: Saudi Arabian police officers force their way into hijacked Russian jet, freeing more than 100 passengers and shooting dead one hijacker after he fatally stabs flight attendant; Turkish passenger is also reported killed in raid; plane was seized by three or four armed men as it took off from Istanbul bound for Moscow; it landed in western Saudi city of Medina; Saudi and Russian officials say hijackers are from rebellious Russian republic of Chechnya; Pres Vladimir V Putin reportedly gave his consent to Saudi authorities to storm plane; Russia's Foreign Ministry asks Saudi authorities to return hijackers to Russia, although two countries have no extradition treaty (M)
news.title: Saudi Arabian Police Raid Hijacked Russian Jetliner

news.abstract: Irina Bugrimova, Russian circus animal tamer, dies at age 90; photo (M)
news.title: Irina Bugrimova, 90, an Enchanter of Big Cats

news.abstract: Rank and file in Japan's Liberal Democratic Party signal that they will no longer entrust transition matters to party's elderly barons when Prime Min Yoshiro Mori steps down; demand that voting for next party president be opened to rank and file for first time; they are stepping up pressure, publicly voicing their discontent with their own party with passion and directness rare in Japan's usually muted politics; some local chapters are even calling for direct election of prime minister; it is not clear how far revolt can go, but open airing of discontent has prompted one major concession from leadership: starting in September, local chapters will be allowed to vote in party leadership elections (M)
news.title: Less Patient, Japan Awaits A Transition

news.abstract: Harold Davis, known as The Great Alanza, high-wire daredevil whose act inspired New York's safety net law for aerial acts, dies at age 82; photo (M)
news.title: Great Alzana, Who Mocked Danger and New York Law on the High Wire, Dies at 82

news.abstract: Colonel's trial in killing of young Chechen woman puts Russian justice to test; Col Yuri D Budanov, highest-ranking officer to be accused of crime against Chechen civilian, admits that he abducted, beat and killed 18-year-old Elza Kungayeva in Grozny, Chechnya's capital, year ago; claims he believed she was rebel sniper who had killed soldiers in his regiment, and that he killed her in uncontrollable fit of revenge; woman's father disputes this, saying Budanov had 'noticed' his daughter in days before abduction; initial accusation of rape, documented by autopsy, has vanished; Human Rights Watch has documented thousands of cases in which Russian military killed, tortured and raped Chechen civilians with no punishment; despite fact that Kremlin itself expressed outrage at Kungayeva's killing, half of Russians polled feel Budanov should be set free; photos; map (M)
news.title: Colonel's Trial Puts Russian Justice to Test

news.abstract: Newspapers in Shijiazhuang, China, carry rare front-page wanted notice for Jin Ruchao, reportedly a suspect in Mar 16 coordinated explosions in four buildings that shook city and caused 108 deaths; Jin lives in one of destroyed buildings and is aready wanted for murder in death of woman several weeks ago; photo (M)
news.title: Suspect Sought In China Blasts; Toll Is at 108

news.abstract: Federal Bureau of Investigation identifies Vladimir Frolov, Russian press attache in Washington who abruptly cut short second tour of duty in US, as spy who may have handled Richard P Hanssen, agency operative who has been charged with spying for Russia; officials say Frolov was not forced to leave by US; speculate departure may have been part of pre-emptive move by Russian government in anticipation of Bush administration demands that some of its intelligence officers leave (M)
news.title: As a Russian Hurries Home, Washington Is Suspicious

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, March 19 — President Bush and Japan's weakened prime minister, Yoshiro Mori, met today to discuss joint strategies for restoring growth to the world's largest and second-largest economies, but ended the session with a vague commitment by Japan to confront its huge banking problem and not to seek a short-term solution by boosting exports to the United States.
news.title: U.S. and Japan Make Pledge to Collaborate on Economy

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, March 19 — Persian Gulf oil states are tossing a lifeline to the financially foundering Palestinian Authority in the form of a $300 million aid package. This will make Arab donors the Authority's chief source of budgetary support for the first time.
news.title: Gulf Arab States Prepare a Bailout to Assist Arafat

news.abstract: Pres Bush prepares for meeting with China's Deputy Prime Min Qian Qichen in Washington, first with senior Chinese official, as administration faces crucial decisions on military issues that could quickly put US on collision course with Beijing; issues are whether to design national missile defense capable of countering China's small nuclear force or whether to sell Aegis destroyers to Taiwan; China's concern that Aegis system could be used as platform for missile shield for Taiwan and usher in new level of American military cooperation with island, regarded as renegade province, noted; importance of issues among conservative Republicans, who are deeply suspicious of Beijing and who represent important Bush constituency, discussed (M)
news.title: BUSH DUE TO MEET CHINESE ON ISSUES CRUCIAL FOR TIES

news.abstract: Senior Western diplomats say ethnic Albanians attacking Macedonian and Serbian governments are hoping to force international community into another diplomatic intervention that will alter borders in Balkans; say West has no intention of calling new international conference, like 1995 Dayton meeting that ended Bosnian war, or of blessing violent shifting of borders; photo (M)
news.title: Rebels Hope to Shift Borders in Balkans, Diplomats Say

news.abstract: Mary Robinson, UN high commissioner for human rights, says she will step down when term ends in September 2001 and will carry on fight for human rights without 'constraints' imposed by organization; criticisms and controversies that have marked her tenure discussed (M)
news.title: Rights Chief At U.N. Says She'll Leave In September

news.abstract: Persian Gulf oil states toss lifeline to financially foundering Palestinian Authority in form of $300 million aid package, making Arab donors its chief source of budgetary support for first time; Islamic Development Bank, under plan devised with support of International Monetary Fund, will provide up to $40 million per month for six months from new 'intifada fund;' most of money will come from Saudi Arabia, United Emirates and Kuwait, which previously refused to privide direct aid to semiautonomous government; payments are in addition to unpublicized transfer of $80 million in Arab grants and loans to authority since December 2000, exceeding $65 million received from European governments; photo (M)
news.title: GULF ARAB STATES PREPARE A BAILOUT TO ASSIST ARAFAT

news.abstract: Intense fighting between Albanian rebels and government forces near Tetovo, Macedonia, described; Albanians appear to have arms, ammunition and men they need in drive taking shape around country's second-largest town to take over large areas of Albanian populations; Macedonian Army deploys tanks and truckoads of troops in and around area for 'final operation' to rout rebels, who have grown from handful of fighters reportedly to force of several hundred; map; photo (M)
news.title: On the Front in Macedonia: A Show of Rebels' Tenacity

news.abstract: Tran Van Lam, former foreign minister of South Vietnam, dies at age 88; photo (S)
news.title: Tran Van Lam, 88, Top South Vietnam Aide

news.abstract: Subcommander Marcos, leader of Mexico's Zapatista rebels who traveled to capital in hopes of achieving political settlement with government, says he will return to jungle in Chiapas; decision follows failure of efforts to pass measure that would give some autonomy to indigenous Indian communities (S)
news.title: Indian Rights Bill Falters in Mexico; Rebel Going Home

news.abstract: Russian Foreign Ministry scores as 'openly confrontational' remarks by United States Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld and his deputy, Paul D Wolfowitz, in British newspaper interview complaining of Russia's role in providing missile technology to Iran and other nations; interview comes at time when Bush administration weighs possibly down-grading ties with Russia (M)
news.title: Moscow Says Remarks by U.S. Resurrect 'Spirit of Cold War'

news.abstract: Pres Vicente Fox, in break with aloof style of past Mexican presidents, is mixing warmly with public, making frequent speeches and putting his Catholic faith on display; his romance with Martha Sahagun, his chief spokeswoman, is frequent fodder for newspaper columns; Fox says he seeks to be closer to people, interview; photo (M)
news.title: President of Mexico Does Not Stand on Ceremony

news.abstract: Macedonia threatens to wipe out ethnic Albanian rebels who occupy hills above Tetovo unless they surrender or withdraw in 24 hours; rebel commander rejects ultimatum; army has begun intensive drive against rebels, using tanks and artillery for first time in weeklong fighting in and around city; Albanian leader Arben Xhaferi threatens to pull out of multi-ethnic governing coalition if civilians are hurt or artillery is used against civilian targets, news conference; he says he opposes offensive and his party was not included in decision to launch it; scores rebels and their use of force; hails accord among all Albanian parties rejecting violence and appealing for peace; map; photo (M)
news.title: Macedonia Gives Rebels an Ultimatum

news.abstract: LONDON, March 21 - A report into five deaths from the human form of mad cow disease in the same English village concluded today that the cause was a traditional local method of slaughter that permitted brain matter from diseased animals to contaminate cuts of meat.
news.title: English Village Butchery Blamed for Mad Cow Deaths

news.abstract: AFRICA    UGANDA: EX-CANDIDATE QUESTIONED -- The police questioned the loser in last week's presidential race over a spate of attacks that have killed more than a dozen people around the country since the election. The former candidate, Dr. Kizza Besigye, left, who was President Yoweri Museveni's physician, denied any involvement in the attacks, saying the government is harassing him because of his accusations that Mr. Museveni won only by wholesale vote rigging. Last weekend, army officials prevented Dr. Besigye from traveling to South Africa because of what they said were suspicions that he may have been linked to the attacks.    Ian Fisher (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: MOSCOW, March 22 — Russia said today that the expulsion of 50 Russian diplomats accused of spying in the United States was a hostile act that would lead to the expulsion of American diplomats here.
news.title: Russia Warns It Will Reply in Kind to Ouster of Envoys

news.abstract: TETOVO, Macedonia, March 22 — Top European Union officials urged the Macedonian government today to exercise restraint against ethnic Albanian militants and to intensify discussions with elected Albanian politicians about political change.
news.title: Europeans Urge Macedonia to Use Restraint With Rebels

news.abstract: Growing numbers of Iraqis are ready to take risk of whispering their fear of Saddam Hussein and deep-seated hatred they say he has engendered among country's 23 million people; even officials at senior levels are beginning to speak of time when Hussein will no longer be country's ruler; some even allude to his eventual death; decade ago, suggesting that Hussein might be mortal was unthinkable in Iraq; there are rumors that Hussein is ill; Hussein has offered no public denial of this, and he has kept up vigorous schedule of official duties; Central Intelligence Agency has been dismissive of such rumors; photo (M)
news.title: Iraqis Now Daring to Talk of Life After Hussein

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  The Hong Kong Internet tycoon Richard Li has made headlines as an Asian technology wizard whose career merited comparison with that of Bill Gates.
news.title: Richard Li's Company Removes Web Site Reference to Degree From Stanford : Hong Kong Tycoon's 'Diploma' Disappears

news.abstract: Paleontologists in Africa say 3.5 million-year-old skull they have found is from entirely new branch of early human family tree; discovery threatens to overturn prevailing view that single line of descent stretches through early stages of human ancestry; it now seems that fossil species Australopithecus afarensis, which lived four million to three million years ago and is best known from celebrated Lucy skeleton, was not alone on African plain, and that Lucy may not even be direct human ancestor after all; Dr Maeve G Leakey, who led research team that made new skull discovery in 1999, reports in journal Nature that skull's flattened face and small molars are strikingly different from those of Lucy species; Leakey has named new member of hominid family Kenyanthropus platyops, or flat-faced man of Kenya; photos; chart (M)
news.title: Skull May Alter Experts' View Of Human Descent's Branches

news.abstract: Chinese government spokesman says Gao Zhan, United States-based sociologist who has been held incommunicado since Feb 11 for unspecified 'activities damaging state security,' has confessed her crimes; refuses to say what she actually confessed to (M)
news.title: China Says U.S. Scholar 'Confessed Her Crimes'

news.abstract: Pres Fidel Castro meets for first time with veterans of Bay of Pigs, doomed invasion of Cuba by anti-Castro forces backed by White House and Central Intelligence Agency 40 years ago; meeting, in Havana, opens three-day conference organized by American historians, scholars and open-government advocates who have helped to force access to secret archives of American, Cuban and other governments; Castro reads with delight from declassified State Dept report from 1959 calling him 'born leader of great personal courage and conviction'; this is first time Cuban exiles who fought Castro's forces at Bay of Pigs have returned to Cuba; CIA's brigade of 1,400 Cuban exiles was crushed by Castro's forces: 114 died and 1,189 were captured; photo; map (M)
news.title: Bay of Pigs Enemies Finally Sit Down Together

news.abstract: Mir space station streaks back to Earth in controlled descent, ending 15 years as orbiting laboratory for Soviet and then Russian science; Russian space agency at Mission Control near Moscow handles descent with remarkable precision; witnesses on Fiji report spectacular display of gold and silver lights streaming across sky as Mir crashes into ocean about 1,800 miles east of New Zealand; efforts to save Mir by turning it into movie set, tourist lodge or venue for television series came too late; photo (M)
news.title: Mir Space Station Sizzles to Ending Over Pacific

news.abstract: Top European Union officials urge Macedonian government to exercise restraint against ethnic Albanian militants and to step up discussions with elected Albanian politicians about political change; in response, Macedonian government appears to pull back from vow to 'neutralize the armed terrorists' before serious political discussions; photo (M)
news.title: Europe Union Asks Restraint By Macedonia

news.abstract: Russian government denounces expulsion of about 50 of its diplomats from United States as 'hostile' act and vows 'adequate' retaliation; Foreign Min Igor S Ivanov makes clear that equal number of Americans will soon be expelled from Russia; expulsions, exchanges and threats revive cold war tone that has been largely absent between Washington and Moscow since Soviet Union disintegrated in 1991, and signals marked departure by Bush administration from Pres Clinton's policies of engagement with Russia; American officials say four Russians ordered out immediately had been involved in handling Robert Philip Hanssen, FBI agent who has been charged with spying for Moscow for many years; say other 46 are Russian intelligence officers; say Washington station chief of Russian intelligence service has not been expelled because he operates openly and was not directly involved in Hanssen case; photo; chart outlining fallout after previous spy scandals (M)
news.title: Russia Calls Expulsions by U.S. Hostile Act and Vows to Retaliate

news.abstract: American and Chinese offici
news.title: Defection of Senior Chinese Officer Is Confirmed

news.abstract: Forecasts about Britain's foot-and-mouth epidemic worsen alarmingly, casting doubt on Prime Min Tony Blair's carefully nurtured plan to seek re-election in spring; number of affected farms and other sites is now expected to reach 4,000 by June; officials concede having lost control of spread of contagion because of delay between finding virus and slaughtering animals; Blair is reportedly dismayed and furious that true dimensions of crisis were kept from him until March 22; orders creation of two-square-mile 'firebreak cull' killing zones around every infected farm; says time between diagnosis and slaughter has been reduced to maximum of 24 hours; photos of cows being killed and heaped on pyre (M)
news.title: LIVESTOCK EPIDEMIC WIDENS ITS MENACE FOR BRITISH FARMS

news.abstract: Chinese police arrest Jin Ruchao and say he 'candidly confessed' to being responsible for explosions that killed more than 100 people in Shijiazhuang and an earlier murder (S)
news.title: Suspect Held in China Bombings

news.abstract: David McTaggart, credited with building Greenpeace in worldwide environmental movement, dies at age 69; photo (M)
news.title: David McTaggart, a Builder of Greenpeace, Dies at 69

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    CANADA: RESIGNATION SOUGHT -- Prompted by the release of new information, opposition leaders accused Prime Minister Jean Chrétien of a conflict of interest and of concealing the truth, and called for him to step aside. The opposition has alleged for months that the prime minister pressured federal officials to approve a $390,000 loan for a failing hotel in which he held a 25 percent stake, though Mr. Chrétien has said that he sold his interest in 1993 before talking to officials. Toronto newspapers have now reported that Mr. Chrétien was listed on ownership records after he took office in November 1993.      Anthony DePalma (NYT)    GUYANA: RULING PARTY WINS -- Guyana's governing party has won a third consecutive term after racially charged elections that prompted accusations of fraud and touched off riots. According to official results, Monday's vote returned to power President Bharrat Jagdeo and  his People's Progressive Party, which is largely backed by Guyanese of East Indian descent.    (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Old enemies from Bay of Pigs invasion in Cuba hold reunion there; photo of former CIA official Robert Reynolds with Alfredo Duran, who was with invading force and went on to become Democratic leader in Florida; Duran, who was expelled from Brigade 2506 Veterans Assn for making trip, says most emotional moment was not meeting Fidel Castro, as he expected it to be, but meeting Cuban soldiers who fought them off (M)
news.title: The Bay of Pigs Revisited, but Arm in Arm

news.abstract: English creeps up as diplomatic language at UN, replacing French; latest edition of UN's blue guide asks 189 UN member nations to list preferred language, and more than 120 choose English (M)
news.title: Diplomatically, French Is a Faded Rose in an English Garden

news.abstract: Argentina legislative leaders hold unusual weekend session to grant extraordinary powers to enable new economy minister, Domingo Cavallo, to cut taxes and labor costs to jump-start economy (M)
news.title: Argentina Presses for Ways to Jolt Its Economy Out of Recession

news.abstract: Three car bombs explode in Russian towns near Chechen border; photo (S)
news.title: Security Heightened as Bombs Kill 20 in 3 Russian Villages

news.abstract: Macedonia uses attack helicopters against ethnic Albanian rebels for first time, firing rockets at their positions above Tetovo (S)
news.title: Macedonia Uses Helicopters Against Rebels for First Time

news.abstract: CARLISLE, England, March 26 - In a sharp escalation of its battle to contain an epidemic of foot and mouth disease, Britain deployed its army today to bury the first of up to half a million carcasses of both infected and healthy sheep in a mass grave the size of a football field on a disused airfield near this northwestern city.
news.title: Britain Deploys the Army in Foot-and-Mouth Battle

news.abstract: Israel's Prime Min Ariel Sharon lashes out at American-sponsored fact-finding committee led by former Sen George J Mitchell, calling inquiry into conflict with Palestinians unjustified; says Israel made 'historic mistake' when it consented to investigation; committee was appointed by former Pres Bill Clinton, with support of Palestinians and previous Israeli government as part of failed cease-fire pact agreed to in October at Sharm el Sheik, Egypt; photos (M)
news.title: Mideast Fact-Finding Panel Angers Sharon

news.abstract: Ellen J Hammer, historian who wrote about Indochina and Vietnam before Vietnam War, dies at age 79 (M)
news.title: Ellen Hammer, 79; Historian Wrote on French in Indochina

news.abstract: Samis, reindeer herders in Kautokeino, Norway, whose traditon of animal husbandry dates back to Ice Age are locked in dispute with government conservationists seeking to regulate reindeer industry to protect wolves and other predators; say government's efforts have hurt business; map; photo (M)
news.title: Kautokeino Journal; Reindeer Herders, at Home on a (Very Cold) Range

news.abstract: South Korea's Pres Kim Dae Jung appoints Han Seung Soo, former ambassador to US during Republican administrations, in effort to improve strained relations with Washington; Han replaces Lee Juong Binn, who resigned after being blamed for series of blunders in dealing with administration on sensitive issue of relations with North Korea; served in Washington between 1986 and 1989; appointment is part of cabinet shakeup as Kim seeks to bolster his sagging popularity (M)
news.title: South Korean Leader Picks Old U.S. Hand as Foreign Minister

news.abstract: UNITED NATIONS, March 27 — Six officials from the World Health Organization and Unicef, and three representatives of Doctors without Borders working on a child vaccination program in Somalia, were taken hostage today by gunmen in Mogadishu, the United Nations spokesman said here.
news.title: 9 Aid Workers Held Hostage After Gunfight by Somalis

news.abstract: Britain deploys army to bury first of up to half million carcasses of infected and healthy sheep in mass grave in Cumbria County in sharp escalation of battle to contain epidemic of foot-and-mouth disease; map; photo (M)
news.title: Trying to Stem Foot-and-Mouth, Britain Buries Carcasses

news.abstract: BEIJING, March 27 — The Chinese government today accused a United States-based sociologist who has been held in isolation for more than six weeks of being a paid spy for "overseas intelligence agencies."
news.title: China Says U.S.-Based Scholar Is Spy for 'Overseas Agencies'

news.abstract: Brazil flexes its economic muscle in trade dispute with US over patents on AIDS drugs, shedding image as easygoing and cordial; is rebutting US case before World Trade Organization which argues that Brazilian law, by forcing foreign companies to provide anti-AIDS drugs at lower prices or licensing Brazilian companies to do so in event of health emergency, violates international trade rules; says it will win not only by legal arguments and requirements of intellectual property law, but by moral dimensions of its case; runs highly successful program to fight AIDS, in part because of ability to provide drugs at prices below those charged by major pharmaceutical companies (M)
news.title: Brazil Flexes New Muscle In Another Trade Fight

news.abstract: Flames erupt in packed dormitory of secondary school in Machakos, Kenya, killing 58 sleeping schoolboys; authorities say blaze may have been deliberately set; launch probe; photo (M)
news.title: 58 Youths Die in Kenyan Dormitory Fire

news.abstract: MOSCOW, March 28 — President Vladimir V. Putin replaced his defense and interior ministers today and fired the atomic energy chief in the most extensive set of personnel changes in his year-old government. He also emphasized that he was putting civilians in key posts "as a step towards the demilitarization of society in Russia."
news.title: Putin, in Big Shakeup, Fires Aides and Brings In Civilians

news.abstract: LIPKOVO, Macedonia, Mar. 27 — Macedonian security forces launched another operation today against ethnic Albanian rebels, this time in northern Macedonia close to the border with Kosovo, in a last effort to rout the guerrillas before political talks begin.
news.title: Macedonia Attempts to Rout Rebels Before Talks

news.abstract: UNITED NATIONS, March 28 — The Bush administration cast its first veto in the Security Council late Tuesday night, ending a weeklong marathon debate and decisively scuttling Palestinian hopes for a United Nations observer force in the Israeli-occupied territories in the foreseeable future.
news.title: U.S. Vetoes Pro-Palestinian U.N. Resolution

news.abstract: EUROPE    UKRAINE: LEADING OPPONENT FREED -- A judge freed the former deputy prime minister, Yulia V. Tymoshenko, from jail. A leading opponent of President Leonid Kuchma, Ms. Tymoshenko was detained in February on corruption charges, which she asserts were politically motivated, after she led an effort to bring order to Ukraine's notoriously corrupt energy sector. Judge Mykola Zamkovenko overturned an arrest warrant issued by the general prosecutor, though criminal proceedings are still pending.      Patrick E. Tyler (NYT)    GERMANY: NUCLEAR SHIPMENT -- The German police said they had detained more than 400 people in protests over a shipment of nuclear waste from France to an underground storage site in central Germany. Anti-nuclear activists tried to halt an armored train carrying six containers of waste to the bunker in Gorleben. The police removed about 1,000 people who staged a sit-down on a main railroad near Lüneburg.      Victor Homola (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Chinese government, in attempt to quell fears and rumors about series of explosions in Shijiazhuang two weeks ago that killed more than 100 people, publishes detailed account of how it says one disgruntled man carried out bombings; Jin Ruchao was arrested last week, but until now police had released little information about investigation, prompting widespread skepticism over whether they had caught real culprit (M)
news.title: Beijing Publishes Detailed Account of Bombings

news.abstract: Macedonian security forces mount another operation against ethnic Albanian rebels in last effort to rout guerrillas before political talks begin; government says it has successfully driven back rebels from area around Tetovo and now has only few villages in north to deal with; latest bombardment angers Albanians; Albanian political parties are making same demands as rebels, namely revisions in constitution and equal rights for Albanians in education, employment and use of their own language; photo (M)
news.title: Before Talks, Macedonia Tries to Keep Albanian Rebels in Check

news.abstract: SKOPJE, Macedonia, March 29 — Fighting between Macedonian security forces and ethnic Albanian rebels in the north spilled over the border into Kosovo today, killing three people and wounding 16.
news.title: Fighting Spills Into Kosovo, Killing 3 and Wounding 16

news.abstract: Bush administration begins comprehensive review of all American aid programs to Russia set up to stop spread of nuclear, biological and chemical weapons; Washington now spends more than $760 million a year trying to dismantle former Soviet nuclear, biological and chemical complexes and prevent unconventional weapons and hazardous materials from being sold to rogue states and terrorist groups or stolen by them; senior official says several programs seem 'very effective,' but others are not; cites $6 billion longterm effort to help dispose of 34 metric tons of weapons-grade plutonium as money not well spent; review comes at time of growing tension between Russia and United States; Russian officials accuse Washington of being intent on reviving cold war (M)
news.title: U.S. REVIEWING AID MEANT TO CONTAIN RUSSIA'S ARSENAL

news.abstract: American investigators studying crash of Egyptair jet in 1999 say they are looking into control problem with same model plane that occurred Mar 27 as it approached Paris; it involved American Airlines Boeing 767, which landed with no injuries (S)
news.title: A New Theory In Egyptair Crash

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  As the parade of layoff announcements from industrial companies around the world grew on Wednesday, economists and investors questioned the optimism of American consumers that brightened the stock market just 24 hours earlier.
news.title: Layoffs Cast Doubt on Burst of U.S. Confidence

news.abstract: UNITED NATIONS    MEASLES KILLS 900,000 -- More than 30 million children still get measles every year and 900,000 die, accounting for more than half the 1.6 million childhood deaths that could be prevented with vaccinations, said the World Health Organization and Unicef. The agencies hope to halve the deaths by 2005 by giving all infants at least one dose of vaccine. Immunizing a child costs 26 cents.       Barbara Crossette (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Pres Bush, speaking at second news conference of his presidency, makes most expansive statements on Middle East since assuming office; says Palestinian leader, Yasir Arafat, should hear 'loud and clear' that United States wants him to 'stop the violence'; Bush urges Israel to exercise restraint in its military actions but reserves most pointed language for Arafat; Bush says he has instructed Secretary of State Colin L Powell to call Arafat to reiterate his message on halting violence; administration officials say strong words about Arafat and renewed frustration with him stem in part from his demands for vote on Security Council resolution seeking United Nations observer force in Israeli occupied territories; United States vetoed move; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Hammers Arafat; Takes a Softer Tone With Israel

news.abstract: John R Bolton, nominee for under secretary of state for arms control and international security at State Dept, tries to explain at his confirmation hearing his seeming about-face on test-ban treaty; he previously characterized supporters of treaty as 'misguided'; now he says he would examine elements of treaty as part of overall strategic review (S)
news.title: Arms Control Nominee Defends Shifting View

news.abstract: SAKHNIN, Israel, March 30 — In the Israeli-Arab community, life is divided into before and after last October, when Israeli police shot dead 13 Israeli Arabs during tense, raucous demonstrations. For many, hope died then that Israeli Arabs would ever be accepted as full citizens of Israel with equal status and rights.
news.title: 10,000 Israeli Arabs Protest in Sympathy With Palestinians

news.abstract: Helge Ingstad, Norwegian writer and adventurer who followed hunch and ancient map to identify place where Vikings landed in North America 500 years before Columbus, dies at age 101; photo (M)
news.title: Helge Ingstad, Discoverer of Viking Site, Is Dead at 101

news.abstract: CANNES—  Judit Polgar, the strongest woman chess player ever, was one move away from checkmating Christian Bauer, a French grandmaster. He resigned.
news.title: To Men, Losing to Judit Polgar Is No Disgrace : Tigress of the Chessboard Purrs Quietly and Pounces

news.abstract: european union takes step toward ties with pyongyangÿ
news.title: European Union Takes Step Toward Ties With Pyongyang

news.abstract: Narino Province, Colombia, Gov Parmenio Cuellar reports some 200 to 300 right-wing paramilitary group raiders marched into Llorente, herded residents into plaza and seized 30 people it accused of collaborating with leftist guerrillas; says 30 are now presumed dead; says security forced did not arrive until five days later; he and human rights officials see raid linked to extensive American-backed fumigation of coca fields in neighboring Putumayo Province, which has displaced coca growers, rebels and paramilitary gunmen to once quiet Llorente region (M)
news.title: 30 Villagers Presumed Dead After Paramilitary Raid in Colombia

news.abstract: Beaver, North America's largest rodent and Canada's national symbol, has also become major pest; population has exploded in Manitoba as antifur movement has depressed demand and prices for pelts; animals' dam-building floods farms and golf courses, blocks streets and railroads and drops trees on power lines and cottages; province now pays bounty for beaver tails; map; photo (M)
news.title: Portage la Prairie Journal; Beavers' Dual Role: National Icon and Huge Pest

news.abstract: Chinese security agents detained a Chinese-born American last month as he crossed the border from Hong Kong, where he works as a business professor, the American Embassy confirmed. The unexplained detention of Li Shaomin, a naturalized citizen, follows several other incidents in which Chinese-born scholars with United States ties have been held on vague security grounds.      Article, Page A7.
news.title: China Holds American

news.abstract: British, whose love of red meat is part of national character, are shunning meat because of outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease even though malady does not harm people who eat it M)
news.title: In a Crisis, Vegetables, Not Beef, For British

news.abstract: Confidential review by US naval officers concludes that Taiwan needs significant infusion of new weapons, including sophisticated ship-borne radar system China does not want it to have; China's bitter opposition to sale of sophisticated weapons, which it fears will lead to new degree of cooperation between Taiwan and US and buttress island's pro-independence sentiment, discussed; three types of weapons systems it finds particularly objectionable noted; pending decision on whether to sell arms is one of first major foreign policy tests for Bush administration; could set tone for US-China relations for foreseeable future; has caused rift among America's China hands, including those in Republican Party, putting pressure on Bush from both sides; some policy experts say it would be foolish to pick diplomatic fight with Beijing before administration has had chance to begin dialogue with leadership; pro-Taiwan conservatives insist US has moral obligation to safeguard Taiwan from threats from Communist government in Beijing; photos; map (M)
news.title: SECRET U.S. STUDY CONCLUDES TAIWAN NEEDS NEW ARMS

news.abstract: Rev John Nduati, 27-year-old minister who heads Church of God's Power in Nairobi, Kenya, has attracted large following with claims that he has cured thousands of AIDS sufferers through prayer; former child preacher says he started healing at age 10; claims direct line to God; photos (M)
news.title: In a Preacher's Prayer, An Instant AIDS 'Cure' For Throngs of Kenyans

news.abstract: Pres Bush's abrupt decision to abandon Kyoto Protocol, treaty on global warming, provokes even more than usual level of anger and frustration in Europe; has aggravated mixture of grudges that have gnawed at Europeans for years; Europeans are angry that US appears oblivious to widespread environmental concerns across most of Europe; are frustrated that US, by virtue of size can undermine treaty negotiated by more than 100 countries; are depressed that there is not much they can do about it; US produces about 25 percent of gases associated with global warming, and refusal to meet goals set by Kyoto to reduce greenhouse emissions makes it difficult for competitors to do so (M)
news.title: Bush Angers Europe by Eroding Pact on Warming

news.abstract: Former Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic surrenders to Serbian authorities after defying series of deadlines; gives up after police surround residence in Belgrade suburb, apparently preparing to storm it; is locked up in Belgrade's Central Prison; reportedly threatened to kill himself and family; Serbian and Yugoslav officials say he will be remanded on variety of domestic charges, including abuse of powers, but will not be transferred to Hague to face 1999 indictment on war crimes charges for actions during war in Kosovo; photos (M)
news.title: SERB AUTHORITIES ARREST MILOSEVIC TO END STANDOFF

news.abstract: Computer technicians iron out glitches in luggage system at South Korea's new $5.4 billion Inchon International Airport (S)
news.title: New Airport for Seoul Irons Out Problems

news.abstract: US Navy EP-3E Aries II spy plane on routine surveillance mission over South China Sea near Chinese coast collides with Chinese fighter closely tailing it; makes emergency landing on China's Hainan Island, but Chinese plane crashes into sea; China says US bears total responsibility; US seeks immediate release of 24 crew members, sophisticated aircraft and all intelligence equipment; US diplomats and other American officials in China travel to Hainan to escort crew out of country and ensure that plane is not inspected or tampered with; US military spokesman says Chinese planes have become increasingly aggressive in tailing American military aircraft in recent months, even prompting US to register protest; map; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. PLANE IN CHINA AFTER IT COLLIDES WITH CHINESE JET

news.abstract: Pres Bush praises Yugoslav government for arresting former president Slobodan Milosevic, but cautions that extent of his crimes warrants trial before UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague and not just trial on local charges in Serbia; suggests Yugoslavia has done well enough in meeting conditions that call for coopertation with war crimes tribunal before American economic assistance is released (M)
news.title: Milosevic Should Face Trial By Hague Tribunal, Bush Says

news.abstract: Slobodan Milosevic, former Yugoslav president, is arrested by Serbian police at residence in Belgrade; surrender follows protracted and sometimes dangerous negotiations; reportedly threatened to kill wife, daughter and himself; surrenders after assurances that he would get fair trial and that arrest was not pretext for transfer to the Hague to face trial as war criminal; is charged mainly with corruption and abuse of power for alleged financial misdealings that caused damage to economy and brought instability to country during period of hyperinflation in early 1990's; is ordered detained in Belgrade's Central Prison for 30 days while charges are investigated; photos (M)
news.title: MILOSEVIC ARREST CAME WITH PLEDGE FOR A FAIR TRIAL

news.abstract: BELGRADE, Serbia, April 2 — President Vojislav Kostunica of Yugoslavia said today that his country should not extradite former President Slobodan Milosevic to The Hague to face war-crimes charges, even if the United States again threatens to withhold foreign aid.
news.title: Yugoslav Firm on His Stand to Bar Milosevic From Hague

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, April 2 — President Bush demanded today "the prompt and safe return" of the crew members and the American spy plane that made an emergency landing in China on Sunday, and he warned that China's continued silence about when the fliers would be returned could harm relations between the two countries.
news.title: Bush Demands 'Prompt' Return of Plane and Crew

news.abstract: Two American Embassy officials arrive in Sanya, China, but are denied access to crew of surveillance plane that made emergency landing at military base on Hainan after collision with Chinese fighter over South China Sea; US officials warn further delays in sending crew home and returning plane could damage already fragile relations; incident has cast cold war pall over China's dealings with Bush administration; photo (M)
news.title: American Embassy Officials Waiting to See Plane's Crew

news.abstract: Families of crew members of US Navy spy plane that made emergency landing in China after collision with Chinese fighter over South China Sea anxiously await word about loved ones; many are impatient with slow flow of information from military; photo (M)
news.title: A Frustrating Wait for Crew Members' Anxious Relatives

news.abstract: TOKYO, April 3 — At their simplest, the early reactions to the collision between an American aircraft and a Chinese one off the coast of southern China on Sunday have highlighted the lines of alliance in this diplomatically complex part of the world.
news.title: Asian Reaction to Collison Is Mixed, but Predictable

news.abstract: Interview with Yugoslav Pres Vojislav Kostunica, who says former Pres Slobodan Milosevic should not be extradited to The Hague to face war-crimes charges, even if US again threatens to withhold foreign aid; says Milosevic's extradition should never happen; accuses war crimes tribunal of being political, practicing selective justice, following shaky rules of law and of being biased against Serbia; says Yugoslavia will investigate war crimes and help The Hague to do so; says Milosevic should be brought to trial for war crimes, but before domestic court; photo (M)
news.title: Yugoslav Chief Says Milosevic Shouldn't Be Sent to Hague

news.abstract: Families of crew of Navy plane held in China anxiously await news; they and other residents of Whidbey Island, Washington, where plane is based, have tied yellow ribbons on trees and other objects; family members comment; photos of crew members (M)
news.title: Coping With Waiting And Sketchy Details

news.abstract: Bosnia holds former Pres Slobodan Milosevic's admission, in his bid for release from Serbian custody, that he channeled state funds to Serbian forces fighting wars in Croatia and Bosnia in the 1990's should resolve any doubts about Yugoslavia's role in atrocities of those wars; Belgrade court rejects bid, ordering him held pending probe of alleged corruption and abuse of power; Yugoslav Pres Vojislav Kostunica insists Milosevic be tried in Serbia on all charges, including war crimes, news conference; questions justice of war crimes tribunal in The Hague; photo (M)
news.title: Admissions by Milosevic Should Speed His Trial, Bosnia Says

news.abstract: Former guerrillas who fought in El Salvador's civil war have used organizational skills honed in conflict to respond quickly and capably to devastation caused by two recent earthquakes; are in competition of sorts with conservative governing parties, with both sides aware that their actions will have impact in next election; scene in Santa Tecla described; map; photo (M)
news.title: Santa Tecla Journal; Shovels Are Easier Than Rifles, Ex-Guerrilla Says

news.abstract: Chinese spokesman blames United States for midair collision of spy plane and one of two Chinese fighter jets trailing plane, news conference; suggests release of 24 American crew members detained on Hainan Island after plane's emergency landing hinges on US's willingness to apologize; Chinese rescuers have been unable to find pilot of downed jet, Wang Wei; Pres Jiang Zemin holds China has evidence that US plane caused collision by violating standard flight rules; calls on US to end frequent reconnaisance flights along China's coast; Amb Joseph W Prueher says US would have 'problem' with apologizing; map; photos (M)
news.title: CHINA FAULTS U.S. IN INCIDENT; SUGGESTS RELEASE OF CREW HINGES ON OFFICIAL APOLOGY

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, April 4 — The United States expressed regret today over the presumed death of a Chinese pilot in his fighter's collision with an American airplane on Sunday. But that regret did not include a formal apology.
news.title: U.S. Offers China 'Regrets,' but Stops Short of Apology

news.abstract: Pres Bush has delayed sending to Senate nomination for next United States ambassador to Russia as his administration continues to debate whether to pursue harder line with Pres Vladimir V Putin; Secretary of State Colin L Powell, in first weeks of administration, recommended appointment of Alexander Vershbow, current US representative to NATO; delay in making decision on Vershbow may reflect decision to downgrade Russia's status in administration's foreign policy calculations (M)
news.title: An Envoy Waits as Russia Policy Is Pondered

news.abstract: ROME, April 5 - Saying they had struck a ``nerve center'' of Islamic terrorism in Europe, Italian officials announced the arrest today of five North African men suspected of having ties to the Saudi exile Osama bin Laden. They added that they were searching for five others.
news.title: Italy Arrests 5 North Africans Suspected of Bin Laden Ties

news.abstract: BEIJING, April 5 — The United States took "a step in the right direction" with Secretary of State Colin L. Powell's expressions of regret for the collision of an American spy plane and a Chinese fighter jet, a Chinese spokesman said today.
news.title: Bush Says China Must Release U.S. Crew

news.abstract: Lori Berenson, 31-year-old New Yorker, is on trial in Lima, Peru, on charges of involvement in terorrist plot to take Peruvian Congress hostage; Peruvian press portrays her as member of Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement, while her parents call entire process a charade; unlike her first trial, which was conducted in secret antiterrorism court, second trial is being conducted in civilian courtroom and televised live on cable channel; second trial was ordered after years of American pressure on Peru; Berenson's lawyer claims she was duped by terrorists to help their cause; Berenson claims she never knew she was living among Tupac Amaru leaders, whom she knew by assumed names; photo (M)
news.title: American Tells Peru Court She Lacked Details on Rebels

news.abstract: China hardens its position on midair collision of American spy plane and Chinese jet, with Pres Jiang Zemin demanding official apology and Chinese Foreign Min Tang Jiaxuan calling United States 'arrogant'; Tang also accuses US of making 'groundless accusations' against China; escalating war of words seen reflecting widespread feeling in China, in and out of government, that Pres Bush has been dismissive of China's concerns ever since incident occurred; despite heated atmosphere, it still appears that both governments hope to minimize long-term fallout of event; Secretary of State Colin L Powell issues statement of regret over loss of Chinese pilot, although US continues to insist it will not apologize for incident; Bush and other American officials demand that 24 Americans on board be returned promptly; photos (M)
news.title: BEIJING STEPS UP ITS WAR OF WORDS OVER AIR COLLISION

news.abstract: Ecologists report troubling trend in Wolong Nature Reserve, China's largest and most heralded sanctuary for endangered giant pandas; say prime panda forest habitat is disappearing more than four times as fast as it was before reserve was established in 1975 because of soaring human population in region; map (M)
news.title: Human Competition Edging Out Those Lovable Icons of Wildlife

news.abstract: WILL the W hotels look impossibly dated in 10 or 20 years? Who will take the place of the Four Seasons' loyal but aging clientele? Will travelers really want to check into their rooms with their Palm Pilots?
news.title: Future Face of Hotels:Industry Looks for Right Formula

news.abstract: From Ramesh Thakur in Tokyo:
news.title: ASK ROGER COLLIS : 'Delayed Baggage' Cover

news.abstract: American ambassador, Adm Joseph W Prueher, meets with China's foreign minister in latest in series of negotiations aimed at securing release of 24 crew members of American spy plane; United States diplomats in China say American representatives would be allowed to have second meeting with crew members, who are being held incommunicado on Hainan Island, as two governments search for face-saving compromise over China's demand for open American apology (M)
news.title: U.S. Envoy Meets Chinese Foreign Minister as Negotations on Plane's Crew Continue

news.abstract: Palm trees and manicured gardens filled with bougainvillea line Doha's Corniche along one of the most beautiful bays in the Arabian Gulf. Residents of Qatar's capital meet on this superbly landscaped Corniche to jog, walk or just to relax while watching dhows, motorboats, sailboats and jet skis on the sparkling blue waters.
news.title: CITY GUIDE:Doha : Of Souks and Malls

news.abstract: Britain is having worse run of bad luck than usual lately--combination of natural disasters and human bungling that has left many subject to malaise as they wonder what dreadful thing might befall them next; weather has been hideous, troubled rail system has led to derailments, and country has been forced to slaughter its farm animals to fight foot-and-mouth epidemic; photos (M)
news.title: London Journal; Soggy Pastures Where All Things Crash and Burn

news.abstract: American government officials meet with detained crew members of downed United States surveillance aircraft on Hainan island in southern China and are expected to meet with them again shortly; Amerian officials report men and women are being treated well and are eating meals brought in from restaurant; say crew is in great spirits (M)
news.title: U.S. Envoy Meets the 24 And Reports 'Great Spirits'

news.abstract: Several American experts say extracting apology, or confession, has long been favorite technique of Chinese Communists in dealing with anyone seen as adversary, especially when person is in custody; say that in current situation, involving American military suveillance plane, Americans should not provoke more suspicious and anti-Western groups within regime (M)
news.title: China's Demand for Apology Is Rooted in Tradition

news.abstract: Lennart Meri, Estonia's only president since tiny country became independent from Soviet Union in 1991, will retire in August; he leaves behind country in such good shape that it is sometimes ranked ahead of other former Eastern Bloc countries as early candidate for entry into European Union; Estonia has more foreign investment per capital than any other former Eastern Bloc country, and its average wage is triple that of neighboring countries; Meri has pushed relentlessly for open markets and clean government; photo; map (M)
news.title: Estonia's President: Un-Soviet and Unconventional

news.abstract: Israeli policy of razing homes of Palestinians stokes bitterness among ordinary Palestinians who have lost houses and property; many consider it another tactic to put down six-month-old Palestinians uprising; Israeli officials claim they are enforcing law against accumulated backlog of offenders who have built in defiance of building restrictions and court orders; Palestinians and human rights advocates contend that restrictive Israeli zoning policies givePalestinian communiities no room to expand, forcing residents to build illegally for their growing families; total of 30 demolitions in West Bank areas under Israeli control have been carried out this week (M)
news.title: Israeli Policy of Razing Homes Draws Protests by Palestinians

news.abstract: Peruvians to vote for new president just year after election so clumsily fraudulent that winner, Alberto Fujimori, finally had to leave country and resign; Alejandro Toledo is likely to get most votes but not enough to avoid runoff, so that real race is between left-wing former president Alan Garcia and moderate conservative Lourdes Flores; photos (M)
news.title: In a Colorful Campaign in Peru, 3 Points of View Emerge

news.abstract: China insists in strongly worded statement that United States has not done enough to end crisis over 24 Americans detained after their spy plane made emergency landing nearly week ago; negotiations to find way out of crisis continue; official propaganda in China both reflects popular anger and keeps it ratcheted high; China asserts that collision was 'entirely caused' by US side, and that US should apologize; photo; maps (L)
news.title: CHINESE INSISTING U.S. MUST DO MORE TO END STANDOFF

news.abstract: Fossils of what may be earliest known ancestor of human family are unearthed in Kenya by Dr Martin Pickford and Dr Brigittte Senut; photos; bones and teeth are about 6 million years old, at least 1.5 million years earlier than similar finds; French discoverers say individual walked mostly upright and was direct ancestor of modern humans, claim rejected by skeptics who believe fossils likely are of chimpanzee of chimp ancestor; growing controversy may be fueled by personal animosity involving Pickford, whose enemies in profession include Richard Leakey; other paleontologists react (M)
news.title: On the Trail of a Few More Ancestors

news.abstract: Bush administration, which has made no significant breaks with recent US human rights policies, is nevertheless finding it difficult to count on support of traditional European allies as UN carries out annual review of rights polices around world; rights groups point to divisions that emerged during Clinton administration over US reluctance to actively back treaties on land mines and International Criminal Court, which US signed at last moment; Europeans perception that Pres Bush has brought back cold war also cited (M)
news.title: U.S. Finding Alliances On Rights Are Tangled

news.abstract: SEOUL, South Korea, April 7 — North Korea announced financial measures this week that place top priority on improving living standards but emphasize the primacy of the armed forces.
news.title: North Korea Gives Priority to Military

news.abstract: Recovery teams remove bodies from crash of helicopter searching for remains of American soldiers missing from Vietnam War; helicopter crashed into mountainside in Thanh Trach, in central Vietnam, on Apr 7, killing all seven Americans and nine Vietnamese aboard; helicopter was part of major cooperative search operation throughout Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and southern China that has been under way since 1985 for missing American servicemen; photo (M)
news.title: Bodies of 16 Recovered From Crash In Vietnam

news.abstract: Striking a slightly stiffer tone, the Bush administration warned China that its relationship with the United States was being hurt and that it risked further harm with every day that the crew of an American spy plane remained in detention.    Senior American officials went out of their way to reject the kind of apology China has demanded for the collision between the American plane and a Chinese fighter jet.
news.title: Tougher U.S. Tone On Spy Plane Crisis

news.abstract: Russia is expected to lead drive to persuade Security Council to impose sanctions on Pakistan, strongest supporter of Afghanistan's militant Islamic government, Taliban; this has potential to place Bush administration in quandary; Washington considers Pakistan an ally, and there are recent signs that Pakistan is having doubts about its support of Taliban, as Taliban becomes heroes to radical Islamic forces within Pakistan; Bush administration has given no indication of how it will deal with Afghanistan (M)
news.title: Russia Seeks Sanctions Against Pakistan for Aid to Taliban

news.abstract: Latest embarrassment for Britain's House of Windsor involves Sophie Rhys-Jones, Countess of Wessex, public relations executive who married Prince Edward, youngest son of Queen Elizabeth II, two years ago; Britain's best-selling paper, News of the World, publishes clandestinely taped interviews with her and her business partner in which she speaks indiscreetly of her misgivings about British politicians and other members of royal family; partner talks of his drug use and of arranging sex tourism and setting up trysts for clients with groups of young gay men; Sophie announces her resignation from her company; voices regret for her own misjudgment in succumbing to what she terms entrapment operation; photo (M)
news.title: A New Royal Blush in Britain's Press

news.abstract: E.ON, large Germany utility, is close to agreement to buy Powergen, British gas and electricity supplier, for $7.4 billion; Powergen assets include seven generators in Britain and LG&E Energy Corp in Louisville, Ky; acquisition would give E.ON foothold in both British and United States electricity markets at time of rapid consolidation and comes as other large European utility companies seek acquisitions abroad to help offset fierce competition at home; deal is subject to regulatory approval in US and Europe (M)
news.title: German Utility Close to a Deal For Powergen

news.abstract: Construction of six-mile security barrier for 34-nation Summit of the Americas, which will weigh formation of hemispheric free trade area, stirs controversy in Quebec; police hold city's layout makes barrier necessary to separate anti-globalization protesters from delegates and ensure delegates' safe passage into and out of meeting site; photo (M)
news.title: Quebec Journal; A Chain-Link Fence Rankles an Old Walled City

news.abstract: Court hearing on corruption charges brought before his election is going badly for Thai Prime Min Thaksin Shinawatra; his possible downfall would deepen political instability in nation still not recovered from economic slump (M)
news.title: Corruption Case Against Thailand's Leader Tests Rule of Law

news.abstract: Bush administration officials say Pres Bush's senior advisers believe that threats of severe retaliation in spy-plane standoff with China would not speed release of American crew members and could harm longer-term interests; say review of options makes clear how little room either side has for maneuver in interdependent and complex relationship; say conservatives in Congress increasingly press for stronger action, while business executives warn against trade sanctions; Bush issues only briefest of comments on delay in freeing crew (M)
news.title: U.S. Shies Away From Threats In Plane Standoff With China

news.abstract: PARIS—  Anyone wondering where U.S. military investment is headed need look no farther than the next generation of spy satellites that are being built now and will start going into orbit in 2005.
news.title: Spying From Space:U.S. to Sharpen the Focus

news.abstract: Brig Gen Neal Sealock again meets with 24 crew members of downed United States spy plane, Hainan Island, China; says they are kept in air-conditioned, 'hotel-like' environment and are in good spirits; brings them e-mail from family and friends; photo (M)
news.title: New Woe For Crew: Boredom

news.abstract: Czech finance minister, Pavel Mertlik, abruptly resigns after losing numerous political battles over plans to privatize and clean up state companies left from Communist era; resignation of Mertlik, who pushed through bank privatization and fought demands to pump government money into bankrupt industrial conglomerates, suggests that economic reform has hit wall (M)
news.title: Czech Resigns After Failure Of Efforts To Privatize

news.abstract: Chinese state news media hints at progress toward resolution of impasse over American spy plane and its crew, now detained on Hainan Island; prominently publicizes Sec Colin Powell's use of word 'sorry' during television comment on midair collision with Chinese fighter jet (S)
news.title: In a Hint of Progress, State News Media Cite Powell's 'Sorry'

news.abstract: Mexico asks wary US to share more intelligence and ideas for fighting criminal organizations on both sides of border; Adolfo Aguilar Zinser, security adviser to Pres Vicente Fox, will meet with Atty Gen John Ashcroft, security adviser Condoleezza Rice and FBI, DEA, State Department and Pentagon officials in Washington (M)
news.title: Mexico Seeks Closer Law Enforcement Ties With Wary U.S.

news.abstract: US sends China formal statement of regret over midair collision between US intelligence plane and Chinese fighter jet, and awaits China's reponse on accepting letter and releasing American crew; statement, after six days of talks and exchanges of drafts, amplifies Sec Colin Powell's initial expression of being sorry about loss of Chinese pilot and emergency landing of US plane on Hainan island; photo; Bush administration official insists 'there is no apology'; statement also proposes joint investigation and talks on avoiding future incidents; Pres Jiang Zemin, in Uruguay, says he trusts in ability of both countries to resolve issue; Bush for first time calls situation 'stalemate,' warning that diplomacy takes longer than people would like; Powell has acknowledged that plane violated Chinese airspace in its landing, but not at time of collision, which US says occurred in international airspace (M)
news.title: U.S. SENDS BEIJING FORMAL STATEMENT EXPRESSING REGRET

news.abstract: TOKYO—  Their heroes are athletes and actors, comedians and television personalities. They tell pollsters they dislike math and science and that they aspire to become beauticians and video game creators. Many color their hair blond and orange and change their jobs frequently, more often than their parents in a lifetime.
news.title: Work Hard?Young Japanese Have Other Ideas

news.abstract: Level of violence in 17-year-old ethnic conflict between Sri Lankan government and Tamil separatist rebels drops sharply over last three months; there are signs that warring parties are moving toward resuming peace talks that broke off six years ago; relative calm comes after gruesome year in one of world's most brutal wars; more than 8,000 troops have died in last six years; rebels say 133 of their fighters have been killed since they declared unilateral ceasefire in December (M)
news.title: Separatist Battles Ebb in Sri Lanka and Hope for Peace Talks Is in the Air

news.abstract: Ile-Alatau National Park near Almaty, Kazakhstan, is little changed in 2,500 years since first nomadic tribes moved through, and chief scientist for park is determined to keep it that way; park is one of 32 nature preserves that were spared nuclear testing, exploitation of recources and general environmental insensitivity of Soviet era; it now faces neglect and desperation bred of poverty; poaching and small-scale logging have become matters of survival for many people in Central Asia; photos; map (M)
news.title: Ile-Alatau Journal; Pristine Park Draws More Poachers Than Tourists

news.abstract: In and around Kansas City, Mo, anger at China seems to evaporate quickly after agreement to release 24 Americans; nature of American apology is subject of some debate, but most people feel Pres Bush and China settled on suitable compromise; photos (M)
news.title: A Readiness to Let Bygones Be Bygones

news.abstract: Cardinal Karl Lehmann, chairman of conference of Germany's Roman Catholic bishops, accuses Netherlands of adopting 'culture of death' by becoming first country to legalize mercy killing and assisted suicide; Lehmann's vehement statement forms part of fierce German reaction to euthanasia law approved by Dutch Senate; new Dutch law formalizes what has become common practice in Netherlands over many years, in which terminally ill people enduring 'lasting and unbearable suffering' ask their doctor to die; German doctors seem unanimous in seeing sinister trends behind Dutch law (M)
news.title: Horror Expressed in Germany Over Dutch Euthanasia

news.abstract: Analysis of what China got out of its latest run-in with United States; says Chinese government acquired secrets from downed American spy plane as well as attention and some respect from new Bush administration; notes that Bush administration initially paid so little heed to China that it had no high-level China experts in its ranks at time of incident, which proved to be handicap when 24 Americans were detained on Chinese soil; says Bush is now calling for 'fruitful and productive relationship' with China (M)
news.title: China's Bonus: Attention, and Respect

news.abstract: Two children are among 43 people killed in stampede of soccer fans in stadium in Johannesburg, South Africa; shaken relatives arrive at municipal morgue to identify bodies; along with dead, 160 people are injured in stampede, and 18 remain hospitalized; catastrophe is worst sporting accident in country's history, and it leaves nation in mourning during holiest week in Christian calendar; Pres Thabo Mbeki impanels judicial commission of inquiry to explore what happened; circumstances surrounding ticket sales--short advance sales period and fact that sales were largely limited to stadium box office--appear likely to form crucial line of inquiry; photo (M)
news.title: The Simple Things That Underlie a Soccer Stampede

news.abstract: Pavel P Borodin, former Russian aide who was accused of pocketing and laundering millions of dollars in kickbacks from Swiss companies that renovated Kremlin, is freed by Swiss court after judges there realize that without cooperation from Russia, there is little likelihood of proving his guilt; Russia pays Borodin's $2.9 million bail, clearing way for his return to Russia; photo (M)
news.title: Extradited Russian Suddenly Free After 3-Year Inquiry

news.abstract: Pacifico Castrellon testifies for prosecution in Peru trial of Lori Berenson, American woman jailed for alleged involvement with Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement; Castrellon, who hopes to have his own sentence reduced in retrial, describes Berenson as go-between for Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, top Tupac Amaru military commander; describes himself as innocent man duped by terrorists, unaware of their plot to attack Congress; Berenson's lawyer is expected to question him about fact that rebels rented him apartment where he drew detailed street maps for them of area around Congress (M)
news.title: In Peru Trial, Ex-Associate Contradicts New Yorker

news.abstract: HONOLULU, April 12 — The 24 crew members of the American surveillance plane held in China landed today at Hickam Air Force Base, part of the Pearl Harbor military complex, and were given a deliberately low-key heroes' welcome.
news.title: A Quick Heroes' Welcome, Then On to Long Hours With Debriefing Teams

news.abstract: Text of Pres Bush's statement on return of service personnel from China; photo (M)
news.title: Bush on China: 'Different Values, Common Interests'
