news.title: Jesse Jackson Says He Might Go to Taliban to Seek Turnaround

news.abstract: German parliament approves sending 600 troops to lead NATO peace mission to Macedonia (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Macedonia Mission Is Approved

news.abstract: King Mswati III of Swaziland orders young women to stop having sex for next five years to prevent AIDS, which has infected at least 25 percent of adults in country; girls are to wear hair tassels signifying celibacy; photo; girls at one high school says they will look like 'social idiots' (M)
news.title: To Fight AIDS, Swaziland's King Orders Girls to Avoid Sex for 5 Years

news.abstract: China releases Wu Jianmin, Chinese-born US citizen and freelance journalist who has been held for almost six months on spy charges; recent high-profile detentions have hindered Chinese effort to improve US relations; US citizens Fuming Fong and Liu Yaping are still being held (S)
news.title: China Frees U.S. Citizen Held Since April on Spy Charges

news.abstract: UN Security Council unanimously adopts US-sponsored resolution obliging all 189 member countries to crack down on financing, training and movement of terrorists, and to cooperate in any campaign against them, including use of force; Amb John D Negroponte says US is very encouraged by rapid, unanimous action on agreement that reflects broad support for crackdown (M)
news.title: U.N. Requires Members to Act Against Terror

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  When Maurizio Bacci, a photographer who normally focuses on fashion, rushed to the ruins of the World Trade Center, the pictures he took were published across Italy.
news.title: A N.Y. Home:City Inspires Italian Photographers

news.abstract: New markets in Central and Eastern Europe usurp Warsaw's role as shopping center for Russians; Asian producers, selling through Poland's sizable Vietnamese community, have undercut Poland's sweatshops; many companies now use Warsaw simply as distribution center; huge outdoor market in Warsaw, once magnet for bargain hunters from former Soviet Union, loses much of its business; photos (M)
news.title: Fate of a Polish Bazaar Shows Shifting Patterns of East Europe's Economy

news.abstract: Saudi Arabia supervised urgent evacuation of 24 members of Osama bin Laden's extended family from United States in first days after terror attacks on New York and Washington, fearing that they might be subjected to violence; bin Laden is estranged from his family; Saudi Amb Bandar bin Sultan says one of bin Laden's brothers in US called Saudi Embassy frantically looking for protection; most of bin Laden's relatives in US attend high school and college; Saudi King Fahd sent urgent message to his embassy in Washington ordering that bin Laden children in America be protected; photo (M)
news.title: Fearing Harm, Bin Laden Kin Fled From U.S.

news.abstract: Government commission recommends that Jamaica decriminalize marijuana for personal use while continuing bans on cultivation and trafficking; American officials, local clergy and police object, but Prime Min P J Patterson says he finds some panel recommendations 'persuasive'; marijuana is widely used in Jamaica, even in public; recommendation, if adopted, would in effect reconcile law with reality; international groups for drug law reform say proposal reflects growing trend in Europe and Canada toward easing drug laws (M)
news.title: Panel Urges Legalization Of Marijuana In Jamaica

news.abstract: Analysis of stunning about-face by Chinese Government, which has voiced strong support for new American war on terrorism; China has practical reasons for supporting campaign against violent Islamic fundamentalists; it fears emergence of unrest and terrorism at home, most immediately in largely Muslim frontier province of Xinjiang, where stewing separatist movement has occasionally set off bombs or attacked police; aside from that concern, Chinese leaders see opportunity in current crisis to meet broader goal to forge improvement in overall relations with US and other Western countries; photo of border China shares with Afghanistan, where security has been tightened by China (M)
news.title: China's About-Face: Support for U.S. on Terror

news.abstract: Article describes emerging picture of Al Qaeda, terrorist network spawned by Osama bin Laden; young men get training in weapons, explosives and religious studies and are then sent where they are needed to await further instructions; Jamal Ahmed al-Fadl, early recruit of Osama bin Laden's, has been cooperating with United States authorities and describes inner workings of Al Qaeda's corporate type of structure as well as his training; background of Mohammed Saddiq Odeh, Mohamed Rashed Daoud al-'Owhali and Khalfan Khamis Mohamed, convicted in East Africa embassy bombings, discussed; photo (L)
news.title: Al Qaeda: Sprawling, Hard-to-Spot Web of Terrorists-in-Waiting

news.abstract: THE HAGUE—  With a six-column banner headline on page one, a leading Dutch newspaper reported last week that as a result of the terrorist attacks on the United States more than 60 percent of the Dutch agreed with the idea that Muslim immigrants who supported the attack should be expelled from the Netherlands.
news.title: Dutch Frankness on Immigrants Treads Where Many Nations Fear to Go : Europe's Muslims:A Difficult Debate

news.abstract: In contrast to statement of Prime Min Jean Chretien, Canadians voice support of United States and say Canada should cooperate with US in areas of immigration, security and antiterrorism policies; photo (M)
news.title: Support for U.S. Security Plans Is Quietly Voiced Across Canada

news.abstract: Moon cakes, elaborately decorated small round pastries that are traditional food of mid-autumn festival in China and were once considered delicacy, have in recent years become elaborately packaged seasonal food that is traded back and forth as gift, but rarely actually consumed in more than minute quantities; as range of food available to Chinese people expands, what was once considered rare and delectable treat is now generally avoided as too sugary and lacking freshness and flavor; photo (M)
news.title: Gross! The Inside Story Of China's Festive Cake

news.abstract: American military and intelligence officials discuss with Pakistani government concerns over security of country's nuclear weapons stockpile and its two nuclear plants; discuss improving security and installing new safeguards amid fears that any attacks against terrorists in Afghanistan could boil over into Pakistan, where Afghan sympathizers in military could seize control of nuclear weapons; Pres Pervez Musharraf says nation's nuclear arsenal is safe and that there is no risk of weapons falling into wrong hands; formal limitations on how much assistance US can provide Pakistan because of latter's refusal to sign nonproliferation treaty discussed; US law imposing restrictions on sharing information about nuclear weapons with other countries noted (M)
news.title: U.S. and Pakistan Discuss Nuclear Security

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair says that he has seen incontrovertible evidence linking Osama bin Laden to Sept 11 attacks on America; statement is intended to offset doubt about whether such evidence exists; Gordon Brown, chancellor of exchequer, announces that Britain will take lead in freezing assets in campaign against bin Laden; photo (M)
news.title: Blair Says He's Seen Proof of bin Laden Role

news.abstract: Bibliotheca Alexandrina, modern incarnation of Library of Alexandria, stages temporary opening welcoming residents of once glamorous but now dilapidated port city in Egypt to use building for six weeks while administrators wrestle with long-delayed formal inauguration; director Ismail Serageldin says facility needs at least four additional months of construction work and continues to lack some basics expected of modern library, like Internet connections and computers (M)

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Abrupt End To Royal Tempest

news.title: Arab-Israeli Cease-Fire? The Deaths Are Mounting, Along With the Finger-Pointing

news.abstract: Sense of American unfairness toward Palestinians has eroded support for US fight against terrorism in prosperous, pro-Western Arab states in Persian Gulf where there is widespread revulsion for September 11 attacks and for methods of prime suspect, Osama bin Laden, but where feelings for Palestinians are at least as strong (M)

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Raising Kursk, Racing Winter

news.abstract: Milan Zec, former chief of Yugoslav Navy, and three other former commanders--Miodrag Jokic, Pavle Strugar, Vladimir Kovacevic Zec--are indicted by war crimes tribunal in the Hague for causing unlawful civilian deaths while shelling Croatian port of Dubrovnik during Bosnian war in 1991; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: The Hague: Indictments In Croatia Shelling

news.abstract: Islam practiced in rebel-held northern Afghanistan sets far less rigid restrictions on women than that enforced by Taliban government that controls most of nation; some of strict Muslim dictates also apply in rebel area, but girls are allowed to attend school, women can ride in back of trucks, can shop in market and can work at limited number of professions; photo (M)
news.title: Education Offers Women in Northern Afghanistan a Ray of Hope

news.abstract: Pentagon shapes war plan against terrorists to minimize use of Pakistani bases for strike against Osama bin Laden and Taliban in Afghanistan, fearing extensive deployments could destabilize crucial but volatile ally, one that has tested nuclear weapons; growing anti-American sentiment in region prompts Pentagon to scramble to make new arrangements; Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld leaves for Saudi Arabia, Oman, Egypt and Uzbekistan to discuss using bases; new alliances are linking US to several authoritarian governments that have records of corruption and rights abuses but also fear radical Islamic movements; Rumsfeld points out importance of Uzbekistan's position bordering Afghanistan; US already trains Uzbeks in counterterrorism, drug interdiction and weapons smuggling; US now has more than 300 warplanes on ships and land bases from Indian Ocean to Red Sea; photo of USS Essex (M)
news.title: Pentagon Tries To Avoid Using Pakistan Bases

news.abstract: Mounting tit-for-tap violence continues to impede Pres Bush's efforts to secure long-term Isrsaeli-Palestinian peace; many believe only reluctance of each side to be first to end talks keeps Israelis and Palestinians from scrapping truce; Israeli tanks bombard Beit Lahia, Gaza Strip, while Israeli bulldozers ravage area farmland, in response to fatal attack on Israeli settlement of Alei Sinai; Palestinian snipers fire into crowd of thousands of Jewish worshippers, Hebron; map; photo (M)
news.title: Mideast Cease-Fire: Who Will Be the First to Scrap It?

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld seeks to solidify Saudi support for strike against Osama bin Laden's terrorist network and broader war against terrorism; meets with King Fahd and other Saudi leaders, but insists he is not negotiating access to air bases, which is confirmed by Saudis; precise extent of cooperation is unclear; speculation on whether old disputes linger discussed; photo (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Meets Saudis and Says He's Satisfied With Level of Support

news.title: World Briefing | Africa: South Africa: Top Lawmaker Arrested

news.abstract: Gen Ne Win, former strongman in Burma, is reported to be in very serious condition in hospital in Singapore (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia/Pacific: Myanmar: Former Leader Failing

news.abstract: Russian airliner carrying 76 people traveling from Tel Aviv to Siberia explodes and plunges into Black Sea off Russian coast; all 64 passengers and 12 crew members of Siberian Airlines jet are presumed dead; Pres Vladimir V Putin, who has thrown Russian support behind United States campaign against terrorism, says disaster may have been work of terrorists, conclusion quickly echoed by Russian intelligence officials; but there are suggesstions from American officials that crash could have been caused by antiaircraft missiles fired by Ukrainian military forces who were conducting training exercises, with Russian help, off Crimean peninsula; Ukrainian Defense Ministry adamantly denies any role in crash, saying that all its missiles hit their intended targets and that exercises were staged far from jet's flight path; map; photo (M)
news.title: 76 on Board Perish As a Jet From Israel Explodes Off Russia

news.abstract: China is cracking down on Uighurs in major effort to suppress potential unrest among the Muslim Turkic ethnic group, which poses most credible threat of any group to country's internal cohesion; China has joined America's developing alliance against Islamic terrorism in part because it is eager to win international support for its own campaign against Uighur separatists, who have long been viewed with sympathy in West; separatists claim that government policies are marginalizing country's eight million Uighurs and will eventually lead to their cultural annihilation; some Uighurs from Xinjiang Province are known to have fought along side of Afghanistan's Taliban in preparation, they say, for fighting for their cause in China; map; photo (M)
news.title: Fearing Unrest, China Presses Muslim Group

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon warns United States that it risks appeasing Arab nations in way European democracies appeased Hitler on eve of World War II; unusually harsh and public rebuke reflects rising frustration over Bush administration's approach to battling terrorism; remarks come after Russian airliner enroute from Tel Aviv explodes over Black Sea and Palestinian terrorist attack on bus station in northern Israel (M)
news.title: Sharon Invokes Munich in Warning U.S. on 'Appeasement'

news.abstract: Argentine Pres Fernando de la Rua and other officials publicly insist they will not devalue peso, despite fally revenues and stock prices and soaring interest rates (S)
news.title: World Briefing | The Americas: Canada: Ban On Same-Sex Marriage

news.abstract: Dr Rhys Maengwyn Jones, pioneer investigator of human origins in Australia, whose research pushed back beginning of human settlement there to far earlier date than previously thought, dies at age 60; photo (M)
news.title: Dr. Rhys Jones, 60, Researcher Of Human Origins in Australia

news.title: World Briefing | Asia/Pacific: The Koreas: Talks On A Road Link Stall

news.abstract: Northern Alliance in Afghanistan shows off 40 Russian-built tanks in military parade near Tajik border, as leaders suggest offensive against Taliban could come in form of powerful strike toward Kabul coordinated with US air strikes; photos; map; equipment appears new, in contrast to broken-down weaponry seen in other alliance areas; soldiers have new fatigues, Kalashnikov rifles and rocket launchers; speculation noted about military advance (M)

news.abstract: The United States, supported by Britain, today launched a long-anticipated attack on Afghanistan, dropping bombs and firing devastating volleys of cruise missiles.
news.title: U.S. and Britain Clearing Way for 'Relentless' Campaign, Bush Says

news.abstract: Investigators in Sochi, Russia, study wreckage of Siberian Airlines jet that crashed into Black Sea as Pres Putin reportedly rejects Ukraine's denial that plane was shot down by accident; Russian Min Sergei B Ivanov caustically refers to 'so-called version' of disaster that killed 78 people and says Putin wants details of Ukraine's launch of antiaircraft missile four minutes before jet disappeared (M)
news.title: Ukrainians Shift Stance On the Cause Of Air Crash

news.abstract: Osama bin Laden was shown on television this afternoon, declaring that "America is full of fear" and will never be safe and secure until Palestinians feel safe and secure.
news.title: On Video, bin Laden Lashes Out at U.S.

news.abstract: World's leading industrial nations agree to share intelligence information relating to financing of terrorism and to pressure other countries to prevent terrorists from using global banking system (M)
news.title: G-7 Leaders Pledge To Work In Concert to Thwart Terrorists

news.title: Thunderous Attack Heard in Kabul

news.abstract: Iran tries to enforce closed border with Afghanistan and many Afghans seeking refuge there will be quickly deported; Iran is already host to 1.4 million Afghan refugees; photo (M)
news.title: Iranian Security Forces Trying to Block Fleeing Afghans at the Porous Border

news.abstract: Dougie Millings, tailor to stars whose crowning achievement was outfitting the Beatles, dies at age 88 (S)
news.title: Dougie Millings, 88, the Tailor for the Beatles

news.abstract: US and Britain launch powerful barrage of cruise missiles and long-range bombers against Afghanistan on October 8 in campaign to destroy terrorist training camps of Osama bin Laden's Al Qaeda network and Taliban government that has protected it; Pres Bush announces start of military campaign in nationwide televised address; says 'carefully targeted' actions are designed to disrupt use of Afghanistan as terrorist base of operations and to attack military capability of bin Laden organization; says Taliban failed to meet demands to surrender bin Laden, stop supporting terrorism and release foreign aid workers they hold; reiterates warning to nations that sponsor or protect terrorists; address is followed by statement of support from British Prime Min Tony Blair; both leaders emphasize that military campaign is not war against Islam; bin Laden issues own threat in videotape broadcast worldwide; stakes claim to lead all Muslims in fight against America, which he casts as murderer, with Israel, of Iraqis and Palestinians; praises hijackers who staged September 11 attacks on US; vows America will not live in peace until peace reigns in Palestine; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld says bin Laden is not specific target; says initial bombing is intended to create conditions for sustained anti-terrorist operations against his organization; says US is seeking to orchestrate overthrow of Taliban by providing military aid and developing relationships with groups that oppose regime and terrorists they support; reiterates that US is not at war with Islam, noting armed forces have been sent abroad five times in last decade to defend oppressed Muslim populations; administration officials indicate opening aerial campaign can go on for week and will be followed by ground operations by Special Forces units to garner information and hunt down leaders of Al Qaeda network; initial bombardment described; is carried out by 15 land-based bombers and 25 strike aircraft from aircraft carriers; weapons include precision guided bombs; American warships and British submarines fire 50 Tomahawk cruise missiles; witnesses say skies over capital of Kabul are lit up with flashes; say thunderous explosions are heard throughout night; report attacks around cities of Kandahar and Jalalabad, strongholds of radical Islamic regime; Pentagon sends C-17 cargo planes to drop relief supplies of food and medicine for hundreds of thousands of refugees believed fleeing Afghan cities during bombing campaign; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. AND BRITAIN STRIKE AFGHANISTAN, AIMING AT BASES AND TERRORIST CAMPS; BUSH WARNS 'TALIBAN WILL PAY A PRICE'

news.abstract: US-led attacks on Afghanistan garner support from European leaders, including French Pres Jacques Chirac, German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, Italian Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi and Belgian Prime Min Guy Verhofstadt, as well as other allies throughout world; Russia issues statement of support; photos (M)
news.title: European Leaders Voice Support

news.abstract: Article discusses Pres Bush's decision to begin military campaign against Taliban government of Afghanistan, which includes drops of food, medicine and transistor radios that would let Afghan people receive Washington's message (M)
news.title: Quietly, Carefully, President Worked Toward a Decision on Attack-Aid Combination

news.title: Copter Downed In Caucasus; 5 From U.N. Among 9 Dead

news.abstract: Senior officer aboard USS Enterprise in Arabian Sea discusses war so far, saying greatest worry is potential for retaliatory action, expressing sense that Sept 11 terrorist attacks have changed traditional rules of war; fighter pilots encountered limited, unguided antiaircraft artillery on initial strikes in Afghanistan; officer describes beginning of next wave of strikes, as fighter planes and support aircraft thunder into action; photo (M)
news.title: A Wary Warship Launches New Salvos

news.abstract: ATHENS—  With cascading drapes one of this summer's top fashion stories, Greek chic has never looked so cool. So how does an eternal ideal become a hot trend?
news.title: A Greek Revival:A New Take on Classicism

news.abstract: Italian voters approve referendum endorsing constitutional changes to increase regional autonomy at expense of central government's power (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Power To The Provinces

news.abstract: Rep Luis Alfredo Colmenares is assassinated, Bogota; is second congressman from Colombia's war-torn Arauca province killed in week (S)
news.title: World Briefing | The Americas: Colombia: Lawmaker Slain

news.abstract: Three anti-American protesters and 13-year-old boy are shot dead by Pakistani police officers as demonstrators try to storm police station in Kuchlak, town near Afghan border; deaths come on second day of violent protests against American-led airstrikes on Afghanistan; longer air attacks on Afghanistan continue, greater danger that protests could threaten stability of Pakistan; public opinion poll says 62 percent of Pakistanis oppose involvement in war; photo; map; chart (M)

news.abstract: Anti-American demonstrations widen in Indonesia, with riot police firing tear gas to disperse angry protesters outside United States Embassy in Jakarta; radical Muslim groups say they are preparing larger demonstrations and threaten to attack foreigners in Indonesia; about 10,000 Americans live in Indonesia; Pres Megawati Sukarnoputri has announced qualified support for US in its campaign against terrorism in wake of Sept 11 attacks, but anger of fringe groups holding demonstrations reflects broad resentment of US and opposition to its bombing of Afghanistan (M)

news.title: Winning Party In Poland Forges Link With Farmers

news.abstract: Fifty-six Islamic nations holding emergency meeting in Doha, Qatar, issue statement that does not directly condemn Sept 11 attacks on America, but warns against inflicting civilian casualties or striking against other Arab states; careful wording reflects complex pressures and fears that weigh on Arab and Muslim governments; photo (M)
news.title: 56 Islamic Nations Avoid Condemning U.S. Attacks, but Warn on Civilian Casualties

news.abstract: World Briefing
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Mexican federal tribunal, citing evidence of election violations, overturns National Action Party's mayoral victory in Ciudad Juarez in political setback for party of Pres Vicente Fox; rules Mayor Gustavo Elizondo unfairly used office to influence outcome (S)
news.title: World Briefing | The Americas: Mexico: Fox's Party Loses

news.abstract: State Dept orders diplomatic missions to stock up on antibiotics to counter any attack using anthrax (M)
news.title: U.S. Missions Are Stocking Antibiotics

news.abstract: Sampling of work by V S Naipaul, winner of Nobel Prize in Literature (M)
news.title: Plumbing the Mysteries of Inheritance

news.abstract: Goals set by Pres Bush to root out Al Qaeda terrorists and Afghanistan's Taliban government become deeply entangled in murky politics that have kept Afghans fighting for more than 20 years; decision not to bomb Taliban front lines at point where breakdown would leave Kabul open to immediate capture by opposition Northern Alliance reflects grim strategic reality: Pakistan, crucial ally for US in meeting Bush's war aims, has threatened to close its airspace to American aircraft and cancel support if bombing allows Northern Alliance to overrun Kabul; Pakistan regards Northern Alliance, which has been supported by Iran and Russia, with deep suspicion; Gen Pervez Musharraf, Pakistan's president, claims he has ironclad understanding with Washington that Northern Alliance will not be allowed to 'draw mileage' from American bombing by closing in on Kabul before arrangements are complete for new government that will be friendly to Pakistan, as Taliban has been; as result, US military strategy could become hostage to bitter enmities that have long bedeviled Afghan politics, allowing Taliban to consolidate its position; photos (M)
news.title: Afghan Region's Politics Snarl U.S. War Plan

news.abstract: United States and Britain make clear that engagement in Afghanistan might stretch into next summer or beyond; Pres Bush, in news conference, says military operation will continue for days, months or even years; Adm Sir Michael Boyce, Britain's top commander, says that if ground forces are called for, commando brigade of Royal Marines now on exercises in Oman would most likely be used; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld is circumspect when asked if US might use significant number of ground troops inside Afghanistan, but says preparations are in progress for using such troops; American and British officials outline overall strategy of destroying Afghanistan's command and control structure from air, thereby clearing way for military operations by specialty units and for covert operations already under way; option of pursuing other terrorists groups in other Arab countries is still to be explored; American officials are concerned that allies such as Egypt and Saudi Arabia do not yet fully grasp that Bush's 'new war' against terrorism may not end with elimination of Osama bin Laden and could involve chasing terrorist groups in other countries; photo (M)
news.title: LONG WAR IS SEEN

news.abstract: Article on new limits of acceptable speech in Germany as country's leaders eagerly support United States in its battle against terrorism; popular television anchorman comes close to losing his job after suggesting on air that Pres Bush and Osama bin Laden have both displayed intolerance; two schoolteachers have been suspended for making comments that seemed sympathetic to terrorists who attacked US; community access cable television channel blocks call-in show that local Iranian resident has conducted for fear that callers might voice religious hatred or promote violence; some Germans feel uneasy to see their support of US leading to new taboos to conform with fight against terrorism; photos (M)
news.title: Frankfurt Journal; Can't Say That? Muzzling the Modern Germans

news.abstract: United Nations refugee agency head Ruud Lubbers, in unusually blunt statement, says Pakistani security concerns and curbs have stalled preparations for expected influx of Afghan refugees; says support has been weak from governments in region and internationally; expected refugee flood has not yet appeared, in part because American bombing has not stirred panic and because all six neighbors have closed borders; photos (M)
news.title: Flow of Afghan Refugees Is Stalled by Pakistan

news.abstract: North Korea cancels fourth set of family reunions with Koreans in South (S)
news.title: North Korea Cancels Reunions With the South

news.abstract: Several hundred Muslims pour out of Jamia Mosque in Nairobi, Kenya, and begin denouncing US; Sheik Haroum Odundo says every single Muslim is being targed by United States and and every Muslim is Osama bin Laden (S)
news.title: A NATION CHALLENGED: ISLAM -- Nairobi, Kenya; Thousands Hear Call Of Prayer and Politics At World's Mosques

news.abstract: In mosques yesterday, Muslims gathered for Friday Prayers, and in many instances the preaching was political and sharply anti-American.
news.title: Thousands Hear Call of Prayer and Politics at World's Mosques

news.abstract: Samarkand, legendary jewel astride ancient Silk Route, has lost its tourists to fears of war to its south in Afghanistan; photos; map; only people coming into Uzbekistan now are American soldiers pouring in to prepare for military action (Samarkand Journal) (M)
news.title: Samarkand Journal; Tamerlane's Capital Suffers From Lack of Tourists

news.abstract: World Briefing
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Brief descriptions of 22 men on United States list of most wanted terrorists in world; photos (L)
news.title: The 22 Most Wanted Suspects, in a Five-Act Drama of Global Terror

news.abstract: Nearly one million Afghan refugees live in dozens of camps in or near Peshawar, in the Northwest Frontier Province of Pakistan.
news.title: Flee to a Camp. To What Kind of Life?

news.abstract: Synthetic wine bottle corks pose threat to Portugal's natural cork industry, which supplies 85 percent of all wine corks; Portuguese have scrambled to create new breed of cork able to compete with taint-free, consistent performance offered by synthetics; photo (M)
news.title: A Defense From Portugal For the Noble Wine Cork

news.abstract: British government faces European Court of Human Rights ruling that could aid residents of Brentford, Eng, which is directly under Heathrow Airport's noisy flight paths, and have implications across Europe; court found Britian violates European Convention on Human Rights by failing to strike fair balance between nation's needs and people's right to good night's sleep; Britain, at least, must rethink process by which it decides how often night flights land at airport and may have to ground such flights; map; photos (M)
news.title: Under Noisy Skies, Britons Assert a Right to Sleep

news.abstract: Intelligence officials now say that cryptic message intercepted by Central Intelligence Agency last year from Al Qaeda member boasting that Osama bin Laden was planning 'Hiroshima' against America was telling sign of drastic shift in last three years in Al Qaeda's ambitions and global reach; say United States failed to grasp group's transformation from obscure group of Islamic extremists into world's most dangerous terrorists; key factor in shift was bin Laden's decision to act as franchiser of terrorism, providing financial and logistical aid to locally sponsored plots brought to his group by Islamic extremists; extent of group's US operations has stunned Federal Bureau of Investigation; chart; photos (M)
news.title: Signs of Change In Terror Goals Went Unheeded

news.abstract: Recent assassination of Northern Alliance leader Gen Ahmed Shah Massoud is slowing alliance's diplomatic and military efforts; his loss is being felt most deeply in efforts to persuade Taliban commanders to defect to alliance; alliance has yet to mount major military attack since start of United States airstrikes, even in areas where jets have bombed front-line Taliban positions; photo (M)
news.title: Without Charismatic General, Rebels Seem to be Trying to Find Their Way

news.abstract: Interview with Afzal, Afghan father of four who has lived through long, painful arc of Afghan history and is testament to country's present plight; like most Afghans he is illiterate, but remains determined and resourceful survivor after 23 years of invasion and civil war; is optimistic country's hour may have finally come with American military campaign to dislodge ruling Taliban, and is optimistic that better era than his own awaits his children; photo (M)
news.title: Afghan Family Salvages Little but Its Hopes

news.abstract: Ireland buries remains of 10 Irish Republican Army volunteers who were executed by British during country's war of independence 80 years ago, with display of both solemnity and pomp; state funeral, only 13th in country's history since independence, brings much of Dublin to standstill for more than six hours as thousands line streets; photo (M)
news.title: Irish Rebury 10 Republicans Hanged by British in 1920's

news.abstract: Military analysis of weeklong US air strikes on Afghanistan; widespread and intensive military campaign is outstripping diplomatic maneuvers as behind-the-scenes effort to organize leadership that would replace Taliban leaders has made no discernible progress; map; photo (M)
news.title: Fast Track, Slow Track

news.abstract: Focus on debate over resumption whaling in Iceland, which resigned from International Whaling Commission in 1991 and forfeited right to catch up to 400 whales annually for 'scientific research;' despite opposition by whale lovers, poll suggests 75 percent of population backs resumption of whaling; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Reykjavik Journal; Whaling Ban, Not NATO, Heats Iceland's Temper

news.abstract: A senior official of the Northern Alliance declared today that his group would not accept any members of the Taliban in a future coalition government set up to run the country once the current Taliban leadership is driven from power.
news.title: Northern Alliance Casts Doubt on Taliban Participation in Next Government

news.abstract: Taliban Foreign Min Wakil Ahmed Muttawakil, in secret talks in Pakistan, appeals for American bombing pause in Afghanistan, while moderates in Taliban government seek to persuade supreme leader Mullah Muhammad Omar to agree to formula for handover of Osama bin Laden; talks come amid widespread rumors of Muttawakil's defection; his presence in Pakistan, apparently without Omar's approval, suggests intensive American bombing is causing policy shift in Taliban leadership; plea for bombing pause reportedly relayed to Sec Colin Powell, who is on one-day visit; Pakistani officials are optimistic Powell's visit will compress political process, accelerating steps to form post-Taliban government and clear way for American military commanders to pound Taliban front-line troops into disarray, defection or disintegration; photos (M)
news.title: Taliban Envoy Talks of a Deal Over bin Laden

news.abstract: Tensions between France's Muslims, most from North Africa, and rest of French society bubbles into open, with echoes of jihad resounding in sprawling working-class suburbs that surround many French cities; squalid slums are home to mostly poor Muslims, caught up in identity crisis and suffer sting of racism and plague of unemployment; conditions in La Cite des 4,000, slum in La Courneuve suburb of Paris where many regard Osama bin Laden as savior, discussed; map; photos (M)
news.title: La Courneuve Journal; In Suburban Squalor Near Paris, Echoes of Jihad

news.abstract: Prime Min Junichiro Koizumi of Japan visits Seoul, South Korea, to express contrition for country's brutal colonial past and is greeted by energetic protests from civilians and from opposition politicians, who accuse him of lacking sincerity in dealing with historical issues; is forced to cancel address to national legislature after outpouring of objections from opposition parties (M)
news.title: Koreans Protest as Japanese Leader Arrives to Express Contrition

news.abstract: Pentagon acknowledges dispatch of AC-130 gunship operated by special operations forces into skies over Afghanistan; use of lumbering AC-130 seen as indication of increasing American confidence that threat from Taliban air defense is greatly diminished; Pentagon officials say bombing campaign, originally expected to last week, has been spurred on longer by discovery of Taliban troops on move, and by identification of new targets from fresh intelligence (M)
news.title: Special Operations Gunship Being Used Against Taliban

news.abstract: Sources: Dr. Stuart Isaacs and Dr. Elizabeth Colston, both of the University of Pennsylvania
news.title: Finding the Presence of Anthrax

news.abstract: Long-awaited Congo peace talks open in Addis Ababa, amid doubts about its ability to end war (S)
news.title: Peace Talks To End War In Congo Finally Begin

news.abstract: Imelda Marcos, former first lady of Philippines, is released on bail after court ordered her arrest on four counts of corruption involving transactions of more than $350 million in money she is accused of stealing in 1970's (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Philippines: The People V. Mrs. Marcos

news.abstract: Pres Hugo Chavez's approval rating falls from 75 to 56 percent as Venezuelans wait for his reforms to materialize; photo; left-leaning president, elected in landslide in 1998, redrafted Constitution, took control of Assembly and used oil revenues to steer through period of lowered inflation and increased foreign reserves; government has tried to extricate country from recession by raising spending but many experts and former supporters see few real gains for vast majority (M)
news.title: Venezuela Waits for 'Revolution' to Bear Fruit

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld speaks on Middle East television network, Al Jazeera, in Qatar, to assure Arab viewers that United States is waging war against terrorists in Afghanistan, not Afghan people; Rumsfeld becomes latest Bush administration official to grant interview to Al Jazeera, which has angered American officials by broadcasting tapes made by Osama bin Laden (S)
news.title: Rumsfeld to Appeal to Arab Public on Mideast TV Network

news.abstract: Pres Bush says American air attacks in Afghanistan are aimed at paving way for friendly anti-Taliban forces on ground to defeat government; says enemy's air force and air defenses are being demolished; aide says Bush's reference was to Northern Alliance and anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan, and not to use of American and British troops; AC-130 gunships flown by special operations forces blast target around Kandahar, important Taliban stronghold; warplanes employed over no-flight zones in southern Iraq join in aerial bombardment for first time; military official says majority of attacks are focused on military garrisons, airfields and air defenses especially around Kandahar and Kabul; attacks are far from front lines being patrolled by Northern Alliance, whose representatives are complaining that US is not doing enough to help; spokesman for Joint Chiefs of Staff says US military is making no special effort to coordinate strategy with anti-Taliban group, but is systematically attacking elements of Taliban military that will eliminate its ability to support Al Qaeda terrorist network; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Says Aim Is to Ease Entry Of Land Force

news.abstract: Ukrainian Defense Min Oleksandr Kuzmuk suspends commanders of air defense force and of air defense training, first disciplinary moves since military accidentally downed Russian passenger plane (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ukraine: Suspensions Over Missile Error

news.abstract: Bush administration moves to reassure India that America's intensifying alliance with rival Pakistan will not come at its expense; visiting Sec of State Colin L Powell tells Indian leaders US is concerned about Pakistani-inspired terrorism in Kashmir and equates September 11 attacks on US with October 1 terrorist assault in Srinagar, Kashmir capital, that killed more than 40 civilians; renews Washington's offer to get more involved in resolving festering conflict; meets with Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee, who says India is determined to come to terms with Pakistan, despite problems over Kashmir; photo (M)
news.title: Powell's Message: America's Courting of Pakistan Will Not Come at India's Expense

news.abstract: Eight men kidnap Italian priest, Rev Giuseppe Pierantoni, while he says Mass in church in southern Philippines; flee with him in boat; incident is close to area where Abu Sayyaf guerrillas hold 10 hostages (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Philippines: Rebels Kidnap Italian Priest

news.abstract: Pres Bush's trip to Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Forum in Shanghai, China, is expected to result in significant shift in his policy toward Beijing as he seeks to build, maintain and expand global coalition against terrorism in response to September 11 attacks; stresses focus will not be on trade issues that traditionally dominate Asian gathering; attacks force shift by administration to develop strategic partnership with China, which president formerly disdained; aides scramble to find middle ground at summit, with declaration against terrorism that leaves every country to define how it pursues mission; other planned highlights of Bush's trip discussed (M)
news.title: Bush's New Focus Requires A Shift in His China Policy

news.abstract: Filipino Pres Gloria Macapagal Arroyo lifts moratorium on capital punishment and says kidnappers should be executed as soon as possible; ransom kidnappings are entrenched in Philippines (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Philippines: Execution Moratorium Lifted

news.abstract: The textbook for one of the five religion classes required of all 10th graders in Saudi public high schools tackles the complicated issue of who good Muslims should befriend.    After examining a number of scriptures which warn of the dangers of having Christian and Jewish friends, the lesson concludes: ''It is compulsory for the Muslims to be loyal to each other and to consider the infidels their enemy.''
news.title: Anti-Western and Extremist Views Pervade Saudi Schools

news.abstract: Singapore government dissolves legislature and sets election, reportedly anticipating economic downturn that could cost it support (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Singapore: Early Elections

news.abstract: Zhang Xueliang, onetime warlord who in two turbulent weeks in 1936 helped turn course of Chinese history -- and then spent next 55 years under house arrest, gradually and reluctantly becoming national hero -- dies at age 100; photo (M)
news.title: Zhang Xueliang, 100, Dies; Warlord and Hero of China

news.abstract: Twenty-eight suspects go on trial in Cambodia, accused of trying to overthrow government last November; 32 other defendants were convicted in earlier trial (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Cambodia: 32 On Trial Over Rebellion

news.abstract: Bush administration is frustrated by China's resistance to implementing its Nov 2000 accord not to sell missile technology to nations developing nuclear arms despite United States pressure in advance of summit meeting between Pres Bush and Pres Jiang Zemin; wants China to supply list of missile parts and missile-making technology that it would ban from export and show how it would enforce ban (M)
news.title: Frustrating U.S., China Balks At Pact to Stem Missile Sales

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS NICARAGUA: PANEL TO HEAR ORTEGA CASE The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights has agreed to hear a case stemming from unresolved sexual-abuse allegations by Zoilamerica Narvaez Murillo, a stepdaughter of Daniel Ortega, the former Sandinista leader. She said in 1998 that she had been abused by Mr. Ortega from age 11, but the case stalled when courts refused to lift his immunity as a congressman. The commission will decide only whether the government failed to provide adequate remedies.    David Gonzalez (NYT).
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Ottawa scrambles to prepare for mid-November meeting of bankers and finance ministers from 20 leading industrial and developing nations, after India backs out of holding event, citing fears of terrorism (S)
news.title: World Briefing | The Americas: Canada: Meeting Shifts From India

news.abstract: Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi of Italy seems thwarted in his efforts to forge close relationship with Pres Bush; one reason is Berlusconi's recent comments about superiority of Western civilization over Islam, another is fact that Italy, with its revolving-door governments, has difficulty being taken with seriousness and respect it feels it deserves; photo (M)
news.title: Rome Journal; A Bush Admirer Longs to Join America's A-List

news.abstract: More than 200 journalists sign letter to Pres Chandrika Kumaratunga of Sr Lanka demanding more active investigation of assassination year ago of Mylvaganam Nimalarajan, who reported for BBCV's Tamil and Sinhala langeuge services from Jaffna Peninsula; rights workers suspect Nimalarajan was killed because of his reporting on vote rigging in last year's election (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Sri Lanka: Journalists Seek Investigation

news.abstract: Brazil's government planners hope to harness Amazon basin's network of rivers to remedy severe energy shortages in urban areas far to south; photo; map; work is speeded up on world's third-largest dam on bend in Xingu River east of Altamira, which would increase country's hydroelectric capacity fifteen percent; photo; map; ambitious programs have so far generated only fierce opposition among local environmental and religious groups (M)
news.title: Brazil Searches for More Energy

news.abstract: Expect more quick forays into Afghanistan by American special forces. That was the message from Pentagon officials after the assault Friday night by more than 100 Army Rangers and other elite forces, the first major ground operation in the war against Osama bin Laden's terrorist network and its Taliban protectors.    RISK IS CERTAIN -- Mindful of the Soviet Union's sorry experience in Afghanistan, a decade of quagmire and the loss of 15,000 troops, American officials said they planned to rely on lightning raids by commando teams, operations expected to be short but intense. The aim, they said, is to surprise and outpace the enemy. But that also involves close combat and inevitable risk. American casualties are more than likely, it was suggested.
news.title: A NATION CHALLENGED: AN OVERVIEW: Oct. 20, 2001; War on the Ground, Allies Around the Globe, F.B.I. on the Case

news.abstract: News analysis on debate within Sharon government in Israel over whether to begin international campaign to undermine Yasir Arafat's legitimacy as leader of Palestinians; photo (M)
news.title: Israel Debates the Cost of Dealing With Arafat

news.abstract: Military analysis of nighttime commando raid in Afghanistan as opening new fast-paced stage of war against terrorism, first of series of stinging jabs intended to unhinge enemy; photo; Pentagon has warned that this phase may be drawn out and will not end until Qaeda network is destroyed and Taliban is toppled, but individual operations will be short and intense, at least for now; US military intends to show it has learned from 1993, when Somalis accustomed to US tactics shot down Black Hawk helicopter and killed 18 Americans (M)
news.title: First of the Stinging Jabs

news.abstract: Since the September  attacks, Al Azhar  the revered mosque, the distinguished university, the leading voice of the Sunni Muslim establishment -- has renewed with accustomed grace the roles it has played in the world of Islam for more than 1,000 years.    It has sought to advise Muslims around the world that those who kill in the name of Islam are nothing more than heretics. It has sought to guide, to reassure Westerners against any clash of civilizations.
news.title: Moderate Muslims Fear Their Message Is Being Ignored

news.abstract: Following are excerpts from the joint news conference in Shanghai yesterday by President Bush and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, as provided by the White House:    PRESIDENT PUTIN      The consequences of the tragic events of Sept. 11 -- political, economic, psychological consequences -- today are acutely felt in many countries and in all the continents. I think nobody has doubts the unprecedented carnage of the terrorists requires our united efforts, unification of the efforts of international community to fight terrorism. And we prepared and we issued a joint statement in this regard.
news.title: Bush and Putin: Accord on Terrorism

news.abstract: Dr Edward P Radford, who energetically promoted a higher estimate of cancer risk from radiation exposure and whose position was eventually upheld, dies at age 79; photo (M)
news.title: Edward Radford, 79, Scholar Of the Risks From Radiation

news.abstract: President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia and President Bush said they could reach agreements that would alter the 1972 Antiballistic Missile Treaty.
news.title: Bush and Putin Declare They Can Alter ABM Pact

news.abstract: A Palestinian went on a shooting spree in a bustling commercial area in southern Jerusalem today, wounding four Israelis before he was killed by a soldier.
news.title: Palestinian Is Killed After His Shooting Spree

news.abstract: The roar of the first jet this afternoon prompted reflexive fears of an enemy attack on this rebel-held territory. But when another and then another jet thundered overhead, flying so high they could not even be seen, it dawned on people what might finally be happening: the end of their years of isolation and defeat.     As night fell, the news spread. The Americans were starting to bomb the Taliban front lines.
news.title: Roar of the Warplanes Overhead Bolsters the Hopes of the Rebels

news.abstract: US warplanes concentrate strikes in Afghanistan on 16th day of bombing on front-line Taliban positions; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld says target are being hit to give direct support to anti-Taliban forces in north; says attacks on Taliban forces and Al Qaeda terrorists are intended to clear way for anti-Taliban Northern Alliance to advance; suggests attacks will continue, if necessary, through Ramadan, Muslim holy month of fasting; military officials say operations are being coordinated with rebels; photo (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Says Attacks Seek to Help Rebels Advance

news.abstract: Carla Del Ponte, chief prosecutor for UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague, accuses Yugoslav authorities of continuing to block cooperation with tribunal and of not being ready to face past; says it is not enough to turn over former leader, Slobodan Milosevic; says it must cooperate more fully to allow truth of past Balkan conflicts to emerge (M)
news.title: Hague Tribunal Chief Says Yugoslavia Still Isn't Cooperating

news.abstract: Thousands of Israelis pour into streets of Jerusalem as Israeli forces engage in broadest action in years against Palestinians; demand that government take even tougher action; demonstration comes as leaders of Labor Party, historically nation's standardbearer of moderation and diplomatic solutions, convene to consider whether military action should drive them from Sharon's coalition (M)
news.title: Labor Party Leaders Weigh Leaving Sharon's Coalition

news.abstract: Amid a third day of airstrikes against Taliban soldiers on the front line, Pentagon officials said for the first time that their goal was to choke off fuel, food and other supplies to the group.
news.title: U.S. Aiming to Cut Supplies to Lift the Taliban's Grip

news.abstract: Interim Assembly of East Timor notifies UN that it wants May 20, 2002, to be date for full independence; map (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: East Timor: Setting A Date For Independence

news.abstract: Israel turned down President Bush's request to withdraw its forces from Palestinian-controlled territory, putting new pressure on American-Israeli relations and the anti-terror coalition with Arab allies. Israel's foreign minister, Shimon Peres, said in Washington that Israel would not pull out until the Palestinians arrested the men who killed Israel's tourism minister.       Article, Page A8.
news.title: Israelis Rebuff U.S. On Pullout Request

news.abstract: Residents of Charikar, Afghanistan, Northern Alliance village, say Taliban forces fired rockets at market, killing two people and wounding dozens; see move as retaliation for American airstrikes; urge continuation of bombing raids, interviews; Northern Alliances forces respond by shelling suspected Taliban position above bustling town; map; photos (M)
news.title: Residents in Rebel Village Tell of Rockets Fired by Taliban Forces

news.abstract: ASIA.
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Israeli Foreign Minister Shimon Peres meets in Washington with Pres Bush and Sec of State Colin Powell and rebuffs their demand that Israel pull out of Palestinian-controlled areas of West Bank; says security forces of Yasir Arafat must first arrest men who murdered Israeli Tourism Minister Rehavam Zeevi; Bush and Powell balance call for immediate Israeli withdrawal with demands on Arafat for arrests in Zeeve's murder, along with suspects in terrorist attacks on Israelis; photo (M)
news.title: Israel Rebuffs U.S. Demand To End Its West Bank Raids

news.abstract: Overview of day's events in war on terrorism and spreading anthrax scare (M)
news.title: New Urgency on Anthrax, Bombs and Blunders, the Ripple Effect

news.abstract: Adm Sir Michael Boyce, Britain's top military officer, says ground troops may have to operate in Afghanistan for weeks at a time if they are to ferret out Osama bin Laden and destroy his terrorist network; raids envisaged by Boyce could be far longer and more risky than raid carried out last week by US Special Operations forces, who were in Afghan territory for only few hours and encountered light resistance; Boyce is heavily involved in planning campaign against Taliban and bin Laden; British role is more vital now that campaign is beginning to involve ground troops; new phase of conflict plays to Britain's military strengths its commandos are among most highly regarded in world; photo (M)
news.title: GROUND RAIDS SEEN AS LONG AND RISKY

news.abstract: Pentagon, citing intelligence sources, holds Taliban might poison food aid and blame United States; warns Afghans not to eat donated food from abroad if has passed through Taliban; warning is pre-emptive strike in intensifying war for public opinion in Afghanistan and broader Islamic world; Pentagon says US strikes have not wholly undercut Taliban; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Warns Afghans That Taliban May Poison Relief Food

news.abstract: Assault units Gen Ahmed Shah Massoud formed in year before his assassination, perhaps joined by Taliban defectors, could prove to be Northern Alliance's best chance to breach maze of Taliban trenches, tanks and minefields north of Kabul; units, intended to be more regular army than guerrillas, wear uniforms and have better arms than other alliance soldiers; visits to two units find soldiers who range from fierce to clumsy; photo (M)
news.title: Rebels Rely On an Elite For a Drive On Kabul

news.abstract: Amsterdam airport has one of latest technological gizmos of security conscious age: state of the art iris scanner to identify travelers; technique is part of growing field of biometric imaging, in which computers are used to identify someone's unique physical features, like palm prints, facial features and eye structure; airport planned to introduce device even before Sept 11 hijackings in United States heightened concern about air safety; photos (M)
news.title: Amsterdam Journal; Security on the Brain, Solutions in the Eyes

news.abstract: Israeli troops storm into another West Bank village, killing at least 5 Palestinians and arresting 11 more, including two men Israelis say helped kill cabinet minister last week; Palestinian leaders accuse Israeli government of inventing link to minister's killing to cover up what they call 'massacre' of at last 10 people; raid on Palestinian town, Beit Rima, brings to seven number of villages and cities in which Israeli troops have captured positions in operation begun after killing of tourism minister, Rehavam Zeevi; latest attack comes hours after Pres Bush appeals for Israeli withdrawal from Palestinian territory; photo (M)
news.title: Israelis Storm Village in the West Bank

news.abstract: Paulo Maluf, former presidential candidate in Brazil and Sao Paulo mayor, is charged with not declaring campaign donations in 1992 and 1998 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | The Americas: Brazil: Ex-Official Indicted

news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Communist legislators stormed the podium and unfurled banners in Parliament in a protest aimed at stopping a proposal that would allow the state to sell its vast farmland holdings to private buyers. The 450-member Parliament has 113 Communists, and the Interfax news agency reported that nearly all of them took part in the protest, holding banners that read ''To sell land is to sell the homeland.'' Ukraine, once a Soviet breadbasket, has 81.5 million acres of fertile farmland but efforts to overhaul the Soviet collective-farm system have gone slowly and production is low.     Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ukraine: Land Reform Roils Communists

news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: Anthrax Scare On Tokyo Subway

news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Nigeria: President Reins In Soldiers

news.abstract: Swiss police say crash and subsequent fire in St Gotthard Tunnel apparently killed far fewer people than first feared; say they have confirmed 11 deaths, with 30 travelers still missing; fire exposes ventilation system weaknesses in heavily traveled tunnel, thought to be one of safest in Europe; map; photo (M)
news.title: Swiss Lower Estimate of Toll in Tunnel Fire

news.abstract: Bush administration has put together aid package for Pakistan that is likely to total several billion dollars and includes sweeping debt rescheduling, grants stretching over many years and trade benefits as reward for its support against terrorism; package, which is encountering some resistance in Washington and abroad, would represent departure from often glacial process of aiding poor countries in recent years; while support may reward Pres Pervez Musharraf for his backing of American-led coalition, critics worry that politically inspired aid could be misdirected; some American lawmakers say Bush administration may have too readily agreed to give Pakistan about $600 million in cash this year and next without reliable way of ensuring that money would be used to improve health and education rather than to underwrite military or Islamic militants that Pakistan backs in disputed territory of Kashmir; Rep Jim McDermott has reservations about aid, while Rep Jim Kolbe opposes it (M)
news.title: U.S. Is Planning an Aid Package for Pakistan That Is Worth Billions

news.abstract: Egypt's Westernized elite, used to effortlessly melding Western and Arab cultures, anxiously seek neutral ground as United States war on terrorism in Afghanistan is widely seen in Egypt as Western war against Arabs and Islam; are uncomfortable with virulent anti-Americanism that has become part of normal public discourse but feel unable to intervene in face of open attacks on US in government-controlled press; photo (M)
news.title: Egypt's Elite Torn by Arab Roots and Western Ties

news.abstract: Talks between Yugoslav Pres Vojislav Kostunica and Montenegrin Pres Milo Djukanovic break off without accord on how to run federal Yugoslav state; both leaders say Montenegro must hold independence referendum in spring (M)
news.title: Talks Fail to Entice Montenegro to Stay Yugoslav

news.abstract: Anxiety has increased about safety of Hamid Qarzai, potential post-Taliban leader, who is believed to have traveled to Afghanistan to incite uprising among his tribesmen; Qarzai, who is favored by some Washington strategists as best bet for leading alliance of southern Afghans against Taliban, is reported by his associates to be in countryside around Kandahar, Taliban capital and home of his tribe; Quetta, Pakistan, has been his base (M)
news.title: Concern Grows Over Fate of Another Foe of the Taliban

news.abstract: Nat

news.title: South African White Party, Hurt by Feud, Collapses

news.abstract: Over 70 journalists face criminal charges in Panama, whose draconian press laws lets public officials bring 'disrespect charges' against journalists who publish exposes or unflattering commentaries; most defendants in cases already settled have been pardoned or fined; laws also let officials block press access to wide variety of government documents deemed confidential almost by whim; journalists charge laws are part of antidemocratic effort to silence and punish critics; cartoon (M)/
news.title: Panama Is Putting Journalists on Trial

news.abstract: Spain's Basque separatists say they want peace, but only if Spanish and French allow vote on independence in region; want referendum that includes French Basque lands and Spanish province of Navarra (S)
news.title: 'Peace Is Possible,' Basque Separatist Group Says

news.abstract: Article profiles China's vice president Hu Jintao, heir apparent to aging Jiang Zemin, who is making first visit to Russia and Western Europe in common diplomatic trip filled with meaning; it is seen as another calibrated step in Hu's cautious but apperently effective ascension, one that under peculiarties of Chinese politics requires him to keep head down; photos (M)
news.title: China's Heir Apparent in Debut on the World Stage

news.abstract: Article on scandal involving Mexican pop star Gloria Trevi and manager Sergio Andrade, both of whom fled to Brazil to avoid prosecution for sexually abusing teenage girls and are awaiting extradition; Trevi who says her life would be endangered if she returns to Mexico, has been imprisoned since February 2000; has become pregnant in jail in apparent attempt to take advantage of provision in Brazilian law that prevents extradition of foreigners who are parents of Brazilian child; photos (M)
news.title: Rio Journal; The Singer, the Scandal, The Jailhouse Pregnancy

news.abstract: Gabrielle Parnes, American who lives in Paris, talks about living abroad in wake of Sept 11 terrorist attacks on US; photo (S)
news.title: The French Seem a Bit Friendlier

news.abstract: Modest funeral without a body is held for Abdul Haq, former Afghan guerrilla commander who was killed by Taliban as he traveled eastern Afghanistan on secretive mission to incite uprising; service is held in Peshawar, Pakistan; family spokesman says Taliban would not allow body to be brought across border to Pakistan, but Haq's brother, Haji din Muhammad, blames Pakistani 'political agent' who refused to allow body through checkpoint; Pakistan's intelligence agency has frequently been accused of backing Haq's plans to topple Taliban, and now its agents are being accused of betraying Haq in ugly double deal; facts about Haq's last journey into Afghanistan are murky; Taliban claim that one or more 'Americans' were with Haq and narrowly escaped; former national security adviser, Robert C McFarlane, says United States did try last-minute assistance, but it proved too late for Haq; photos (M)
news.title: Slain Taliban Foe Is Buried. So They Say.
World Briefing

news.abstract: Border between Pakistan and Afghanistan is officially closed, but it is so porous that wounded Taliban fighters cross for treatment and easy flow of commerce and people between two countries continues, helping Afghanistan retain semblance of normalcy; Taliban profits, taxing shipments into Pakistan; closed border was condition set by Washington when it established relationship with Pakistan, but fabled, centuries-old smuggling route has not changed much and Pashtun tribesmen on both sides of border feel more allegiance among themselves than to respective countries; photo (M)
news.title: Taliban Continue Trade Through Closed but Porous Border

news.abstract: Israeli forces remain in Palestinian enclaves of Tulkarm, Jenin, Qalqilya and Ramallah in West Bank after vacating Bethlehem and Beit Jala; has remained entrenched, despite American pleas to leave immediately; Israeli government says soldiers are vital bulwark against terrorist attacks; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Troops in No Hurry To Leave West Bank Towns

news.abstract: Indian Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee, after meeting in Delhi with German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, rejects proposal to meet with Pakistani Gen Pervez Musharraf in New York during United Nations General Assembly (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India-Pakistan: No Talks At U.N.

news.abstract: Thousands of mourners in Behawalpur, Pakistan, bewail killings of 15 Christians at funeral procession for victims of shootings at St Dominic's Roman Catholic Church; no group has claimed responsibility for attack, however, Muslim militants are under suspicion (M)
news.title: Funeral Held For Christians In Pakistan

news.abstract: Chancellor Gerhard Schroder lauds economic contribution of Turkish immigrants as Germany marks 40th anniversary of accord inviting Turkish workers to Germany (M)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Tribute To Turkish Workers

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld will leave this week for Russia and nations near Afghanistan as Bush administration strives to hold together coalition for military campaign against Osama bin Laden and Taliban; Gen Tommy Franks meets with Uzbek leaders, saying US military activity may change from day to day; Sen Carl Levin says in interview that US may have to add to special operations forces to intensify pressure; British Sec Geoff Hoon, in Washington, says allies should make clear that they are 'taking account of Ramadan' holy month to avoid further strains with Muslim countries; photos; Rumsfeld observes that Taliban and Al Qaeda are 'unlikely to take a holiday' from trying to kill Americans; Prime Min Tony Blair tells Britons not to forget horror of Sept 11 attacks (M)
news.title: U.S. Campaign On 2nd Front: Public Opinion

news.abstract: Yasser al-Siri, Egyptian who gave letter of accreditation to two men who posed as television journalists to assassinate Afghan rebel leader Ahmed Shah Massoud, is charged with conspiracy under Britain's antiterrorism law; photo; Siri sought asylum in 1994 after Egyptian court convicted him in absentia in failed bomb attack against prime minister that killed schoolgirl (S)
news.title: Britain Charges Man in Death Of a Top Afghan Rebel Leader

news.abstract: Channel Tunnel is closed to freight traffic for 11 hours after dozens of asylum seekers break into freight yard near Calais, France, and try to hide on trains bound for Britain; some 150 migrants are arrested (M)
news.title: Flood of Asylum Seekers Closes Channel Tunnel for Freight

news.abstract: Olexy Romashko, Ukrainian official who policed legality of stock market transactions, is found murdered in his apartment building elevator, apparent victim of mafia-connected clans that dominate nation's business and financial sectors (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ukraine: Stock Market Monitor Slain

news.abstract: Beatriz Paredes has emerged as leader of once-dominant Institutional Revolutionary Party, rare woman at top of Mexican politics; holds party must embrace calls for change to be credible opposition force; is trying to rally both party faithful and potential new supporters; is seen as someone who could draw women and young people back to party; photo (M)
news.title: A Rare Leader Tries to Save Mexico's Fallen Party

news.abstract: Paul C Warnke, who was highest Pentagon official in Johnson administration to question openly the aims and conduct of Vietnam War and later, as Pres Jimmy Carter's chief arms-control negotiator, sought to trim American and Soviet nuclear stockpiles, dies at 81; photo (L)
news.title: Paul Warnke, 81, a Leading Dove in Vietnam Era, Dies

news.abstract: AFRICA KENYA: DON'T FORGET US, BOMB VICTIMS SAY Kenyans wounded in the 1998 bombing of the American Embassy in Nairobi accused the United States government of failing to compensate them while rushing to the aid of those injured in the Sept. 11 attacks on New York and Washington. The victims insisted on cash payouts and dismissed as paltry the more than $40 million the United States has spent on medical care and reviving businesses.
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Danish Prime Min Poul Nyrup Rasmussen calls election for Nov 20, saying that waiting for mid-March deadline would force four months of campaigning on country at time of uncertainty brought on by terror attacks of Sept 11 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Denmark: Premier Calls Quick Election

news.abstract: Georgia descended further into political crisis today after a police raid on a popular television station set off mass protests and the dismissal of most of the government.
news.title: Protests and Firing of Cabinet Plunge Georgia Into New Crisis

news.abstract: Anti-Taliban leader Hamid Karzai reports from Derawat, Aghanistan, that he is indeed alive and well and that his forces did not sustain any casualties in fighting against Taliban militia in southern part of country; Karzai is considered prime target as he tries to foment anti-Taliban uprising which he hopes will attract major defectors from ruling regime (M)
news.title: Rebel Chief Flees Raid By Taliban

news.abstract: Iran marks 22d anniversary of takeover of US Embassy with special exhibit on grounds of compound, opened to public for first time; features include carnival game involving pounding on devilish face wearing US-flag hat; photos; conservatives use occasion to stoke fresh anti-American sentiment, even as those who once climbed walls mellow and officials take tentative steps toward cooperating with US (M)
news.title: Step Right Up! On Show in Iran, Sins of Uncle Sam

news.abstract: Accurate US bombing of front-line Taliban forces in northern Afghanistan has been delayed for weeks by difficulty of infiltrating up to 100 elite American commandos; Sec Donald Rumsfeld and other officials cite howling sandstorms, ground fire and coordination problems with opposition forces; US special forces are training and organizing rebel militias and spotting targets for warplanes, but only about two dozen are on ground so far; delays complicate campaign to oust Taliban, get Osama bin Laden and promote resistance in south, where some angry Pashtuns seem to have rallied to Taliban; national security adviser Condoleezza Rice sees no bombing pause for Ramadan, saying enemy has to be pressed to the end; Gen Richard B Myers reports B-52's are having some effect on entrenched Taliban troops around Kabul and Mazar-i-Sharif; he and Rumsfeld say such strikes now account for 80 percent of missions (M)
news.title: Trouble in Deploying Commandos Is Said to Hurt U.S. Air Campaign

news.abstract: Zimbabwe Finance Min Simba Makoni, in annual budget speech to parliament, says he expects economy to shrink by 7.3 percent this year (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Zimbabwe: Economic Outlook Gloomy

news.abstract: Western and Arab news organizations receive copies of letter handwritten in Arabic, carrying Osama bin Laden's signature, urging Pakistan's Muslims to defend Islam against what it calls Christian crusade; letter is given relatively little coverage by Arab and Western news programs (M)
news.title: Bin Laden Letter Calls Upon Pakistanis to Defend Islam

news.abstract: Following is the translated text of Osama Bin Laden's latest statement, as posted on the British Broadcasting Corporation's web site.
news.title: Bin Laden's Statement

news.abstract: Hamid Karzai, anti-Taliban Pashtun commander now on clandestine mission in southern Afghanistan, must persuade potential allies that US will provide kind of military support that so far has gone largely to Northern Alliance; relatives outside Afghanistan describe efforts by Karzai, who is favorite of some of Afghanistan experts in Washington (M)
news.title: Without U.S. Support, Pashtun Rebel Leader Is Finding Few Allies

news.abstract: Bush administration imposes stringent financial sanctions on Hamas, Hezbollah and 20 other suspected terrorist organizations; move is sign that admistration feels confident enough in Arab countries' support for action against Osama bin Laden to include anti-Israeli groups that have considerable support in Arab world; US has long frozen Hamas and Hezbollah assets in US, but members of Congress have urged stronger action; new list includes other Arab groups, three Colombian groups, Real Irish Republican Army and Basque group ETA; latter are included to show US is not just focusing on Israel and Palestinians; photos of Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and Hamas founder Ahmed Yassin (M)
news.title: U.S. Widens Net to Snare Terror Assets; Expands List

news.abstract: japan blocks trip by foreign minister**Japan Foreign Min Makiko Tanaka has shakier hold on her job after ruling opposition legislators join forces to deny her permission to participate in opening of United Nations General Assembly; Prime Min Junichiro Koizumi says he finds vote 'disappointing' (S)
news.title: Japan Blocks Trip By Foreign Minister

news.abstract: Indonesia will issue decree allowing banks to freeze assets of terrorism suspects as United States has requested (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Indonesia: Ready To Freeze Assets

news.abstract: Osama bin Laden portrays American military campaign in Afghanistan as war against Islam; his videotaped speech, broadcast by Al Jazeera television network in Qatar, is seen as attempt to play to Arab and Muslim popular opinion; he denounces as infidels Muslim leaders who cooperate with United Nations and refers to its secretary general, Kofi Annan, as 'a criminal'; he praises what he calls 'great strikes' made against New York and Washington on Sept 11, and says US has not produced any evidence for its attacks against Afghanistan; says it is not war against terrorism, but against religion and creed; Bush administration has vehemently denied that campaign against terrorism begun after Sept 11 attacks is directed against Islamic faith; photo (M)
news.title: Bin Laden, in a Taped Speech, Says Attacks in Afghanistan Are a War Against Islam

news.abstract: American military advisers are in Zamboanga in southern Philippines to pursue terrorist group, Abu Sayyaf, which American officials link to Osama bin Laden; government of Philippines is determined to wipe out Abu Sayyaf, and has found dedicated, well-equipped partner in United States; Lt Cmdr Jeff Davis says Abu Sayyaf is not just Philippine problem; calls it international terrorist group that poses as much of threat to US as to Philippines; nevertheless, suggestion that Abu Sayyaf is Philippine branch of bin Laden's Al Qaeda strikes people in Philippines as faintly bizarre; they say Abu Sayyaf has lost whatever religious fervor it once had; photo (M)
news.title: The Temperature's a Lot Warmer but the Mission's the Same: Hunting Down Terrorists

news.abstract: Village elections have become more widespread and in some cases more free in China over last three years, but local Communist Party leaders, appointed from above, retain real power; conflicts between elected committees and party secretaries are on rise; map; photo (M)m
news.title: China's Villagers Vote, but Its Party Rules

news.abstract: Japanese consumers abandon beef in response to single case of mad cow disease; beef sales have fallen 50 percent; beef barbecue restaurants are changing their menus and cutting prices; consumers lack faith in government in wake of disclosure that it suppressed European Commision warning that Japan was likely candidate for disease; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Japan, Beef Business Sinks in a Sea of Skepticism

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld, beginning trip through Russia and Central Asia aimed at bolstering antiterrorism coalition, meets with Russian Min Sergei B Ivanov and later with Pres Vladimir V Putin; Ivanov says they discussed use of Russian intelligence to support United States military campaign in Afghanistan and arms control; again says Russian troops are not involved in war; sees some merit in Rumsfeld push to abandon Antiballistic Missile Treaty; photo (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Visits Russia and Central Asia to Bolster Coalition

news.abstract: Tajikistan and US move toward agreement that could lead to American military strikes against Taliban forces from its territory; Tajikistan would receive millions of dollars in return; Pentagon officials say that if bases are found to be in satisfactory condition, warplanes could use them for bombing raids against Taliban forces in Afghanistan; say air field could be used by helicopter-borne Special Operations forces, and as hub for military supplies being sent to Northern Alliance and relief supplies being dropped to Afghan refugees by US Air Force; US military will also look at bases in Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan; Joint Chiefs of Staff chairman, Gen Richard B Myers, says US is rushing supplies to Northern Alliance forces so they can fight through winter; photo; map (M)
news.title: U.S. MAY GAIN USE OF MORE AIR BASES TO STRIKE TALIBAN

news.abstract: Senior official in Northern Alliance reports that six-member team of American military personnel has landed in alliance territory north of Kabul to inspect new airstrip and to carry out covert activities; whether sluggish and fractious opposition alliance will actually carry out attack near Kabul is unknown; alliance exercises and arrival of American team suggests effort may be under way to begin attack before winter and Islamic holy month of Ramadan; photo (M)
news.title: Team of American Military Personnel Arrives in Rebel Territory in Afghanistan

news.abstract: The United States is committed to building closer military ties with India, an ally in the global campaign against terrorism, the defense secretary told Indian officials today.
news.title: Rumsfeld Tells India That U.S. Wants to Extend Military Ties

news.abstract: Overview of day's events in Afghan war front, with Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld arriving in Pakistan after quick visits to Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan
news.title: Lull in Tension, Traveling Diplomacy and New Help in the War Zone

news.abstract: American jets pound Taliban positions in heaviest bombing yet along country's far northern front, as rebel troops appear to take their first steps toward mounting attack on the ground; dozens of bombs are dropped on single ridge in Kalakata near border with Tajikistan; for all their intensity, bombs are unable to wipe out Taliban postions there; alliance fighter claims Taliban are riding out bombing by ducking into caves in hillsides; photo; map (M)
news.title: U.S. Jets Pound Taliban Positions in Heaviest Bombing Yet
