news.abstract: Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israeli Foreign Min Shimon Peres meet for second time in three days, joining European Union officials for informal gathering in Brussels; European Union, in absence of high-level American engagement in Middle East, is pressing hard to provide nervous Arab world with at least impression of movement in peace process after 13 months of deterioration and bloodshed; photo (M)
news.title: European Union Brings Peres and Arafat Together Again

news.abstract: Pres Daniel Arap Moi agrees to open Kenya's 420-mile border with Somalia in recognition of progress in talks between Somali government and opposition warlords; ordered border closed in July, saying illegal arms were entering his country (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Kenya: Somalia Border Reopened

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon explains decision to postpone upcoming trip to US, saying he needs to remain in Israel to cope with possible surge in attacks as result of new army tactics in confrontation with Palestinians; says army, after withdrawing troops from Qalqilya in West Bank and expected withdrawal from other Palestinian-governed cities, will use other means to combat terrorism (M)
news.title: Sharon Cites Possible Surge In Attacks for Delaying Trip

news.abstract: Enrique Bolanos, businessman arrested and stripped of property in 1980's for outspoken opposition to Sandinista rule, is elected president of Nicaragua, defeating nemesis, Daniel Ortega, by surprisingly wide margin; captures estimated 53.7 percent of vote, compared with 44.7 percent for Ortega, on strong voter turnout; political analysts say margin of victory, which defied opinion polls showing candidates in statistical tie, resulted from fear of Sandinistas' past and declarations by US officials who doubted Ortega's sincerity in stating that he had moderated views and wanted national reconciliation; photos (M)
news.title: Nicaragua Voters Reject Ortega's Bid for the Presidency

news.abstract: LONDON—  As the world's largest economies appear headed into a simultaneous recession, central bankers stand poised this week to deliver a new round of interest-rate relief. But economists are divided on the size of the cuts and on whether they will stimulate a rebound.
news.title: Central Banks Poised for a New Round of Rate Cuts

news.abstract: Pres Chandrika Kumaratunga of Sri Lanka accuses her former parlimentary affairs minister, S B Dissanayake, of having offered to kill two critical journalists (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Sri Lanka: Mud Flies Before Election

news.abstract: European Union urges Israelis and Palestinians to resume talks, without preconditions, to establish lasting cease-fire, ensure security and move toward peace talks on settlement that would establish independent Palestine; Min Shimon Peres and Yasir Arafat hold several meetings in Brussels, Peres reporting he pressed Palestinian leader to crack down on terror attacks; photo; Javier Solana says what matters is that Israelis and Arabs met at all (M)
news.title: Europeans Urge Israelis and Palestinians to Resume Talks

news.abstract: Northern Alliance spokesmen say they have captured three districts near approach to strategic city of Mazar-i-Sharif in northern Afghanistan with help of US military advisers; photo; map; Sec Donald Rumsfeld warns US has not confirmed claim; Qudratullah Hurmat says Americans in fight gave orders to commanders, organized troops, photographed Taliban positions and delivered ammunition by helicopter; claims capture of Taliban fighters (M)
news.title: Afghan Rebels Assert Gains, Saying U.S. Troops Helped

news.abstract: Former Pres Jimmy Carter, leading observer mission to Nicaragua, urges vigilance as election officials resume counting votes from presidential and legislative elections; Enrique Bolanos defeats Daniel Ortega in presidential vote; Carter photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Nicaragua: Carter Wary On Vote Count

news.abstract: Bush administration takes first steps to expand coalition fighting Taliban and Al Qaeda terrorist network after weeks of deflecting European offers of military forces; acts amid signs of waning popular support overseas for bombing campaign; Pres Bush speaks by video to Central and Eastern European leaders and in Rose Garden with French Pres Jacques Chirac; photos; likens Al Qaeda to fascists who darkened 20th century, saying they show 'same mad, global ambitions' and brutal determination to control every life; also warns that Osama bin Laden seeks biological, chemical and nuclear weapons; Britain has urged enlarging coalition; Germany pledges 3,900 troops who could become first German forces outside Europe since end of World War II; NATO weighs dramatic mission to get food into Afghanistan, joining US effort; Italy offers 1,000 troops and equipment; France also offers commandos and warplanes but does not have base nearby; Pentagon says more than 50,000 National Guardsmen and Reservists have been mobilized; 16 European leaders listening in Warsaw applaud Bush reference to their own past domination by Soviet Union (M)
news.title: U.S. TAKES STEPS TO BOLSTER BLOC FIGHTING TERROR

news.abstract: Opposition candidate for local elections in Cambodia is beaten to death, fourth such murder (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Cambodia: 4th Opposition Candidate Killed

news.abstract: Concorde, world's only supersonic jetliner, resumes service for first time since July 2000 Air France crash; France has treated plane's return, with stronger tires, armor-plated wiring and redesigned fuel tank, as matter of national honor; photo (M)
news.title: The Sleek Concorde Is Once More Carrying Passengers

news.abstract: Nepal and Bhutan fail to resolve longstanding dispute over refugees; about 100,000 Hindus fled mostly Buddhist Bhutan decade ago and settled in UN-run camps in Nepal (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Brazil: Not Happy With U.S.

news.abstract: Israeli lawmakers vote to lift parliamentary immunity of Azmi Bishara, Israeli Arab legislator, so he can be prosecuted for remarks urging resistance to Israel, and for arranging Israeli Arab visits to Syria; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Israel: Arab Lawmaker Faces Charges

news.abstract: American sailor aboard aircraft carrier Kitty Hawk is feared lost at sea after helicopter crew tries unsuccessfully to save him; officials say sailor went overboard at dusk; refuse to cite location of carrier; if confirmed lost, sailor would be fourth American death in war against Taliban and Al Qaeda (S)
news.title: Sailor Is Feared To Be Lost at Sea From Kitty Hawk

news.abstract: Turkey and Greece agree that Greece will be able to return illegal immigrants to Turkey; long-sought deal comes as Greece fears new wave of illegal refugees from US bombing campaign in Afghanistan (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Turkey: Immigration Accord With Greece

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook describes night sky in Afghanistan, where natural world looms large; stars and moon are very bright without competition from electric lights; cratered landscape is harsh; there is no bridge across Kokcha River so people cross on horseback; elements dictate life in land where rains--and hunger--can force people to move; describes working in mud-brick hut that operates with gas-powered generator and no plumbing; photo (M)
news.title: To the Stranger, a Wild Land, Strangely Awesome

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook on Saudi Arabia, where recent telethon raised more than $36 million for Afghan people; photos; Saudi government picks careful path between supporting US campaign against terrorism and expressing public's unease about civilian suffering; telethon mirrors government's way of throwing money at nasty problems, and leaving unpleasant details under rug; television Islamic-style, Americans at American International School and lack of jobs for young educated Saudis also discussed (M)
news.title: Reporter's Notebook; No Jerry Lewis, but Saudi Telethon Reaches Goal

news.abstract: Pres Pervez Musharraf says he is visiting United States in search of major gestures from Bush administration to blunt criticism in Pakistan of his strong support for war on terrorism, interview; seeks release of 28 F-16 jets, whose delivery was blocked because of Pakistan's development of nuclear arms; says he is unsure how long bombing campaign can continue in Afghanistan without becoming threat to his government; sees intensity of demonstrations against stance waning; photo (M)
news.title: PAKISTANI LEADER SEEKS  'GESTURES' FOR  BACKING  U.S.

news.abstract: Article profiles Gen Abdul Rashid Dostum, described as model of modern Uzbek warlord; his forces were instrumental in taking control of Mazar-i-Sharif, important crossroad in northern Afghanistan; photo (M)
news.title: Rebel With Long Career of Picking Fights (and Sides)

news.abstract: Iranian Pres Mohammad Khatami brands as extremist Osama bin Laden's version of Islam, interview; says it does not represent majority of world's Muslims; scores Sept 11 terrorist attacks in United States; says Iran has not been given proof of bin Laden's role in attacks; denies Iran spurs terrorism; scores Israel but suggests Iran might eventually recognize it; photo (M)
news.title: IRAN CHIEF REJECTS BIN LADEN MESSAGE

news.abstract: In preview of speech to United Nations General Assembly, Pres Bush is critical of countries who express sympathy for Sept 11 attack, but fail to take action on behalf of coalition against terrorism; speaking at White House news conference, Bush does not name names as he calls for action; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Chides Some Members of Coalition for Inaction in War Against Terrorism

news.title: Giovanni Leone, Italy's Ex-President, Dies at 93

news.abstract: China joins World Trade Organization; ceremony in Doha, Qatar, ends 15 years of haggling over whether China's fitful embrace of market economy entitles it to full trading rights of capitalist countries; American and European negotiators in Doha continue to press for trade liberalization while poorer nations demand concessions on trade issues they care about, such as drug patents (M)
news.title: World Trade Organization Admits China, Amid Doubts

news.abstract: US identifies sites in Afghanistan that it suspects were involved in Osama bin Laden's efforts to acquire and produce chemical and biological weapons, but none have been bombed since military campaign began; Al Qaeda is believed to have already produced cyanide gas at site in Derunta; other sites are fertilizer plant in Mazar-i-Sharif and anthrax-vaccine plant in Kabul (M)
news.title: Al Qaeda Sites Point to Tests Of Chemicals

news.abstract: Split appears within political leadership of Northern Alliance that has potential to sap alliance's ability to govern territory it has seized, retard its military operations and delay formation of post-Taliban government; younger, pro-Western, religious moderates are led by foreign minister, Dr Abdullah Abdullah, interior minister, Yunos Qanooni, and Anwari, leader of ethnic Hazara forces; older, religious conservatives, who are more skeptical of West, are led by alliance's president, Burhanuddin Rabbani, and one of its more senior Pashtun leaders, Abdul Rasul Sayyaf; photo (M)
news.title: Rift Grows Among Anti-Taliban Leadership

news.title: Global Warming Impasse Is Broken

news.title: Taliban Begin to Pull Out of Kabul as Rebels Move In

news.abstract: Article discusses new book by Jean-Charles Brisard published in France titled Bin Laden: The Forbidden Truth, which asserts that America was unwilling to confront Saudi Arabia over Osama bin Laden and that oil dictates American foreign policy; photo (M)
news.title: Oil Diplomacy Muddled U.S. Pursuit of bin Laden, New Book Contends

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook column on World Trade Organization summit in Doha, Qatar; says that representatives fear they will deliver shock to world economy unless they agree to liberalize trade, but that only shocking thing may be if manage to agree on anything at all; notes trade organization operates by consensus since voting is forbidden, meaning that smallest holdout can in principle sink weightiest agreement; photo (M)
news.title: Equality at Trade Talks: No Country Gets a Vote

news.abstract: Two Iraqi defectors, veterans of country's intelligence service, say they worked in secret site outside Baghdad where 80 Kuwaitis captured during 1991 war are detained in an underground prison; contradict Iraqi government's longstanding contention that it has not been holding any Kuwaitis; Kuwaiti government has received many reports of people being held, but says they cannot be confirmed (M)
news.title: Iraqi Defectors Tell of Kuwaitis in Secret Jail in Baghdad

news.abstract: Article describes scene near Chagatai in northern Afghanistan, as front line of fighting teeters forward and back and soldiers advance and retreat in kind; photo (M)
news.title: On One Afghan Front Line, the Rebel Tide Surges, Then Flows Back

news.abstract: Lazaro Cardenas, candidate of left-wing Democratic Revolutionary Party, is elected governor of Michoacan state, Mexico, defeating Alfredo Anaya of Institutional Revolutionary Party; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Leftist Wins Race for Governor

news.abstract: The secretary of state said that Turkey, Bangladesh and Indonesia have offered forces for an operation that would prepare the ground for an interim government.
news.title: Powell Says Muslim Nations Should Be Peacekeepers in Kabul

news.abstract: President Bush and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia pledged today to cut their nuclear stockpiles by roughly two-thirds over the next decade.
news.title: Bush and Putin Agree to Reduce Stockpile of Nuclear Warheads

news.abstract: Simon Wiesenthal Center says Germany has stopped paying pensions to 72 World War II veterans who have been accused of or prosecuted for crimes against humanity; additional 11 pensions could be canceled in coming weeks and around 250 other investigations are in progress that could lead to prosecutions for war crimes (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: War Criminals Lose Pensions

news.abstract: Trade ministers attending international summit in Doha, Qatar, all but clinch deal that would give developing countries greater access to cut-price drugs to fight epidemics, defusing most inflammatory dispute between rich and poor nations that had threatened to scuttle talks; breakthrough creates sense of momentum as mediators seek consensus on multiyear agenda for global trade liberalization; negotiators warn substantial differences remain to be settled before talks end on November 15; US help in brokering deal, despite strong opposition from multinational pharmaceutical companies, discussed (M)
news.title: Trade Deal Near for Broad Access to Cut-Rate Drugs

news.abstract: Pres Bush and Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin separately vow deep cuts in their nuclear stockpiles over next decade that would leave each side with fewer than 2,200 warheads; Putin calls for written accord, move Bush wants to avoid, news conference, Washington; two nations still seem far apart on missile defenses, with Putin apparently resisting United States bid for quick accord to ease ABM Treaty, meeting with Bush; Bush and Putin stress emergence of US and Russia as allies, news conference; Bush pledges to speed through Congress bill to take Russia and other former Soviet republics off list of nations subject to economic sanctions; much of their four-hour meeting focuses on Afghanistan; Putin suggests joint consulations and action on terrorism of last two months are model for new military ties with US and NATO; photos (M)
news.title: Bush and Putin Agree to Reduce Stockpile of Nuclear Warheads

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Chechnya Withdrawal Planned, AGain

news.abstract: Thousands of demonstrate, Seoul, demanding South Korea pull out of accord with World Trade Organization under which it will cut subsidies for home-grown rice; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Farmers Stage Protest Over W.T.O. Rice Deal

news.abstract: Argentines are transfixed by bittersweet return of revered soccer great Diego Armando Maradona after two years in Cuba, where he was treated for cocaine abuse; Maradona, 41, overweight and sluggish, plays with national team against international all-stars in exhibition match in his honor; photos (M)
news.title: Buenos Aires Journal; Home From Cuba, Soccer Star Kicks Some Shins

news.abstract: Analysis of war in Afghanistan notes United States military, which created conditions for sudden fall of Kabul to Northern Alliance, has little control over alliance, which moved into city despite its repeated promises to wait; notes other US allies in war against terrorism in Afghanistan are also unpredictable; military success leaves US with no clear answers to questions about Afghanistan's future; alliance is now pledging to keep bulk of its forces outside city; has deployed 3,000 security troops across city to bring order, not occupy it (M)
news.title: A 3rd Front: War's Spoils

news.abstract: Eight Western aid workers, including two Americans, are plucked out of Afghanistan by United States military helicopters and flown to Pakistan; they were arrested and imprisoned by Taliban in Kabul on Aug 5, accused of preaching Christianity; they were put on trial and threatened with death penalty; their trip out of captivity involves International Committee of Red Cross as well as local Pashtun militia leader; details of rescue mission are unclear; spokesman for American Embassy in Islamabad refuses to provide futher details, citing privacy laws; two Americans, Dayna Curry and Heather Mercer, as well as two Australians and four Germans, were working for German-based charity, Shelter Now; Pres Bush hails their safe exit from Afghanistan; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. Flies Aid Workers to Safety in Pakistan

news.abstract: American officials consider new war plan that would shift from bombing to counterguerilla operations; strategy would emphasize gathering intelligence and hunting leaders of Taliban and Al Qaeda and use coalition troops to secure key areas; effect could result in diminishing airstrikes that coincide with beginning of holy month of Ramadan, without official declaration of reduction in air campaign (M)
news.title: Rapid Changes on the Ground Lead the Pentagon to Focus on Counterguerrilla Tactics

news.abstract: Chinese officials in largely Muslim western province of Xinjiang extends country's anticrime crackdown to religious groups that do not have official approval (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Crackdown In Muslim Region

news.abstract: Aid arrives in Afghanistan via route through Uzbekistan, which aid workers say, will allow them to get significant shipments where relief is most needed; photo; map (M)
news.title: Food Shipment May Be Start of Something Big

news.abstract: Unexploded Russian bomb from World War II is unearthed during construction near Reichstag in Berlin, Germany, forcing temporary shutdown of building's observation deck (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Wartime Bomb Near Reichstag

news.abstract: Overview of events in war on terrorism (M)
news.title: A Need for Order, the Smallpox Matter and Oil Prices

news.abstract: Western nations rush to assemble international force to keep order in Afghan areas wrested from Taliban; 160 British marines and American Special Operations troops fly to airfield north of Kabul and begin preparing it for shipments of food; American forces seek to make contact with Northern Alliance officers who forward credible claims of capturing some Taliban commanders and at least one high-ranking Al Qaeda leader; prisoners could provide valuable intelligence about location of Osama bin Laden and Mullah Muhammad Omar, chief of Taliban; country appears deeply fractured, with rival warlords filling power vacuum left by departing Taliban and with Mullah Omar vowing to fight on and 'destroy America'; America's allies signal willingness to fill power vacuum; France, Canada, Turkey and Jordan offer to send troops to maintain security in Afghanistan; Bangladesh and Malaysia said to be preparing to contribute as well; sense of urgency stems from fact that Taliban's resistance in northern Afghanistan has collapsed more quickly than expected, raising fears that unstable situation might interfere with delivery of badly needed aid shipments; photo (L)
news.title: Allies Building Force to Keep Order in a Vacuum

news.abstract: The highest-ranking Chechen guerrilla ever captured by Russian forces went on trial with three other rebels in Dagestan, a southwestern province bordering Chechnya. Salman Raduyev is charged with leading an attack on a Dagestani town in 1996 in which 70 people died and 2,000 were taken hostage. Mr. Raduyev fought mostly in the first Chechen war, in the mid-1990's; he has played little role in the second war, which began in 1999 and continues today.   Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Chechen Rebel Goes On Trial

news.abstract: President Bush and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia ended their three-day summit meeting today with warm jokes and a pledge to bring stability to Afghanistan, but no discernible progress on amending the treaty that constrains Washington's plans to test an antimissile system.    After 24 hours on Mr. Bush's ranch here, punctuated by hours of private discussions and a barbecue dinner on Tuesday night that included lessons in how to dance the Cotton-Eyed Joe, the two presidents emerged this morning to visit the local high school.
news.title: Before and After Bush and Putin's Banter, No Agreement on Missile Defense

news.abstract: Mohammed Atef, the Al Qaeda terror network's military chief and a close confidant of Osama bin Laden, is believed to have been killed in an American airstrike.
news.title: U.S. Says Top Bin Laden Aide Believed Killed in Airstrike

news.abstract: Police in South Africa arrest Shabir Shaik, brother of Defense Dept's chief acquisitions officer, on charges of improperly obtaining classified documents that helped him win lucrative defense contract; acquisitions officer is found to have conflict of interest in matter (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: South Africa: Arrest In Brotherly Deal

news.abstract: Ingrid Betancourt, who has written about her fight against corruption in Colombia, is former congresswoman and senator who won widespread support abroad for denouncing corrupt colleagues and graft-ridden administration of former president, Ernesto Samper; Colombian news media is strangely silent about her new book detailing corruption, and although many Colombians blame institutional corruption for country's unending civil unrest, Betancourt's style of in-your-face accusations does not sit well; nor does her airing of country's dirty launder abroad; her persistence has led to death threats against her and her family; photo (M)
news.title: Bogotá Journal; Corruption's Her Story; Colombia Doesn't Like It

news.abstract: Northern Alliance fighters encircling Kunduz, Afghanistan, pause briefly to celebrate start of Ramadan, but commanders say they will be moving, perhaps within 24 hours, to attack city where they have as many as 20,000 Taliban fighters surrounded; photo (M)
news.title: Rebels Pause for Ramadan, but Vow Swift Attack on Kunduz

news.abstract: Pres Jacques Chirac will make first visit to Algeria by French head of state in 12 years as part of North African tour; Chirac, who faces presidential elections in April, is said to be trying to polish his image as international statesman (M)
news.title: Chirac to Visit Algeria in North Africa Tour

news.abstract: The Taliban leader, Mullah Muhammad Omar, a main target of the American war in Afghanistan, has decided to cede control of his political stronghold in Kandahar to two commanders from the Pashtun ethnic group, the Afghan Islamic Press reported tonight.     The retreat would end the seven-year reign of the extremist Islamic group, which gave safe harbor to Osama bin Laden and Al Qaeda.
news.title: Taliban Leader Said to Be Yielding Grip on Stronghold to 2 Once-Powerful Supporters

news.abstract: Of the 75 to 80 prisoners being held at Arg prison here, 5 are from outside Afghanistan. That makes them ''important prisoners,'' said the prison's commander, Haji-Abdul Kareem Qayabatani, adding that ''they are evidence that other countries were involved'' in supporting the Taliban.     No one knows, however, exactly which countries.
news.title: Alliance Jails Foreign Foes, But Isn't Sure About Origins

news.abstract: Gov. Alfredo Avelín is an eccentric country doctor known for his homespun philosophy, his poetry and a peculiar habit of playfully slapping the faces of visitors to his office.     So perhaps it is not surprising that the other day he broke into a full-throated rendition of the tango classic ''It's a Kid's Dream'' when asked about President Fernando de la Rúa's plans to balance the federal budget to avert a national financial collapse.
news.title: Argentina's Provinces Struggle to Stay Afloat

news.abstract: It could have been a short, sweet story: planes get diverted, local people pitch in to help stranded passengers. Polite thank-you letters and gifts follow.    What happened in Newfoundland in one terrifying week in September was all that. But in the next two months, the story continued to grow. Here and in scattered hamlets for miles around, everyone has a part of it to tell -- how half a dozen or so isolated communities have been embraced by strangers who dropped from the sky and changed their lives.
news.title: Unexpected Guests Warm Hearts in the Frozen North

news.abstract: The Bush administration said today that it would apply intense pressure on the Northern Alliance, newly in control of Kabul and much of Afghanistan, not to create a government on its own but to fulfill its promise to let the United Nations put together a broad coalition to rule the country.    At the same time, after a meeting of the National Security Council conducted from President Bush's ranch here this morning, the administration also vowed to vigorously prosecute the war against remaining Taliban holdouts. It pledged, as well, to refocus its efforts on crushing Al Qaeda, the terrorist network, and its surviving leaders, who apparently include Osama bin Laden.
news.title: U.S. to Press Afghan Rebels Not to Form Government

news.abstract: Shortly after Sept. 11, when the United States sent out urgent inquiries for leads on the suspected hijackers, German officials quickly traced three of the ringleaders to an apartment in this affluent northern port.    It was an important break. But the names and address -- Marienstrasse 54 -- suddenly seemed familiar, German investigators say, and then they realized why: in 1998 and 1999, they had those same men and that same apartment under surveillance because of suspected links to an operative for Osama bin Laden.
news.title: RETRACING A TRAIL TO SEPT. 11 PLOT

news.abstract: Galaxy of corrupt warlords, who tore Afghanistan apart in early 1990's before being vanquished by Taliban, regain control of strategic cities they fled six years ago and are poised to exercise power in ways they always have; rapid return will make forming broad-based Afghan government Bush administration says it wants to help forge much more difficult (M)
news.title: The Corrupt and Brutal Reclaim Afghan Thrones, Evoking Chaos of Somalia

news.abstract: Ibrahim Rugova, whose party easily wins elections in Kosovo and is expected to become its first president, announces that his first priority is to seek independence of province, which is still technically part of Serbia (S)
news.title: Kosovo Winner Wants Independence

news.abstract: Pakistani intelligence officials, addressing subject of mounting concern, estimate 3,000 or more Tailban and Al Qaeda fighters slipped over border into country's tribal areas in week since fall of Kabul and could add to potentially volatile mix in semiautonomous region; fear they could mount antigovernment operations inside Pakistan or cross back into Afghanistan to carry out hit-and-run raids; some tribal leaders remain sympathetic to Taliban and are willing to conceal them out of longstanding loyalties; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistan Fears 3,000 Pro-Taliban Troops Have Slipped In

news.abstract: Northern Alliance commander says at least 300 Taliban soldiers died in fighting when his troops laid siege to Taliban barracks at Mazar-i-Sharif; says most of those housed in barracks were foreign fighters; alliance fought for two weeks to take city, advancing from three directions and using 600 fighters on horseback as well as standard fighting units; United Nations spokeswoman raises fears that captured men were slain; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld calls such reports 'unsubstantiated and sensational' (M)
news.title: A Deadly Siege At Last Won Mazar-i-Sharif

news.abstract: United States will accuse North Korea, Iraq, Iran, Libya and Syria of developing germ weapons in violation of treaty they ratified banning such weapons; Bush administration officials say they suspect additional countries are violating treaty in secret, including some that are friendly with US, but administration is not ready to identify them; accusations will be formally made in Geneva by John R Bolton, under secretary of state, at international conference aimed at strengthening compliance with and enforcement of treaty; public nature of accusations is departure; allegations are not specific, nor is source of any evidence provided; they are intended to deflect criticism of Bush administration from those who say Washington has undermined treaty by rejecting agreement last summer that was meant to strengthen compliance by establishing inspection system (M)
news.title: U.S. Publicly Accusing 5 Countries of Violating Germ-Weapons Treaty

news.abstract: The governing African National Congress hooted with delight when South Africa's leading white party collapsed last month, declaring that the last of its political opponents had been swept away.    But in recent weeks, officials have privately acknowledged that the most serious threat to A.N.C.'s political dominance is alive and growing. The threat comes not from this nation's white minority, but from dissatisfied blacks within the party ranks.
news.title: South Africa Sees Turmoil Dividing Ruling Party

news.abstract: Kosovo's Serbs turned out in much greater numbers than originally thought in elections on Saturday, showing that they see a future despite the Albanian domination of their province and securing a real level of power in a new provincial assembly, Western officials said today.    Most Serbs appear to have voted just before polls closed, and after dark so they would not be seen by community leaders opposed to taking part in the vote for a 120-seat assembly. The elections were devised by the international officials who have ruled Kosovo since the war over it ended in June 1999 and NATO troops arrived here.
news.title: Serb Turnout in Kosovo Vote Seen as an Encouraging Step

news.abstract: Four foreign journalists are reportedly kidnapped and shot dead by armed gunmen on Afghan highway halfway from Jalalabad to Kabul; fifth man, translator, is reported missing; witness says gunmen claimed to be Taliban; journalists' bodies have not been found; they are Maria Grazia Cutuli, reporter for Italian daily Corriere della Sera, Julio Fuentes from El Mundo in Madrid, and Harry Burton, Australian television cameraman, and Aziz Haidari, Afghan-born photogrpher, both working for Reuters; journalists were in second and third cars of eight-car convoy; their cars were stopped at gunpoint by men clad in style favored by Taliban; photos (M)
news.title: 4 Foreign Journalists Are Shot And Possibly Killed in Ambush

news.abstract: Article describe siege of Taliban stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif and its capture by forces of Northern Alliance (M)
news.title: Conflicting Tales Paint Blurry Picture of Siege

news.abstract: The United States is considering closing its original embassy building on Novinsky Boulevard and moving all operations deeper within the embassy's square-block compound because of security concerns, a senior diplomatic official said. Much of the building was vacated after Sept. 11 and many workers moved to a new embassy building, in the center of the compound, which was recently completed after almost 15 years of construction. The new embassy was completely rebuilt after security experts found in the mid-1980's that its framework was riddled with listening devices.   Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Security Fears At U.S. Embassy

news.abstract: Data from probe for 1999 trial in Egypt of Islamic Jihad details scope and ruthlessness of terrorist group, which merged with Al Qaeda in 1998, vastly enhancing Osama's bin Laden's reach and organizational ability; network two groups developed ranges across world, with Egyptians providing tactical support by forging travel documents, transferring money and arranging communications; merger shifted Islamic Jihad's focus from overthrowing Egyptian government to attacking American interests and seems to have increased Egyptians' sense of purpose; Dr Ayman al-Zawahiri, Jihad's leader and bin Laden's second in command, reportedly was with bin Laden in Afghanistan earlier in November; photos (M)
news.title: An Investigation in Egypt Illustrates Al Qaeda's Web

news.abstract: Travelers from Kandahar, Afghanistan, say air of fear and suspense hangs over city as Taliban leader Mullah Muhammad Omar seems to be maneuvering toward his exit; say dwindling number of remaining civilians are rattled by American bombs and by uncertainty over whether Taliban will slip quietly out of city or stay and fight; say intense talks are under way among Taliban hierarchy and between some senior Taliban and opposition commanders (M)
news.title: Fearful City Wonders Whether Taliban Will Leave Quietly or Fight

news.abstract: PARIS—  Gene Fenn, 90, a fashion photographer for Harper's Bazaar and other popular women's magazines, died Nov. 14 in Paris.
news.title: OBITUARY : Gene Fenn, 90, Photographer

news.abstract: The foreign militants who are trapped inside Kunduz have asked to leave Afghanistan through a protected corridor and travel to Pakistan, a senior Northern Alliance official said today.
news.title: Foreign Militants in Kunduz Seek Safe Passage to Pakistan

news.abstract: Ehud Barak, the former Israeli prime minister, told a state inquiry commission today that he was caught by surprise by the wave of violent protests by Israeli Arabs that erupted after the outbreak of the Palestinian uprising last year.    ''I did not expect those type of events'' Mr. Barak, said, referring to the Israeli Arab protests in October 2000 in which 13 people were killed by police gunfire. ''There was no concrete warning of such an eruption from any intelligence agency. The power, scope and intensity of the violence could not have been expected.''
news.title: Barak Testifies on Israeli Arab Violence

news.abstract: Taliban leadership vows not to give up stronghold in southern Afghanistan or spiritual home of Kandahar, ruling out talks with Northern Alliance or other opposition groups on future national government; spokesman, Mullah Omar's private secretary Tayab Agha, warns of return to anarchy and warlordism; photo at news conference (M)
news.title: Taliban Will Rise Again, Aide to Leader Promises

news.abstract: Afghan cooking-oil seller named Hefozullah, arrested in Herat for keeping shop open during Friday prayers, turns out to be last of several thousand tailors, bakers, shoe polishers and confectioners detained by Taliban religious police before they flee city in advance of Northern Alliance; left behind are registers and people who tell of bureaucracy largely indifferent and inept, except in its ruthless enforcement of Mullah Muhammad Omar's harsh Islamic penal code; punishments are spelled out for women who leave home unveiled or alone, for those who fly pigeons or fly kites and for possession of 'unclean things' from pork to photographs to televisions; photos (M)
news.title: No TV, No Chess, No Kites: Taliban's Code, From A to Z

news.abstract: World Briefing
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Dutch Experience cafe in northern English town of Stockport hosts marijuana smoking and could be thin end of wedge in Britain, where government is signaling it may ease laws on use of soft drugs in name of creating workable drug policy; photos; government says police spend inordinate amount of time dealing with minor drug offenses, with 65 percent of 120,000 drug-related arrests last year for marijuana possession; Stockport police raided cafe day it opened in September but did not act again until cafe began attracting publicity (M)
news.title: English Pot Smokers' Pub May Prove a Model

news.abstract: Second case of mad cow disease is confirmed in Japan, on Hokkaido (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: New Mad Cow Case

news.abstract: Five Palestinian boys, cousins ranging in age from 6 to 14, were killed when a powerful explosive detonated beneath them near an Israeli settlement in the Gaza Strip. Palestinians said the boys had been killed by an unexploded tank shell, a remnant of recent fighting, but the Israeli authorities said that a Palestinian explosive might be to blame.    Article, Page A3.
news.title: 5 Palestinian Boys Die in Blast in Gaza

news.abstract: Heavy fighting breaks out between Taliban and Northern Alliance troops along front lines outside Kunduz as senior alliance leader says Taliban officials have agreed to surrender encircled city; thousands of Taliban troops and foreign soldiers are trapped in city; fierce fighting suggests that Taliban leaders who struck surrender deal might not speak for all rank-and-file soldiers, or even for other commanders; as fighting rages, several Taliban soldiers cross front lines and switch sides, lending air of chaos to scene; peace deal supposedly worked out by Gen Abdul Rashid Dostum, longtime Uzbek warlord, seems fraught with questions; photos (M)
news.title: Fierce Fighting Erupts Near Kunduz, Despite Surrender Deal

news.abstract: Jack McConnell, leader of Scottish Labor Party, is elected first minister of Scottish Parliament to replace Henry McLeish, who stepped down in scandal (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Scotland: New Leader For Parliament

news.abstract: Namibia's minister of defense, Erkki Nghimtina, is condemned by National Society of Human Rights for threatening to shoot anyone found to be collaborating with rebels from neighboring Angola (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Namibia: Threat To Shoot Dismays Rights Group

news.abstract: Pres Nursultan Nazarbayev of Kazakhstan dismisses six high government officials who had joined group calling for democratic political reforms; dismissals were demanded by Prime Min Kasymhomart Tokayev, who threatened to resign, saying would-be reformers are seeking to enrich themselves (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Kazakhstan: President Fires Reform Advocates

news.abstract: Overview of day's events in war on terrorism, fighting in Afghanistan and anthrax attacks
news.title: Taliban Holdouts, Europe's Reservations and Anthrax Frustrations

news.abstract: Northern Alliance soldiers in Afghanistan report Pakistani airplanes have again flown into encircled city of Kunduz to evacuate Pakistanis who had been fighting with Taliban; photo; map; sightings are not confirmed and US officials are evasive on subject; US is indebted to Pakistan for helping with war but also wants foreign fighters captured or killed; surrender of Kunduz is yet unclear; Taliban forces regroup elsewhere, forming strong pockets of resistance in east, including Jalalabad vicinity (M)
news.title: PAKISTANIS AGAIN SAID TO EVACUATE ALLIES OF TALIBAN

news.abstract: Photo of balloon vendors riding to market in Kabul, city throwing off Taliban constrictionsó
news.title: In Kabul, Happiness for Sale

news.abstract: UN Committee Against Torture says that while Israel has made some progress in ending practices it says amount to torture, government should install 'effective' complaint and investigation mechanisms; report also cites abuses by Indonesian military and Ukraine's alleged use of torture in jails(M)
news.title: Citing Some Progress, U.N. Panel on Torture Urges Israel to Take More Steps

news.abstract: Carlos Sanchez, aka Juan Valdez, is being retired after thirty years because plummeting coffee prices are forcing Colombian growers' group to cut back on famous ad campaign; map (M)
news.title: Medellín Journal; A Coffee Icon Rides His Mule Off Into the Sunset

news.abstract: Northern Alliance commanders said tonight that their troops had captured Kunduz, overrunning the last Taliban stronghold in northern Afghanistan.
news.title: Taliban Foes Say Kunduz Is Theirs

news.abstract: Sighting of wolf pack in nature preserve along Germany's border with Poland gives new impetus to effort of Society for the Protection of Wolves, founded in Germany in 1991 partly to create conditions to resettle animals, which were eradicated from German soil 140 years earlier; pack may have migrated from northwestern Poland or Carpathian Mountains; society's president Peter Blanche comments (M)
news.title: Wolves Wander Into Germany, Aiding a Resettlement Effort

news.abstract: Ghullan Muhammad, warlord of collection of villages in Maidan Shahr, Afghanistan, surrenders to, joins or makes deal with North Alliance; just which it is still is not clear after one day of frantic negotiations and marshaling of forces; hard-core Taliban fighters and unknown number of Islamic zealots slip away during negotiations; they could be headed for Taliban stronghold of Kandahar, or they could be disappearing into mountains, perhaps to fight another day as guerrillas; possibility that Taliban fighters will be allowed to fade into hills, with potential to re-emerge and destabilize Afghanistan, is worrying to Western diplomats trying to reconstruct country; photo (M)
news.title: As Alliance Deals With a Warlord, Taliban Fighters Slip Away

news.abstract: Afghanistan's new rulers lament loss of Northern Alliance's legendary guerrilla commander Ahmed Shah Massoud, who was assassinated on Sept 9; Dr Abdullah Abdullah, Northern Alliance foreign minister and one of best friends of Massoud, says Massoud might have saved nation from its tumult; photos (M)
news.title: Kabul's New Rulers Lament a Leader Who Died Too Soon

news.abstract: Australia, which is as large as US minus Alaska, but which has only 19.3 million people compared with more than 280 million in United States, wants more inviting policies and programs for both migration and parenthood to counter long decline in national birthrate, and to avoid demographic black hole of zero population growth; birth rate of 1.7 births per woman is well below 2.1 'replacement rate' last reached in 1975; similar problem is emerging in political and economic agendas of developed nations elsewhere, particularly in Western Europe and Japan; UN Population Fund report forecasts if currrent trends continue, population of Europe will fall from current 723.6 million to 603.3 million by 2050, and Japan's population of 127.3 million will fall to 109.2 million (M)
news.title: Australia Wants More People, but Without More Immigration

news.abstract: Northern Alliance commanders report capture of city of Kunduz, last Taliban stronghold in northern Afghanistan: deputy defense minister, Atiqullah Baryalai, says Taliban troops have fled west to uncertain fate toward army of another alliance general, Abdul Rashid Dostum; photo (M)
news.title: TALIBAN FOES SAY KUNDUZ IS THEIRS

news.abstract: At least 150,000 Afghans live in refugee camp in Maslakh that has population of major city but none of its services; inhabitants were pushed from their homes, not by war but by drought heading into its fourth year in three provinces in northwestern part of country; people in Maslakh wait for food, for bricks to build homes, and for sick children to die; graveyards are growing every day, result of illness, hunger and cold; photos (M)
news.title: Where Thousands Of Drought Refugees Wait for Food or Death

news.abstract: Czech Republic Communist Party complaint against Rev Vojtech Vlastimil Protivinsky, who urged parishioners to vote against local Communist candidates, has reawakened bitterness of many persecuted under past Communist rule; Pres Vaclav Havel has blocked prosecution and local prosecutor who began proceedings has resigned; Protivinsky cites need to oppose ideas that are assault on basic human rights; analysts score Communists for using instruments of democracy against priest who disagrees with them (M)
news.title: Communist Effort to Prosecute Czech Priest Raises Ghosts of Past

news.abstract: Afghanistan's varied landscape and geology make it ideal for caves, which are used as hideouts by Taliban and Al Qaeda terrorist network (S)
news.title: Nature Made The Perfect Hiding Place

news.abstract: Hundreds of Afghan teenage boys go to movies in Kabul, something they could not do for past six years under Taliban rule; owner of cinema, who was once jailed by Taliban for three weeks, says he hid films in his home for last six years, as did several other theater owners he knows; photo (M)
news.title: Film Critics With a Keen Eye for Violence

news.abstract: Liberation of Kunduz, last big garrison of Taliban soldiers in northern Afghanistan by forces of Northern Alliance, described; fate of many foreign Taliban fighters remains unclear; many surrendered, but others vanished and may have left aboard flights villagers saw operating from local airport two weeks before city fell; photos (M)
news.title: A Deathly Peace Settles on Kunduz's Streets

news.abstract: Catholic children walk to North Belfast school peaceably for first time in three months after Protestants end protests that forced them to seek protection of riot squad police officers and British troops; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Northern Ireland: A Peaceful Walk To School

news.abstract: Britain's Defense Sec Geoff Hoon says most of 6,400 British troops, placed on 48-hour alert for action in Afghanistan, will have readiness downgraded to week; says 400 troops from parachute regiment and air assault brigade will remain on two-day standby; reports four soldiers were wounded in fighting in Afghanistan; photo (M)
news.title: British Defense Secretary Says Troops for Afghanistan Are Being Taken Off High Alert

news.abstract: Article in series about HIV epidemic in South Africa describes crucial role of sangomas, or traditional healers, in health care; polls say 60 percent of all South Africans consult sangomas; traditional doctors know their patients come to them only after seeing sangoma; Martha Shokwakhe Mtshali, pre-eminent sangoma, admits that one illness that stumps her is AIDS; says if she knew what was in Western AIDS drugs, she might be able to find herbal equivalent; she and her colleagues say they are not hostile to Western medicine; Mtshali seeks working partnership with doctors; because South Africans place so much trust in sangomas, hospitals sometimes 'deputize' them for tasks like monitoring patients who need to take daily drugs; photo; map (M)
news.title: AIDS Crisis Leaves Africa's Oldest Ways at a Loss

news.abstract: Human rights advocates in Egypt express concern that police are monitoring Web sites; cite arrest of Shohdy Naguib after he posted poem condemning Egyptian leaders (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: Concern Over Monitored Web Sites

news.abstract: North Korean soldier fires few bullets at South Korean outpost in demilitarized zone; South Korean forces return fire; incident is first of its kind in over three years in zone; map (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Shots Exchanged In DMZ

news.abstract: Career sketch of retired Gen Antÿ
news.title: Envoy Forges Bonds and Reaps Benefits

news.abstract: Bush administration official says United States seeks to avoid future military obligations in Afghanstan once mission to defeat Taliban and destroy Al Qaeda terrorist network is over; says US expects to be 'partner' in shaping nation's political and economic future, but will not take part in international security force charged with bringing stability to nation (M)
news.title: U.S. Sees Limited Mission In Postwar Afghanistan

news.abstract: Interview with Mullah Amirjan Selabe, who commanded 30 Taliban soldiers in Kabul before fleeing to Pakistan month ago; he cites effort to change his way of life; is one of countless Taliban soldiers or commanders who have disappeared by melding selves into Pakistan's Afghan communities; many are transforming their appearance to survive, but not necessarily renouncing their beliefs (M)
news.title: From Jihad To Thoughts Of Studying Computers

news.abstract: United Nations calls for increased aid to Somalia (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Somalia: The 'Forgotten Emergency'

news.abstract: Truckers from all over southern Africa have sex with prostitutes in Ladysmith, in rural KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa; it is assumed that is one reason HIV spread so rapidly in province; prostitutes working truck-stops make clear how hard it would have been to stem spread, even if government made concerted effort, which it has not; photo; map (M)
news.title: Rare Condoms, Deadly Odds For Truck-Stop Prostitutes

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  After years of seeming indifference, the United States is again courting Southeast Asian countries — this time in its search for allies in the global war against terrorism.
news.title: America's War on Terror Ends Years of Indifference to Region : U.S. Woos Southeast Asian Allies

news.abstract: Vietnam joins United States in approving far-reaching trade agreement that throws open its economy and brings end to final chapter of war; Vu Khoan, Vietnam's minister of trade, says with trade accord, process of normalizing relations between Vietnam and US is fully realized; new agreement is expected to take effect at start of new year; agreement commits Vietnam to series of far-reaching reforms over next several years, setting stage for development of fully free market in Vietnam; American tariffs on Vietnamese goods will be cut to 4 percent from as high as 40 percent, removing Vietnam from company of small number of unfavored states; World Bank estimates that lower tariffs could eventually double amount of Vietnam's exports to US, which currently is $800 million a year; photo (M)
news.title: Relations at Last Normal, Vietnam Signs U.S. Trade Pact

news.abstract: Gen Anthony C Zinni, Bush administration's new envoy, begins complex task of trying to broker new cease-fire between Israel and Palestinians; scope of his mission and of his authority remain unclear to Israelis and Palestinians, who have expressed doubts about possibility of durable truce after 14 months of bitter conflict; Zinni meets in Ramallah with Yasir Arafat, who says peace is his 'strategic choice'; shortly later, Palestinian gunmen again open fire from town of Beit Jala on Jewish area of Jerusalem, Gilo, that they regard as illegal settlement; Israeli forces return fire; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Envoy Meets Arafat and Asks for End to Violence

news.abstract: Schools and businesses close in Srinagar, summer capital of Kashmir, to protest new Indian antiterror measure that was invoked for first time to seal house in Srinagar where suspected Islamic militants are hiding (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Protest Against New Terror Law

news.abstract: Anthropologist Thor Heyerdahl says his excavations i
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Norway: New Theory On Norse God

news.abstract: Negotiations on a future government for Afghanistan stalled badly today, after the leader of the Northern Alliance refused to authorize his delegation to submit a list of proposed candidates.
news.title: Northern Alliance Refuses to Submit Candidates for Interim Government

news.abstract: North Korea threatens 'countermeasures' against US because Bush administration insists on raising questions about its human rights record and religion, and demanding inspection of weapons of mass destruction; threat increases fears of complete breakdown of peace talks engineered by Pres Kim Dae Jung over last year and half (M)
news.title: North Korea Threatens U.S. Over Demand for Arms Inspections

news.abstract: Article in series, Death and Denial, exploring aspects of HIV epidemic in South Africa, describes plight of rape victims; country has one of world's highest rape rates; in rural KwaZulu/Natal province, there is 40 percent chance that young male rapist is HIV positive; public health system does not provide antiretroviral drug therapy for people with HIV, so infection means virtual certainty of death for many rape victims; by law, accused rapist could refuse blood test; this means that even if drugs were available, young women often would not get them in time; photos; map (L)
news.title: South African Victims Face Rapists and H.I.V.

news.abstract: America's military allies in war on terror are encamped at MacDill Air Force Base in Florida, in so-called Coalition Village; they are outsiders in what some diplomats and military officials say remains essentially all-American fight in Afghanistan; about 35 countries have offered to send aircraft, ships or solders to help hunt down Taliban and Al Qaeda leaders; as more than 1,000 American marines pour into base near Kandahar, some coalition partners wonder whether US really wants their offerings of help afte all; Gen Tommy R Franks, head of military operation, says their help will be used when time is right; photo (M)
news.title: Many Eager to Help, but Few Are Chosen

news.abstract: Japan's foreign ministry will punish 328 employees for embezzlement after six-month investigation into misuse of nearly $2 million in official funds over last 5 years (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: Embezzlement At Foreign Ministry

news.abstract: Northern Alliance discovers small compound in Kunduz used as headquarters by Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, Central Asia's largest terrorist group, and its leader Juma Namangani, who is thought to have been killed nearby; Namangani's home within compound served as academy for preparing soldiers and terrorists to export international Islamic jihad and emphasized incursions into Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan; academy was abandoned as Northern Alliance forces swept through Kunduz but documents and other materials salvaged confirm Namangani's ambition of fomenting religious war; photo of document showing how to make suitcase bomb (M)
news.title: Alliance Says It Found School Run By a Titan of Terrorism

news.abstract: India's Supreme Court orders all states to provide cooked lunches in all government schools by January 2002 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Ruling On School Lunches

news.abstract: Bush administration says it is too soon to send international peacekeepers to Afghanistan, calling conditions too uncertain and dangerous; several American allies, including Britain, France, Canada and Turkey, are prepared to send troops for keeping peace and to ensure safety of food convoys; map (M)
news.title: Bush Administration Says It's Too Early to Deploy International Peacekeepers

news.abstract: Daniel Arap Moi, Yoweri K Museveni and Benjamin W Mkapa, presidents of Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania, re-establish East African Community, nearly quarter-century after economic and political union was disbanded because of regional strife; inaugurate joint legislative assembly to handle regional policy matters and court to settle cross-border disputes; initially intend to reduce trade barriers and slash bureaucracies currently interfering with regional growth (M)
news.title: East Africans Rekindle Regional Grouping

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of students are joined by university staff and faculty members in demonstration to protest plan to overhaul Spain's universities; Education Min Pilar del Castillo says aim is to improve quality of teaching by instituting new selection procedures for tenured professors and creating national evaluation agency that will rank colleges and improve administration of universities; critis contend overhaul is start of subtle process of privatization, that it handicap public institutions and favors private colleges, which will lead to two-tier system; most of all, they say plan is flawed because government has not proposed any new resources to put new system in place; photo (M)
news.title: In Spain, Thousands Protest New Plans for Universities

news.abstract: Immigration detention center in Woomera, Australia, holds more than 1,000 people, many of them women and children and many of whom have been in detention for years; 20-acre complex is biggest and most troubled of six centers in Australia that together house more than 2,500 illegal immigrants; detentions have not caused widespread alarm in Australia, but lawyers acting on behalf of detainees are beginning to complain more loudly about their treatment; advocates for immigrants also criticize what they say is increasing evidence of detriorating conditions at Woomera; although Woomera has gloomiest record, assaults by guards and suicide attempts are evident at all centers; drawing by child detainee (M)
news.title: Australia Migrants, Many Children, Land at Troubled Camp

news.abstract: Anger Erupts At Mosque, Site of Raid And Arrests**Members of Islamic Cultural Center and mosque in Milan, Italy, protest raid and arrests at center, saying investigations there are trumped up and racist; since Sept 11, officials in Italy and US have been describing place as Europe's logistical center for Al Qaeda terrorist network; center has played recurring role in various terrorist investigations; police say they obtained wiretap evidence of contacts between leader in Milan and adviser to those responsible for 1993 bombing of World Trade Center; key witness in trial of four Al Qaeda members in 1998 bombings of American embassies in Kenya and Tanzania testified that he had visited center, too; terrorist suspect who worked at center was arrested two weeks ago at Milan train station; investigators raided center on Nov 29, taking second man employed there into custody; police say both of arrested men are Al Qaeda recruiters (M)
news.title: Anger Erupts At Mosque, Site of Raid And Arrests

news.abstract: Fate is uncertain for hundreds of foreign soldiers who fought with Taliban and who are now imprisoned by Northern Alliance; they are foreign soldiers in civil war; their rights are uncertain, and no one--neither Northern Alliance, which took them, nor foreign countries, which spawned them--seems to want them anymore; many of men say they heeded call of aged mullahs who told them to wage holy war, and men set off with little sense of where they were going or what their war was about; many say they tried to leave very day they landed; some prisoners of Northern Alliance in Mazar-i-Sharif, including Fahad Nasir, Saudi Taliban fighter, Pakistani Taliban members Muhammed Jamalhuddin and Amzah Zia Shah, and Abdul Satar Nafisi, Pakistani who says he was journalist captured along with Pakistani soldiers, comment; photos (M)
news.title: Taliban Arab, Like Many, Longs for Home but Faces a Doubtful Fate

news.abstract: Afghanistani women return to Kabul University for first time since October 1996 when Taliban took control and barred them from classes; Farida Afzali comments; photo (M)
news.title: After Years Away From Campus, a Joyful Return

news.title: Swiss Voters Reject Effort to Abolish Their Army

news.abstract: Israeli missiles landed near the headquarters of the Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat in Gaza today in an apparent response to three suicide bombings in Israel last weekend.
news.title: Arafat Not Present at Gaza Headquarters

news.title: Argentina Limits Withdrawals as Banks Near Collapse

news.abstract: ISLAMABAD, Pakistan, Dec. 3 - George J. Tenet, the director of central intelligence, urged the president of Pakistan in a weekend meeting to go further in cracking down on militant clerics and other extremists, government officials said today.
news.title: C.I.A. Chief Urges Pakistani to Crack Down on Militants

news.abstract: Delegates from four Afghan factions are in Bonn, Germany, to negotiate over draft of agreement for post-Taliban government drawn up by United Nations; it calls for 28-member executive administration, international security force for capital, and symbolic role for former king, Mohammad Zahir Shah; delegates and diplomats say that if parties agree on draft, four factions will propose 15 names each, complete with biographies and suggested portfolios, to UN special envoy for Afghanistan, Lakhdar Brahimi, who is chairing conference (M)
news.title: Afghan Factions Work On a Draft Agreement

news.abstract: Many Muslims in Spain, where immigrant Arab population has swelled to estimated 500,000, are feeling burned in aftermath of September 11 terrorist attacks against US by dawning realization that their community has become busy logistical rear guard, apparently humming with Islamic terrorists; while overwhelming majority of newly arrived immigrants are law-abiding North African laborers, terrorist fringe appears to pose threat that some authorities acknowledge was underestimated before attacks; Mohamed Atta, suspected coordinator of suicide hijackers, visited Spain twice in month before September 11; police have since carried out three roundups of men accused of belonging to Al Qaeda, terrorist network of Osama bin Laden, and are monitoring about 200 Arab immigrants suspected of working with 20 Islamic terrorist cells; mistaken arrest of Ahmad Mardini, Madrid shopkeeper, in antiterrorist dragnet discused; photos (M)
news.title: Spain Pursues Terrorists Among Its Muslim Immigrants

news.abstract: Eight former organizers and guides of Swiss adventure company, Adventure World; go on trial on charges connected with deaths of 21 young people who drowned during Alpine canyoning expedition two years ago; guides had decided to continue trip even as thunderstorm was breaking over Saxet Valley near resort town of Interlaken, where trial is being held; young tourists, most of them from Australia, were swept to their deaths when mountain stream they were navigating turned into raging torrent; case reviewed (M)
news.title: Trial Begins In Death of 21 During Trip In Switzerland

news.abstract: Pentagon reports several pockets of Taliban resistance in northern Afghanistan as Americans marshal forces in south; cites enclave near Mazar-i-Sharif, where up to 2,500 hard-core Taliban and foreign fighters refuse to surrender; approximately 1,200 marines with attack helicopters and armored vehicles are poised to strike from base southwest of Kandahar as opposition Northern Alliance forces close in on last major Taliban stronghold in fierce fighting; Pentagon more than doubles number of Army troops securing Bagram air base outside capital of Kabul to as many as 250; American warplanes continue bombardment of cave-riddled mountain complexes near Jalalabad, where Taliban and Al Qaeda fighters are believed hiding; Pentagon confirms American Special Operations forces are working with opposition groups in Jalalabad area, conducting reconnaissance and calling in air strikes; says they will not go into caves and tunnels to root out Taliban or Al Qaeda forces; map (M)
news.title: Taliban Resists In Some Pockets North of Kabul

news.abstract: US marines transform desolate airstrip in southern Afghanistan, seized eight days ago, into heavily-fortified, highly technological base of operations to support final assault on Taliban's last stronghold in Kandahar; photo (M)
news.title: Growing Marine Force Turns Desolate Airstrip Into a High-Tech Base

news.abstract: Officer testifying in military trial of 94 suspected Muslim militants in Egypt say they planned to assassinate number of Egyptians and Americans, including Pres Hosni Mubarak; human rights orgns criticize trial because there is no appeal and because charges of violent activity were added after Sept 11, giving appearance that government is using climate against terrorism to settle old scores (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: Militants Said To Plot Killings

news.abstract: ASIA JAPAN: AN EQUAL-OPPORTUNITY THRONE The governing Liberal Democratic Party began deliberations on whether the law governing imperial succession should be changed to allow women to ascend the throne. The deliberations began three days after the birth of a baby princess, the first child of Crown Prince Naruhito and Princess Masako, with public support growing to change a 1948 law that allows only male succession. There have been no male births in the imperial family since 1965. Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi has said he will support a change in the law but has urged careful consultations beforehand.    Howard W. French (NYT).
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Bush administration is questioning whether Yasir Arafat can lead Palestinians; drops its public calls for Israeli restraint in wake of deadly suicide bombings and shootings by Palestinians; it is unclear whether policy shift is tactical move to pressure Arafat to dismantle terror groups or strategic change; administration denies United States has given Prime Min Ariel Sharon approval to eliminate Arafat as Palestinian leader; denies Israeli airstrikes on Palestinian Authority offices were aimed at Arafat; State Sec Colin L Powell holds terrorist attacks were also assault on Arafat's authority; calls Israeli reprisals justified (M)
news.title: U.S. Questions if Arafat Can Lead the Palestinians

news.abstract: Terrorists believed to belong to Maoist Shining Path bomb electricity tower east of Lima, Peru (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Peru: Maoist Group Suspected In Bombing

news.abstract: Afghan delegates meeting in Bonn, Germany, reach agreement on new post-Taliban government for Afghanistan that will assume power in Kabul on December 22; interim administration will be led by Hamid Karzai, Pashtun leader currently fighting Taliban in home territory of Kandahar; one of five vice chairmen will be Dr Sima Samar, who will also be in charge of women's affairs; Dr Suhaila Seddiqi will be in charge of public health; other appointees not identified; new administration will be made up of chairman, five deputies and 23 other ministers; will take over country's seat at UN; current administration in Kabul, led by former president Burhanuddin Rabbani, will be supplanted; photos (M)
news.title: Talks in Bonn End With Deal On Leadership For Afghans

news.abstract: Article describes former Al Qaeda terrorist camp in Rishkhor, Afghanistan, that was destroyed by American warplanes; photo (M)
news.title: Arms, Books And Noose Were Fixtures At Terror Lair

news.abstract: Hamid Karzai, man appointed to lead Afghanistan's new interim government, says he has begun talks with senior Taliban officials over surrender of Kandahar, last major stronghold of Taliban and Arab fighters loyal to Osama bin Laden; declines to identify Taliban officials or describe nature of attacks; Afghan and Pakistani officials do not believe Karzai is negotiating directly with Mullah Muhammad Omar, Taliban's paramount leader, but through emissary who is member of Karzai's Populzai clan; Karzai's appointment could quicken pace of talks with Taliban holdouts, who are mostly Pashtuns and are cornered in Kandahar, where Karzai's well-respected family lives (M)
news.title: New Leader Urges Foes To Surrender

news.abstract: About 300 supporters of Holy Land Foundation for Relief and Development gather in Richardson, Texas, for religious vigil; local imam, Dr Nabil Al-Sadoon, leads them in series of noisy chants and protests; protesters had gathered to express their anger at raids conducted earlier this week by federal authorities on four of foundation's offices around country, including its headquarters in Richardson; Pres Bush has said that assets of orgn are being seized because foundation, which collected estimated $13 million last year, is providing money to militant Palestinian group Hamas (M)
news.title: In Texas, Donors to Muslim Charity Seethe at Raids by Government

news.title: Clan Leader Turned Statesman: Hamid Karzai

news.abstract: Berlin Social Democrats begin talks to form coalition with former Communist Party of Democratic Socialism, after negotiations with Greens and Free Democrats fail (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Social Democrats Seek Coalition

news.abstract: The Taliban agreed on Thursday to surrender the city of Kandahar, but negotiators had yet to resolve the fate of Mullah Muhammad Omar, the Taliban leader.
news.title: Surrender Deal May Hinge on Amnesty for Mullah Omar

news.abstract: Sir Peter Blake, famous New Zealand yachtsman, is shot and killed by masked robbers on his boat anchored in harbor near mouth of Amazon River in Macapa, Brazil; photos; map; police say he resisted holdup by gang known as Water Rats; two crew members are injured; Blake, 53, led New Zealand crew that won America's Cup in 1995 and 2000; vessel Seamaster was on research expedition (M)
news.title: Renowned New Zealand Yachtsman Killed in Amazon

news.abstract: Afghan Taliban forces surrounded in Kandahar agree to surrender their last stronghold, but negotiators have yet to resolve crucial issues of fate of leader Muhammad Omar and thousands of Arab fighters loyal to Osama bin Laden; yet uncaptured is bin Laden, who Gen Muhammad Fahim says has retreated to caves of Tora Bora region close to Pakistan frontier; surrender terms call for Omar to cede power to local tribal leader and have soldiers lay down weapons; new Afghan leader Hamid Karzai says Omar and top aides must face trial for crimes, noting that Omar has not even made statement of regret; former Taliban envoy Abdul Salam Zaeef comments in Islamabad; photo; map; intense negotiations and role of various factions detailed (M)
news.title: OFFER IS MADE TO SURRENDER TALIBAN'S LAST STRONGHOLD; DEAL MAY HINGE ON AMNESTY

news.abstract: One day after plans for interim Afghan government are announced, Gen Abdul Rashid Dostum, whose forces dominate much of northern Afghanistan, vows to boycott new administration and says he will not go to Kabul until 'proper government' is in place; his representatives to negotiations in Germany came away with ministries of agriculture, mining and industry in interim government, but he had hoped for foreign ministry as reward for role his forces played in toppling Taliban (M)
news.title: Boycott Threat Is Early Test for Afghan Leadership Pact
